title: New insights into tumor size in colorectal cancer: smaller size, higher risk?
authors: Ding R, Li T, Li C, Song W, Gao X, Xu M, et al.
abstract: In colorectal cancer, the AJCC T category is defined by the depth of bowel wall invasion rather than by the absolute size of the primary tumor. The clinical value of tumor size in assessing tumor aggressiveness, metastatic risk, and prognosis remains insufficiently investigated. To evaluate the clinical value of tumor size in assessing potential metastatic risk and prognostic stratification in colorectal cancer. We retrospectively included 10,513 patients with colorectal cancer who underwent surgical treatment at FUSCC between 2008 and 2020. We integrated tumor size with clinicopathological characteristics to assess metastatic risk using machine-learning models and SHAP-based interpretation. By modeling tumor size as both a categorical and continuous variable, we further investigated its prognostic relevance using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression incorporating restricted cubic splines. Additionally, an independent cohort of 6,739 patients from Changhai Hospital was used for external validation. Machine-learning identified lymph node metastasis as the primary predictive endpoint, with the CatBoost model achieving the highest AUROC of 0.800. SHAP analysis showed that smaller tumor diameter contributed positively to predicted metastatic risk. Multivariable restricted cubic spline analysis further demonstrated a significant nonlinear association between tumor diameter and OS, with mortality risk increasing as tumor diameter decreased within the approximately 0-3 cm range. Among younger male patients with locally advanced disease, tumors ≤3 cm were associated with significantly worse OS and DFS than tumors >5 cm (both Smaller tumor size may paradoxically indicate higher lymph node metastatic risk and poorer prognosis in a subset of patients with colorectal cancer, particularly younger male patients with locally advanced disease. Tumor size may therefore serve as a complementary factor for postoperative risk stratification beyond conventional TNM staging.
cn_title: 结直肠癌肿瘤大小新见解：尺寸越小，风险越高？
insight: 大样本回顾性研究揭示结直肠癌肿瘤直径与淋巴结转移风险及预后呈非线性负相关，小肿瘤（≤3cm）在特定亚组中反而预后更差，提示肿瘤大小可作为TNM分期外的补充风险分层指标。
grade_rationale: 基于单中心大样本回顾性队列（n=10513）并外部验证（n=6739），采用机器学习与限制性立方样条分析，但回顾性设计及亚组分析局限性使其暂不足以改变临床实践。

title: Global research landscape of ferroptosis in colorectal cancer: a multi-database bibliometric analysis (2017-2025).
authors: You F, Tan R, Long F, Yang B, Tang D
abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, has attracted increasing attention in recent years because of its critical roles in tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune regulation. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and imposes a substantial mortality burden. This study aimed to systematically analyze the global research landscape, hotspots, and developmental trends of ferroptosis in CRC research from 2017 to 2025. English-language publications related to ferroptosis and CRC published between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus databases. A total of 1, 354 original articles and reviews were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix package in R were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses to evaluate annual publication trends, country/region and institutional collaboration networks, author contributions, journal distribution, co-cited references, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. The number of publications in this field increased rapidly after 2020 and peaked in 2025. China ranked first in both publication output and total citations, followed by the United States, and China-United States collaboration constituted the core of the international collaboration network. Central South University was the most productive institution, while journals such as Frontiers in Oncology and Frontiers in Immunology served as major publication platforms. Research hotspots were mainly concentrated on chemotherapy resistance, the tumor immune microenvironment, PANoptosis, prognostic models, non-coding RNAs, gut microbiota, and the regulation of ferroptosis by traditional Chinese medicine and natural products. Ferroptosis has become a rapidly evolving frontier in CRC research. The research focus is gradually shifting from fundamental molecular mechanisms toward translational medical directions, including chemosensitization, combination immunotherapy, reversal of drug resistance, and precise prognostic evaluation. This study provides a systematic reference for understanding the global knowledge structure and future research directions in the field of ferroptosis and CRC.
cn_title: 铁死亡在结直肠癌中的全球研究格局：多数据库文献计量分析（2017-2025）
insight: 该文献计量分析系统描绘了铁死亡在结直肠癌中的研究热点与趋势，提示化疗耐药、免疫微环境及预后模型是未来转化方向，为肝转移相关铁死亡研究提供选题参考。
grade_rationale: 文献计量分析属描述性研究方法，无临床干预或验证，但样本量大、覆盖多数据库，对领域趋势有参考价值但不改变实践。

title: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 as a cancer predisposition syndrome: A case report of quadruple primary malignancies with review of the literature.
authors: Fujiyama K, Nakahara M, Ito Y, Yamada H, Aoki M, Takahashi M, et al.
abstract: Myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) is the most common adult-onset muscular dystrophy and is increasingly recognized as a cancer predisposition syndrome, with 2- to 8.5-fold elevated risks of endometrial, ovarian, thyroid, and colorectal cancers. Evidence on the oncological management of DM1 patients-including perioperative care, chemotherapy tolerability, and cancer surveillance-remains scarce. A 56-year-old woman with DM1 developed four primary malignancies over 16 years: papillary thyroid carcinoma at age 40, breast carcinoma at age 49, and synchronous endometrial carcinoma and low-grade serous ovarian carcinoma at age 56. Progressive respiratory muscle weakness necessitated tracheostomy and nocturnal ventilation from age 49, and DM1 was diagnosed at age 50. Three general anesthesia surgeries were completed without complications under multidisciplinary DM1-tailored perioperative protocols. For FIGO stage IIIB ovarian carcinoma, four cycles of paclitaxel-carboplatin chemotherapy were administered without dose reduction. First-degree atrioventricular block and left ventricular function remained stable, and treatment was discontinued for Grade 2 nausea rather than a DM1-specific toxicity. Standard-intensity multimodal cancer treatment was feasible in this DM1 patient with appropriate perioperative and cardiac monitoring. DM1 should be recognized as a cancer predisposition syndrome, and individualized surveillance strategies analogous to those used in hereditary cancer syndromes warrant further investigation.

title: Clinical utility and reproducibility of intravoxel incoherent motion MRI in rectal cancer: a structured narrative review.
authors: Alyami AS, Elbashir M, Ali S, Refaee T, Ageeli W, Alwadani B, et al.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a crucial imaging modality for the management of rectal cancer. Conventional MRI provides detailed anatomical information but has a limited capacity to evaluate tumor biology. Intravoxel Incoherent Motion (IVIM) is an advanced functional MRI technique that simultaneously measures tissue cellularity and microvascular perfusion without contrast agents, providing deeper insights into the tumor microenvironment. This narrative review critically examines the current evidence on the clinical usefulness of IVIM MRI in rectal cancer, focusing on three key areas: tumor characterization and staging, prediction and monitoring of treatment response, and the reproducibility and limitations of IVIM parameters. A literature search was conducted in vid MEDLINE, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Google Scholar from 2015 to October 2025. The search included keywords such as "intravoxel incoherent motion OR IVIM" and "rectal cancer OR colorectal cancer." Original studies with at least 10 patients were included; reviews, case reports, and animal studies were excluded. The true diffusion coefficient D appears to be the most biologically interpretable and reproducible IVIM-derived parameter, with several studies linking lower D values to greater cellularity or more aggressive tumor features; however, findings are not uniform across all cohorts. While the perfusion fraction (f) has shown associations with markers of aggressiveness in some studies, its clinical utility is limited by poor reproducibility. For nodal staging, primary-tumor IVIM histogram models have shown promising diagnostic performance, although most evidence remains from single centers and is insufficiently validated. When assessing the response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT), a post-treatment increase in D appears to be the most consistent IVIM-derived marker of treatment response. However, its clinical use still requires standardized acquisition and external validation while perfusion parameters (f and D*) exhibit poor test-retest reproducibility. Combining IVIM with complementary techniques, such as diffusion kurtosis imaging or radiomics, may improve predictive performance compared with individual parameters. IVIM-DWI provides non-contrast quantitative information on diffusion and perfusion in rectal cancer. Current evidence suggests that D is the most reproducible and biologically interpretable IVIM parameter, whereas f and D* remain limited by poor repeatability and protocol dependence. IVIM may add value for tumor characterization, nodal risk assessment, and treatment-response evaluation, particularly when combined with histogram analysis, DKI, or radiomics; however, standardized acquisition protocols and external validation are required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, pneumoperitoneum, and SCE after colonic ESD: a case report.
authors: Zhang J, Huang H, Jiang W, Huang X, Fan C, Wu Y
abstract: Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has become a widely accepted technique for en bloc resection of colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs). Although the procedure is generally considered safe, complications including bleeding and perforation may occur. The simultaneous development of pneumothorax, pneumomediastinum, pneumoperitoneum, and extensive subcutaneous emphysema following colorectal ESD represents an exceptionally rare but potentially serious adverse event. A 56-year-old female patient underwent ESD for a granular-type LST measuring 8 mm × 20 mm located in the ascending colon. The procedure was performed under general anesthesia with tracheal intubation and carbon dioxide insufflation. Complete en bloc resection was achieved, and the post-ESD mucosal defect was closed with 16 titanium clips. Approximately 3 h after the procedure, the patient developed progressive neck swelling without respiratory distress or chest pain. Computed tomography (CT) revealed a small amount of pneumothorax on the right side and fluid pneumothorax on the left side (lung compression <10%), extensive subcutaneous emphysema involving the neck, chest wall, and right proximal thigh, pneumomediastinum, and pneumoperitoneum. The patient was managed conservatively with high-flow nasal cannula oxygen, bowel rest, intravenous antibiotics, and proton pump inhibitor therapy. Serial imaging demonstrated gradual resolution of the ectopic gas collections. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day 7. This case demonstrates that extensive gas extravasation involving multiple body compartments can occur as a rare complication of colorectal ESD, particularly when procedures are performed in the retroperitoneal portion of the colon under general anesthesia with positive pressure ventilation. Prompt recognition, timely CT evaluation, and conservative management in hemodynamically stable patients can lead to favorable outcomes without the need for surgical intervention.

title: Prevalence of colorectal adenocarcinoma among Iraqi patients: a pathological analysis.
authors: Raji A
abstract: Colorectal adenocarcinoma is a significant health concern in Iraq, with variations in demographic and histopathological characteristics compared to global trends. This study retrospectively analysed 120 colorectal carcinoma cases from multiple medical centres in Iraq to assess patient demographics, pathological features, and disease staging. Data were gathered, and variables were examined statistically. The mean patient age was 58.6 years, with 35% of cases occurring in individuals under 50 years old, indicating a trend toward earlier onset. A slight male predominance was observed (54.2% male vs. 45.8% female). Tumour location was most frequently in the left colon (41.7%), followed by the right colon and rectum (29.2% each). Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma was the most common histopathological type (66.7%), and 75% of patients presented with advanced disease stages (Stage II or III). Adverse prognostic factors, including lymphovascular invasion (37.5%), perineural invasion (25%), and tumour budding (16.7%), were also noted. The results underscore the need for enhanced screening programs and public health initiatives in Iraq to promote early detection and improve colorectal cancer outcomes.

title: Determination of the approach of Polish gastroenterologists and surgeons to the diagnosis and treatment of complex cases of Crohn's disease-related perianal fistulas.
authors: Eder P, Banasiewicz T, Głażewska J, Reguła J, Rydzewska G, Wallner G, et al.
abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorder that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract. CD-related perianal fistulas are difficult to treat and require coordinated surgical-medical care. The aim of this study was to describe how Polish gastroenterologists and surgeons diagnose and manage complex perianal fistulas associated with Crohn's disease during initial and subsequent lines of treatment, including surgical care. A nationwide retrospective analysis was conducted, including a review of the medical records of 80 patients with complex perianal fistulas after failure of standard therapy, and surveys of 27 gastroenterologists representing the majority of centres involved in the B.32 programme and 12 colorectal surgeons (February-March 2023). In surveys, clinicians estimated that about 20% of their CD patients currently had a perianal fistula, while another 20% had a history of one; 24% of first fistulas reportedly preceded CD diagnosis, 36% occurred within 3 years, and 13% after > 10 years. Magnetic resonance imaging was the most frequently used imaging modality for complex fistulas. In the chart cohort, initial ("standard") therapy most often combined azathioprine, antibiotics, metronidazole, and glucocorticoids (median duration 13 weeks). After failure, 80% received combined surgical-medical care; 91% received biologics as first or second post-failure therapy (infliximab Management patterns vary and interdisciplinary coordination is inconsistent; structured care pathways and multidisciplinary clinics are needed in Poland.

title: Psychiatric diseases in patients following colorectal operations: a single-centre retrospective study.
authors: Mulita F, Pano I, Shaska E, Liolis E, Antzoulas A, Tasios K, et al.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the second most common cause of cancer-related death globally and the third most common type of cancer. This study aims to evaluate the prevalence of psychiatric morbidities after colorectal surgical procedures, identify associated risk factors for their development, and determine whether improved access to psychological therapies would benefit this patient population. Between January 2019 and December 2023, 603 patients with a diagnosis of colorectal disease underwent elective colorectal operations in our institution and were considered for this retrospective study. Data were collected from medical and operating theatre records as well as from the hospital-coded database. Patient data were primarily analysed for the incidence of colorectal diseases such as colorectal cancer, diverticulitis, and inflammatory bowel disease. Secondary variables include patient characteristics (age at operation, gender), length of hospital stay, and operative parameters (time and type). During the 5-year study period, a total of 603 records of patients operated on for colorectal disease in our institution were retrieved from the computer database. A total of 499 (83%) colectomies were performed using the open method, and 104 (17%) were performed using the laparoscopic technique. Among patients undergoing colorectal operation in our institution 126 (20.1%) had a psychiatric disorder in the one-year postoperative follow-up. The most common type of mental disorder was mood disorder, which appeared in 26 patients. This retrospective study shows that the technique of colectomy does not appear to affect the incidence of psychiatric disorders. However, our study indicates the need for a prospective randomised controlled trial with a larger number of participants.

title: A common germline 3' UTR variant controls DDIT4 translation efficiency and stress responses in cancer cells.
authors: Hamadou MH, Alunno L, Venturelli T, Valentini S, Dalfovo D, Lorenzini F, et al.
abstract: Systematic strategies for identifying and classifying variants that directly modulate ribosome engagement are lacking. Here, we develop and extensively validate a pipeline to identify translation-associated single-nucleotide polymorphisms (tranSNPs) by integrating analysis of total and polysome-associated mRNAs. Common variants showing allele-specific enrichment in polysomes, without corresponding changes in mRNA levels, were uncovered. We focused on rs1053639, a frequent germline SNP located in the 3' UTR of DNA damage-inducible transcript 4 (DDIT4), a key negative regulator of mTORC1. Using edited cell models, we showed that this variant controls DDIT4 protein output. Mechanistically, the two rs1053639 alleles differ in their interaction with the RNA-binding protein RBMX, leading to altered mRNA subcellular localization and translation. Functionally, allele-specific regulation of DDIT4 translation impacts stress-dependent mTORC1 repression and autophagy, resulting in divergent competitive fitness in co-culture or xenograft assays and response to therapeutic perturbations. Analysis of cancer patient datasets revealed an association between rs1053639 genotype and clinical outcome in colorectal cancer.

title: Fluoroscopy-Guided Colonoscopic Transanastomotic Drainage of a Delayed Presacral Collection After Rectal Cancer Surgery: A Case Report.
authors: Zouaoui M, Assili MA, Hnach Y, Azouaoui M, Aqodad N
abstract: Anastomotic leakage after rectal resection may present months after surgery as a contained presacral collection. When an established defect communicates with the rectal lumen, endoscopic transanastomotic drainage can use that tract without creating a new transmural access route. We report a 54-year-old man who presented six months after anterior rectal resection with fever, pelvic pain, tenesmus, and purulent rectal discharge. Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging showed a multiloculated 6 × 5 × 2 cm presacral collection with a fistulous tract to the posterior colorectal anastomosis. Radial endoscopic ultrasonography measured a longest cavity dimension of 87.1 mm, and colonoscopy identified a draining posterior anastomotic defect. After intravenous antibiotic therapy was initiated, the defect was cannulated under colonoscopic and fluoroscopic guidance, the cavity was lavaged, and a 7-Fr × 7-cm double-pigtail plastic stent was deployed for internal drainage. Symptoms and inflammatory markers normalized within one week. At two months, a residual 40-mm cavity remained, and a second identical stent was placed alongside the first. At three months, the patient remained asymptomatic, but both stents were still in situ, and definitive cavity closure had not yet been documented. This case demonstrates the technical feasibility of transanastomotic drainage and short-term clinical control in a selected patient without peritoneal signs; it does not establish durable healing or generalizable efficacy.

title: Pharmacological mechanisms of quercetin in liver and intestinal diseases: a gut-liver axis perspective.
authors: He X, Zhang T, Li Y, Qiu Y, Wang C, Wang H, et al.
abstract: Hepatic and gastrointestinal disorders share interconnected pathogenic mechanisms, yet their clinical management remains challenging. This has prompted interest in therapeutic approaches targeting the gut-liver axis. Quercetin, a natural flavonoid, has been studied in this context. To assess its pharmacological effects, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library for literature published since 2000 on quercetin in hepatic and intestinal diseases. This review focuses on the gut-liver axis as a framework for understanding the pharmacological effects of quercetin. Mechanistically, quercetin modulates gut-liver communication by reshaping the gut microbiota, promoting short-chain fatty acid production, and modulating bile acid metabolism. In preclinical models, it has been reported to modulate FXR/TGR5 signaling and preserve intestinal barrier integrity, thereby reducing endotoxin translocation and systemic inflammation. These effects are associated with downstream modulation of oxidative, inflammatory, and apoptotic pathways, including NF-κB, PI3K/Akt, and Nrf2. Furthermore, preclinical evidence indicates that quercetin attenuates liver injury, MASLD/MASH, fibrosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, and exerts protective effects in models of ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer. title: Bowel preparation for colonoscopy in patients with surgically altered anatomy: a narrative review and institutional protocol.
authors: Jaber F, Peicher M, Gomez Cifuentes JD, Forero Rios MP, Sealock RJ
abstract: Colonoscopy is a vital diagnostic and therapeutic procedure for diseases affecting the rectum, colon, and terminal ileum. In patients who have undergone colorectal surgery, postoperative colonoscopy is frequently required for purposes such as colorectal neoplasia surveillance. However, administering bowel preparation in this population poses significant challenges for patients, caregivers, and the endoscopy team, including gastroenterologists and nurses. Despite these challenges, there is limited peer-reviewed guidance on optimal bowel preparation strategies for these patients. This review summarizes the current data on bowel preparation in patients with surgically altered anatomy, identifies key challenges, addresses existing gaps in knowledge, and presents a tailored approach to bowel preparation in this population based on institutional protocol. In addition, we propose future directions for research and quality improvement to enhance outcomes in this cohort.

title: Underwater hybrid ESD versus conventional ESD for colorectal laterally spreading tumors: a retrospective study.
authors: Cheng Q, Feng YL, Chen LP
abstract: Conventional endoscopic submucosal dissection (C-ESD) is standard for colorectal laterally spreading tumors (LSTs) but is time-consuming. Underwater hybrid ESD (U-Hybrid ESD) is an emerging technique. We compared the efficacy and safety of U-Hybrid ESD versus C-ESD for colorectal LSTs. This exploratory, single-center retrospective study included 300 patients with LSTs ≥20 mm (U-Hybrid ESD, After multivariable adjustment, U-Hybrid ESD had significantly shorter procedure time (adjusted mean 21.29 vs. 31.99 min, adjusted mean difference -10.70, In this exploratory analysis, U-Hybrid ESD was associated with shorter procedure time and modest improvements in postoperative recovery metrics, without a significant increase in complications. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that U-Hybrid ESD may offer efficiency benefits for selected lesions, but the potential trend toward lower R0 rates for large or high-grade lesions warrants caution and prospective validation before any definitive size-based recommendations can be made.

title: Patient-aware single-cell analysis of fibrovascular remodeling in a predominantly colorectal cancer immunotherapy cohort.
authors: Gu Y, Li L, Zhang Y, Tang J, Wang Z, Luo X
abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and vascular mural cells may shape extracellular matrix organization in colorectal cancer. However, single-cell comparisons are susceptible to unequal cell recovery, ambient RNA, doublets, treatment-stage mixing, and repeated sampling within patients. We investigated fibrovascular remodeling using patients as the inferential unit and distinguished reproducible signals from donor-concentrated and context-dependent findings. We reanalyzed a published single-cell RNA sequencing cohort of 22 patients, including 20 with colorectal cancer and 2 with duodenal carcinoma. The primary pericyte analysis included 14 pretreatment matched normal-tumor pairs with at least three pericytes per tissue. We assessed ambient contamination and doublets using DecontX and scDblFinder. CAFs were reclustered at six response-blind resolutions, and the stable parent population was tested by patient-blocked pseudobulk analysis after excluding its dominant donor. Independent CRC single-cell and spatial datasets, a cross-cancer immunotherapy cohort, and TCGA were used for external testing. After DecontX correction, tumor pericytes had higher ECM6 scores (median paired change 0.309; false discovery rate [FDR] 0.018). Scores were also higher for the matrix stiffness transcriptional proxy (0.277; FDR 0.012) and the hypoxia/angiogenesis transcriptional program (0.255; FDR 0.028). All three signatures remained significant at the five-pericyte threshold (n=13). COL1A1 and FN1 increased in the analysis, although COL1A1 was borderline in the five-cell sensitivity analysis. Response-blind stability analysis identified a 2,983-cell ECM-remodeling CAF population represented in all 22 patients. After excluding P02, patient-blocked pseudobulk analysis in 15 patients showed higher matrix, inflammatory, and myCAF-related programs and a lower iCAF program. Neither SPP1 nor baseline enrichment in stable disease was supported. In GSE205506, a disjoint 10-gene fibroblast gate retained higher inflammatory and composite CAF scores in non-pCR samples. The highest-scoring unsupervised cluster was donor-concentrated and showed no patient-level association with response. Spatial and cross-cancer analyses yielded mixed or null results. These results support pretreatment fibrovascular transcriptional remodeling at the patient level. They do not establish an SPP1-high response biomarker, a mechanical stiffness phenotype, or causal CAF-to-pericyte signaling. Donor-aware analysis places the rare-cluster observation within a broader, reproducible ECM-remodeling CAF program while defining its evidential limits.
cn_title: 患者感知的单细胞分析揭示结直肠癌免疫治疗队列中纤维血管重塑
insight: 该研究以患者为推断单位，识别出治疗前纤维血管转录重塑的可重复信号，但未证实SPP1高表达作为反应生物标志物或机械刚度表型，提示肠癌免疫治疗研究需警惕供体集中效应。
grade_rationale: 基于已发表单细胞队列的再分析，虽方法严谨但为探索性研究，未提供临床干预证据，暂不改变实践。

title: Gracilis Muscle Flap Reconstruction for Refractory Urethral Complications After Pelvic Surgery: A Report of Two Cases.
authors: Maeda A, Tobu S, Yukimoto M, Kusano S, Kawasaki M, Kakinoki H, et al.
abstract: Iatrogenic urethral injury and rectourethral fistula are rare and challenging complications of pelvic surgery. Case 1 involved a 72-year-old man with persistent urinary leakage after primary repair of a prostatic urethral injury sustained during rectal cancer surgery following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Approximately 2 years later, reclosure of the urethral defect with local periurethral reinforcement and gracilis muscle flap coverage enabled catheter removal and spontaneous voiding. Case 2 involved a 62-year-old man who developed a rectourethral fistula after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy. After conservative management failed, fistulectomy, rectal and urinary tract repair, and gracilis muscle flap interposition achieved fistula closure and subsequent colostomy reversal. These cases illustrate two distinct reconstructive roles of the gracilis muscle flap: vascularized reinforcement of a compromised urethral repair and interposition between repaired urinary and rectal sites.
cn_title: 股薄肌皮瓣重建治疗盆腔术后难治性尿道并发症：两例报告
insight: 股薄肌皮瓣可为直肠癌术后难治性尿道损伤及直肠尿道瘘提供血管化加固与组织间隔，为盆腔肿瘤术后复杂并发症的修复提供新思路。
grade_rationale: 仅两例个案报道，无对照或长期随访，证据等级低，但为临床罕见并发症提供可借鉴的手术策略。

title: Noninvasive Biomarkers for Early Detection of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis in Ulcerative Colitis.
authors: Asadi Sarabi P, Beheshti-Maal A, Judaki AA, Teymoorian SK, Hashemian Z, Rismani E, et al.
abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a progressive cholestatic liver disease strongly associated with ulcerative colitis (UC). Although uncommon, PSC-associated ulcerative colitis (PSCUC) represents a distinct subtype of inflammatory bowel diseases characterized by a higher risk of colorectal and hepatobiliary cancers. Early diagnosis remains a challenging issue because of the lack of specific biomarkers. Bioinformatic analysis of Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets identified potential, specific, and noninvasive biomarkers via differential gene expression and functional enrichment. After processing the data, S100A8 and S100A12 were identified as candidate biomarkers for detecting PSC in patients with UC. S100A8 encodes one component of calprotectin, the S100A8/S100A9 heterodimer widely used as a marker of intestinal inflammation. These two genes are primarily involved in inflammation, immune responses, and leukocyte recruitment, making them potentially useful biomarkers for early detection in PSC in UC patients. These biomarkers offer potential implications for disease stratification and therapeutic targeting. Further validation in prospective clinical studies is warranted to confirm their diagnostic and prognostic utilities.
cn_title: 溃疡性结肠炎中原发性硬化性胆管炎早期检测的无创生物标志物
insight: 生物信息学筛选出S100A8/S100A12作为UC患者中PSC早期检测的无创候选标志物，提示可用于疾病分层，但需前瞻性验证。
grade_rationale: 基于GEO数据的生物信息学分析，无临床验证，证据等级低，尚不足以改变实践。

title: Joint Model for Assessing the Effect of Frailty and Longitudinal Measures in Time-To-Event Outcome.
authors: Hari A, Dennis D, Nair JKKPM, Mathew A
abstract: Joint modeling provides a robust statistical framework for simultaneously modeling longitudinal covariate and time-to-event outcome. Apart from the interdependence between longitudinal and survival outcomes there may exist some unobserved random heterogeneity which can be modeled using a joint frailty model (JFM). Unlike existing JFMs, where two survival events are modeled using a frailty, our framework incorporates frailty into the survival sub-model to accommodate an additional source of variation at the survival endpoint. So here we developed a novel JFM and estimated the parameters using maximum-likelihood estimation method. The analyses were performed using R Software and illustrated using colorectal cancer data. The frailty component was introduced in colorectal cancer data to account for the unobserved variability in survival risk beyond the observed clinical characteristics. The highly significant frailty variance confirmed the presence of unobserved heterogeneity in survival outcomes. When compared with the standard Joint model (JM), the JFM demonstrated improved model fit and captured additional unexplained heterogeneity among individuals, leading to more precise hazard estimates. Further we conducted Monte Carlo simulations to compare the performance of the proposed model under various simulation scenarios (censoring [20% and 50%], frailty variance (≈0, 0.5, 1), and sample sizes [n = 100, 250, 500]). Performance was assessed using bias, root mean squared error and model fit indices. The findings highlight the importance of incorporating the frailty term in joint modeling, particularly in cancer prognostic studies where individual heterogeneity plays a crucial role.
cn_title: 联合脆弱模型评估衰弱与纵向指标对结直肠癌生存结局的影响
insight: 提出新型联合脆弱模型，能更精准估计结直肠癌患者生存风险，提示个体异质性在预后研究中的重要性，为肝转移等复杂场景的纵向数据分析提供方法学工具。
grade_rationale: 方法学创新但仅基于回顾性数据模拟验证，尚未进入临床决策流程，实践改变潜力有限。

title: Research trends and hotspots in colorectal cancer screening: Bibliometric and visualization analysis (2015-2024).
authors: Zhou J, Zhou H, Xu J, Wang M, Liu L, Tang X
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC), is a highly prevalent malignant tumor worldwide, and early screening is key to improving its prognosis. Currently, CRC screening research is growing exponentially, but its core research hotspots, evolutionary trends, and interdisciplinary features are not clear. In this study, we used bibliometric analysis to analyze the distribution of literature, research hotspots, and cutting-edge developments in the field of CRC screening worldwide, and to provide a scientific basis for optimizing screening strategies. Publications on CRC screening from 2015 to 2024 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. VOSviewer (v1.6.20), RStudio (v4.4.1), and CiteSpace (v6.4.2) were used for bibliometric and visual analyses. The main analyses included publication trends, countries, authors, journals, references, and keywords. A total of 3245 publications were included in the analysis. Global publications on CRC screening showed a steady upward trend over the past decade, with an annual growth rate of 2.17%. The United States contributed the highest number of publications, and the University of North Carolina ranked as the most productive institution. GASTROENTEROLOGY and GUT were the most frequently cited journals in this field. Lansdorp‑Vogelaar I was among the most prolific authors. The most cited article was "CRC screening for average-risk adults: 2018 guideline update from the American Cancer Society." Keyword analysis showed that the research hotspots in this field included colonoscopy, biomarker, adenoma detection rate, artificial intelligence, etc. Current research in CRC screening focuses on traditional screening methods, population-related factors, and emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence. Stronger international collaboration and interdisciplinary studies are needed to advance the field.
cn_title: 2015-2024年结直肠癌筛查研究趋势与热点的文献计量与可视化分析
insight: 该文献计量分析揭示结直肠癌筛查研究聚焦结肠镜、生物标志物、腺瘤检出率与人工智能，提示AI辅助筛查与优化筛查策略是未来方向，对肝转移早期发现具间接启示。
grade_rationale: 文献计量分析属描述性研究方法，无临床干预或结局验证，虽样本量大但不改变临床实践。

title: Trends and projections of colorectal carcinoma mortality in U.S. adults, 1999-2050: A CDC WONDER-based ecological time-series analysis.
authors: Atif K, Atif E, Das V, Qazi S, Ali M, Ahmad A, et al.
abstract: Colorectal carcinoma (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer mortality in the United States (U.S.); however, contemporary long-term projections by demographic and geographic strata are limited. This study examined national colorectal cancer mortality trends from 1999 to 2025 and projected age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) through 2050. We conducted an ecological time-series analysis of U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years using Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research Multiple Cause of Death data. CRC-related deaths were identified by any mention of International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision codes C18-C20 on the death certificate. AAMRs per 100,000 population were calculated overall and stratified by sex, age group, race and ethnicity, urbanization, census region, state, and place of death. Joinpoint regression was used to estimate the annual percent change and average annual percent change. A demographically optimized ensemble forecasting model was used to project AAMRs from 2026 to 2050. From 1999 to 2025, 1,674,393 CRC-related deaths were recorded. Overall, the AAMR declined from 38.11 in 1999 to 23.14 in 2025 (average annual percent change, -1.99%; 95% confidence interval, -2.13 to -1.85; P < .001), but recent rates have stabilized. The mean AAMR was higher among men than women (34.13 vs 23.43) and higher in nonmetropolitan than metropolitan areas (32.43 vs 28.49). Non-Hispanic Black adults had the highest racial and ethnic burdens (37.45). Adults aged 25 to 44 years showed a significant increase in mortality (annual percent change, 1.13%; 95% confidence interval, 0.93 to 1.33; P < .001). Most deaths occurred at home (41.15% of deaths). The overall AAMR was projected to continue declining slowly, from 23.02 in 2026 to 21.56 in 2050, at a slower pace than the 1999 to 2016 decline. U.S. CRC mortality has declined substantially and is projected to continue declining slowly through 2050, rather than resume its earlier faster decline, with persistent sex, racial, rural, age, and geographic disparities. Targeted strategies are needed to improve screening completion, diagnostic follow-up, rural access, equity, and early-onset colorectal cancer detection.
cn_title: 美国结直肠癌死亡率趋势与2050年预测：基于CDC WONDER的生态学时间序列分析
insight: 美国结直肠癌死亡率总体下降但趋于停滞，25-44岁人群死亡率上升，提示需关注早发性肠癌筛查与卫生公平。
grade_rationale: 基于CDC WONDER大样本死亡数据的生态学时间序列与预测分析，样本量大但为描述性、无个体数据，对临床实践影响有限。

title: Endoscopic self-expandable metal stent placement before conversion therapy for advanced and recurrent gastrointestinal malignancies: A single-center retrospective study.
authors: Liu Q, Yu R, Wang J, Zong X, Bai M
abstract: Endoscopic self-expandable metal stent (SEMS) placement is an established palliative treatment for malignant gastrointestinal (GI) obstruction, but data on its use in patients eligible for subsequent conversion therapy remain limited. We describe our single-center experience with SEMS placement in advanced and recurrent GI malignancies and report the proportions of patients who subsequently completed antitumor therapy and underwent R0 resection. We retrospectively reviewed 148 consecutive patients with advanced or recurrent GI malignancies who underwent SEMS placement for malignant obstruction or fistula at a single center between January 2019 and December 2022. Technical success, clinical success, fistula closure, adverse events, subsequent antitumor therapy, R0 resection, and overall survival were assessed. All analyses were descriptive and exploratory; no adjustment for confounding was performed. Gastrointestinal SEMSs were successfully placed in 146 patients (98.6%). The overall obstruction-relief rate was 95.7%, and the overall fistula-closure rate was 80%. No patient in this cohort required rescue gastrostomy or colostomy because of failed stent therapy during the study period. A total of 132 patients (94.3%) completed antitumor treatment after endoscopic metal stent placement (EMSP). R0 resection was performed in 8.89% of patients with esophageal malignancies, 10.10% of those with gastric malignancies, and 17.9% of those with colorectal malignancies. Median survival time (MST) was generally longer among patients who underwent conversion surgery than among those who did not. Comorbidities, anemia, and SEMS-related adverse events were also analyzed as factors associated with conversion therapy after SEMS placement; the respective P values were .039, <.001, and .012. In this retrospective single-center series, SEMS placement was technically feasible and relieved obstruction or closed fistulas in most patients with advanced or recurrent GI malignancies; a subset subsequently completed antitumor therapy and underwent R0 resection. These data support feasibility and demonstrate associations but cannot establish a survival benefit; prospective comparative studies are required.
cn_title: 晚期及复发消化道肿瘤转化治疗前内镜下自膨式金属支架置入的单中心回顾性研究
insight: SEMS在拟行转化治疗的晚期/复发消化道肿瘤中技术可行、可解除梗阻，部分结直肠癌患者后续获R0切除，为肠癌梗阻转化路径提供可行性依据，但需前瞻验证。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性描述性研究，无混杂校正与对照，仅提示可行性，不足以改变实践。

title: Presumed oxaliplatin-related Guillain-Barré syndrome: A case report and review of chemotherapy-related Guillain-Barré syndrome.
authors: Chohan S, Saif MW
abstract: Oxaliplatin, a platinum-based chemotherapeutic widely used in colorectal, hepatobiliary, and pancreatic malignancies, commonly causes a symmetric, cold-induced sensory neuropathy. Rarely, it has been linked to immune-mediated Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS), which can be misattributed to drug-induced sensory neuropathy and delay diagnosis. Distinguishing the two is critical because GBS can progress to respiratory failure and death. A 77-year-old woman with concurrent metastatic cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal carcinoma developed acute, symmetric, ascending motor weakness with clinically preserved sensation approximately 2 weeks after her last cycle of gemcitabine, oxaliplatin, leucovorin, and 5-fluorouracil (GOLF), rapidly progressing to an inability to ambulate. Neurological examination and cerebrospinal fluid analysis (albuminocytologic dissociation) were consistent with GBS, and nerve conduction studies demonstrated absent motor and sensory responses, indicating a severe axonal variant (AMSAN); sensory involvement was electrodiagnostic rather than clinical. An extensive infectious, autoimmune, and paraneoplastic workup was negative, supporting a diagnosis of presumed oxaliplatin-related GBS; a Naranjo score of 4 indicated a "possible" drug association. She received 5 sessions of therapeutic plasma exchange followed by 4 sessions of intravenous immunoglobulin. No meaningful neurological recovery occurred; she developed progressive respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation and died. Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for GBS in patients on platinum-based chemotherapy who develop abrupt, symmetric motor weakness after common causes have been ruled out. Because causality is difficult to establish, the association remains presumed; early recognition, prompt immunotherapy, and pharmacovigilance are essential to reduce mortality.
cn_title: 奥沙利铂相关吉兰-巴雷综合征：病例报告与化疗相关GBS综述
insight: 提示铂类化疗后急性对称性运动无力需警惕GBS而非单纯神经毒性，早期识别与免疫治疗可能降低致死风险，对肠癌奥沙利铂方案安全管理有警示意义。
grade_rationale: 单例个案结合文献综述，Naranjo评分仅提示可能关联，证据等级低，但具临床警示价值。

title: Comparative outcomes of natural orifice specimen extraction surgery versus conventional minilaparotomy-assisted specimen extraction in colorectal cancer: A single-center retrospective study.
authors: Liao Y, Qiu R, Ma W
abstract: Natural orifice specimen extraction surgery (NOSES) has emerged as an advanced minimally invasive technique that eliminates abdominal wall incisions for specimen retrieval; nevertheless, comparative data on its efficacy relative to conventional minilaparotomy-assisted extraction in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain limited. This retrospective analysis was conducted on 126 patients who underwent laparoscopic CRC resection at our institution, allocated to either the NOSES group (transanal specimen extraction, n = 49) or the conventional group (minilaparotomy-assisted extraction, n = 77), comparing perioperative parameters, postoperative recovery indicators, complication rates, and pathological outcomes. The NOSES group demonstrated significantly shorter time to first flatus (2.3 ± 0.9 vs 2.9 ± 1.1 days, P = .002), time to first liquid diet (3.1 ± 1.0 vs 3.8 ± 1.3 days, P = .001), and postoperative hospital stay (8.4 ± 3.2 vs 10.1 ± 4.1 days, P = .014). Visual analog scale pain scores on postoperative day 1 were significantly lower in the NOSES group (3.2 ± 1.1 vs 4.5 ± 1.3, P < .001), with reduced additional analgesic requirements (22.4% vs 44.2%, P = .014). Overall complication rates were significantly lower in the NOSES group (12.2% vs 24.7%, P = .043), with wound infections occurring exclusively in the conventional group (0% vs 6.5%, P = .045). No significant differences were observed in operative time, estimated blood loss, anastomotic leakage, lymph node yield, or R0 resection rate (all P > .05). In conclusion, NOSES appears to be a safe and feasible alternative to conventional minilaparotomy-assisted specimen extraction in highly selected patients with CRC, offering advantages in postoperative pain control, gastrointestinal function recovery, and wound-related complication reduction without compromising oncological integrity.
cn_title: 自然腔道标本取出术与传统小切口辅助取标本在结直肠癌中的疗效比较：单中心回顾性研究
insight: NOSES可减轻术后疼痛、促进胃肠功能恢复并减少伤口并发症，且不损害肿瘤学完整性，为结直肠癌微创手术提供了可选方案，但需前瞻性研究验证。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性设计，样本量有限（126例），证据等级较低，但结果支持NOSES的短期优势，可能影响术式选择。

title: The bidirectional causal relationships of insomnia with eleven cancers: A Mendelian randomization study.
authors: Li J, Cheng L, Li F, Xu Y
abstract: Insomnia is closely associated with tumors and is recognized as a risk factor for cancer development. This two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) study investigated the potential causal link between genetically determined insomnia and various cancers, including brain, colorectal, esophageal, gastric, hepatic bile duct, liver, lung, malignant lymphoma, pancreatic, skin, and thyroid cancers. Summary statistics from genome-wide association studies for insomnia and eleven cancer types were examined. instrumental variables (IVs) were selected from single nucleotide polymorphisms that passed strict quality control for minimal linkage disequilibrium and genome-wide significance. All IVs demonstrated strong predictive power for insomnia, with F-statistics exceeding the conventional threshold of 10. The primary analysis was conducted using the inverse variance weighted method. Sensitivity analyses were performed using MR-Egger regression, weighted median, and weighted mode methods to test robustness, pleiotropy, and heterogeneity. MR analysis suggested potential causal associations between insomnia and increased risk of hepatic bile duct cancer (odds ratio [OR] = 4.458, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.074-18.493, P = .040), reduced risk of hepatic cancer (OR = 0.312, 95% CI: 0.100-0.973, P = .045), and reduced risk of skin cancers (OR = 0.599, 95% CI: 0.439-0.818, P = .001). However, after Bonferroni correction (adjusted threshold P < .0045), these associations did not retain statistical significance. No notable causal influence of these cancers on insomnia was observed. Sensitivity analyses showed no evidence of reverse causality or significant bias. These findings, though not retaining statistical significance after stringent multiple testing correction, provide suggestive evidence that genetically predicted insomnia may influence the risk of certain cancers, potentially through mechanisms involving genetic predisposition and biological pathways that modulate inflammation, immune function, and circadian rhythms. The study highlights the translational value of understanding insomnia's role in cancer risk, suggesting that clinicians should consider this association when managing patients with insomnia. Further research with larger sample sizes is warranted to validate these findings.
cn_title: 失眠与十一种癌症双向因果关系的孟德尔随机化研究
insight: 该研究提示失眠可能因果性影响肝内胆管癌等风险，但经多重校正后不显著，对肠癌/肝转移研究启示有限，需更大样本验证。
grade_rationale: 基于GWAS的孟德尔随机化研究，但主要结果经Bonferroni校正后无统计学显著性，证据等级有限。

title: Prognostic value of systemic inflammatory markers in patients with malignancy-associated pulmonary thromboembolism: A retrospective observational study.
authors: Arslan Aksu E, Özdemir L, Gegin S, Özdemir B
abstract: Pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE) is a severe and potentially fatal complication in patients with malignancy. Systemic inflammation plays an important role in both cancer progression and thrombogenesis. This study aimed to evaluate the association of systemic inflammatory indices with in-hospital mortality and clinical risk classification in patients with malignancy-associated PTE. This retrospective study included 75 adult patients diagnosed with both malignancy and PTE at a tertiary chest diseases center between February 2018 and June 2025. Demographic characteristics, cancer types, laboratory values at diagnosis, treatment details, and clinical outcomes were recorded. Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), lymphocyte-to-CRP ratio (LCRPR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), and systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) were calculated from blood samples obtained at diagnosis. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality, and the secondary outcome was the association between systemic inflammatory markers and ESC PTE clinical risk classification. The mean age was 69.5 ± 11.8 years, and 56% of patients were male. Lung (24%), colorectal (13.3%), and breast (9.3%) cancers were the most common malignancies. In-hospital mortality was 20%. Neutrophil count (P = .026), NLR (P = .032), and lactate (P = .027) were significantly higher in patients who died during hospitalization. ROC analysis identified an NLR cutoff value of 4.95, with a sensitivity of 86.7% and a specificity of 51.7%. Neutrophil count and SIRI were significantly higher in the intermediate-risk group (P = .036 and P = .049, respectively), whereas troponin was highest in the high-risk group (P < .001). Neutrophil count, NLR, and lactate levels were associated with in-hospital mortality in patients with malignancy-associated PTE. Neutrophil count and SIRI were also associated with ESC clinical risk classification. These findings should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger prospective studies.
cn_title: 系统性炎症标志物对恶性肿瘤相关肺栓塞患者预后的预测价值
insight: 小样本回顾性研究提示NLR、中性粒细胞计数与肿瘤相关肺栓塞院内死亡相关，为肠癌患者血栓并发症风险分层提供廉价炎症指标线索，但需前瞻验证。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性小样本（75例）、结直肠癌仅占13.3%，仅探索性发现，不足以改变实践。

title: Prophylactic administration of probiotic strains Weizmannia coagulans and Saccharomyces boulardii attenuates early dysplastic changes in an AOM/DSS-induced mouse model.
authors: Matboli M, Eissa S, Mohamed RH, Kotb N, Hamam GG, Tarek M, et al.
abstract: Colorectal dysplasia represents an early stage of colorectal carcinogenesis and is closely associated with chronic inflammation and altered microRNA (miRNA) expression. Probiotic strains such as Weizmannia coagulans (formerly Bacillus coagulans) and Saccharomyces boulardii possess anti-inflammatory properties and may influence host miRNA expression, suggesting their potential as prophylactic agents against inflammation-associated colorectal dysplasia. Mice received prophylactic oral administration of Weizmannia coagulans or Saccharomyces boulardii beginning one week before azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium (AOM/DSS) induction and continuing throughout the experimental period. Histopathological examination, TNF-α immunohistochemistry, serum pro-inflammatory cytokine measurements, and miRNA expression profiling using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) were performed to evaluate the prophylactic effects of both probiotic strains. Prophylactic administration of both probiotic strains significantly attenuated early dysplastic alterations and inflammatory cell infiltration compared with the AOM/DSS group (p < 0.05). These histopathological improvements were accompanied by significantly lower serum levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and IL-1β, together with reduced TNF-α immunoreactivity (p < 0.05). In addition, probiotic pretreatment attenuated the altered miRNA expression profile induced by AOM/DSS. Compared with the model group, expression of miR-122-5p, miR-29b-5p, and miR-15b-5p was significantly reduced, whereas miR-98-5p, miR-202-5p, miR-21-5p, and let-7i-5p showed increased expression and were associated with miRNA expression patterns that more closely resembled those of the control group (p < 0.01). Prophylactic administration of Weizmannia coagulans and Saccharomyces boulardii reduced inflammation-associated early dysplastic changes while preserving normal miRNA expression patterns in an AOM/DSS-induced murine model. These findings support the potential of probiotic prophylaxis as an early preventive strategy against colorectal dysplasia and provide a foundation for future studies investigating its clinical applicability.
cn_title: 益生菌预防给药减轻AOM/DSS小鼠模型早期结直肠异型增生
insight: 益生菌通过抗炎和调控miRNA表达抑制结直肠癌早期异型增生，提示微生态干预可能成为肠癌化学预防新策略，但需临床转化验证。
grade_rationale: 临床前小鼠模型研究，样本量有限，无外部验证，但机制探索较深入，尚不足以改变临床实践。

title: Educational Materials for Health-Related Discrete Choice Experiments: A Theory-Driven Approach.
authors: Marceta SM, Tabbers HK, de Koning BB, Falahee M, de Bekker-Grob EW, Veldwijk J
abstract: To make informed choices in health-related discrete choice experiments (DCEs), respondents need to understand the choice scenarios, alternatives, attributes and attribute levels presented to them. Respondent populations are often highly diverse in knowledge and experience, leading to varying informational needs that make it challenging to design educational materials that sufficiently inform all respondents without disengaging others. At present, however, structured guidance on developing DCE educational materials is lacking. Drawing on the instructional design literature, this paper investigates whether theory-driven adaptations to educational materials improve respondent comprehension and engagement in health-related DCEs. Informed by three focus groups on DCE informational needs, we identified four design principles from the instructional design literature relevant to DCE educational materials: whole-task instruction, making inferences explicit, adapting information to respondents' prior knowledge and embedding self-check questions with corrective feedback. Educational materials for three existing DCEs (influenza vaccination, colorectal cancer screening and rheumatoid arthritis prevention) were redesigned to incorporate these principles. Panel respondents (N = 1754) were randomized to receive either the original or the adapted educational materials, and effects on comprehension, engagement, internal validity and choice consistency were assessed. Adapted materials increased time spent on educational content and were associated with small improvements in selected comprehension outcomes, though effects were often not statistically significant against the co-created comparator. Self-check questions revealed considerable comprehension gaps regardless of condition, underscoring that co-creation and pre-testing alone do not guarantee sufficient respondent comprehension. Educational materials also emerged as a meaningful source of selective dropout in all surveys, predominantly among respondents with lower education levels, posing a risk to sample representativeness that warrants attention in future research. Adapting DCE educational materials based on educational theory and instructional design principles offers a promising approach to improving respondent engagement and understanding. To enable cumulative learning, we further encourage researchers to report comprehension outcomes and publish educational materials as supplementary materials.
cn_title: 健康教育材料设计理论对结直肠癌筛查离散选择实验的影响
insight: 理论驱动的教育材料可小幅提升DCE理解与参与度，但理解缺口仍存；提示肠癌筛查偏好研究需重视材料预试与代表性偏倚。
grade_rationale: 随机对照方法学研究但非临床干预，聚焦DCE方法学，对临床实践改变潜力有限。

title: Prognostic nomogram for early-onset locally advanced rectal cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy: a SEER analysis.
authors: Kao YK, Chen PC, Yang PW, Chen CH, Chen CI
abstract: Early-onset locally advanced rectal cancer presents unique challenges in treatment and prognosis. This study aimed to develop and validate a prognostic nomogram for patients aged 18-50 years with locally advanced rectal cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, addressing the lack of tailored prognostic tools for this growing patient population. Using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) database, we analyzed 2,853 patients who received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy between 2010 and 2020. Patients were divided into training (n = 1,990) and validation (n = 863) cohorts. Cox proportional hazard regression models identified prognostic factors for overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS). Nomograms were constructed and validated using Harrell's C-index and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Independent predictors of poor OS and CSS included male sex, unmarried status (particularly divorced/separated/widowed), non-Hispanic black and American Indian/Alaskan native races, advanced T stage, increased positive regional nodes, and positive carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA). The nomogram demonstrated good discriminative ability in the validation cohort, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.767 and 0.742 for 3-year OS and CSS, respectively, and 0.705 and 0.697 for 5-year OS and CSS, respectively. The developed nomogram and identified prognostic factors provide valuable tools for individualized risk stratification and treatment optimization in young patients with locally advanced rectal cancer. These findings can aid in clinical decision-making and patient counseling. However, further external validation and prospective evaluations are necessary to confirm the clinical utility of this prognostic model in diverse healthcare settings.
cn_title: 早发性局部晚期直肠癌新辅助放化疗预后列线图的SEER分析
insight: 基于SEER大样本构建早发性局部晚期直肠癌新辅助放化疗预后列线图，为年轻患者个体化风险分层提供工具，但需外部验证。
grade_rationale: 基于SEER数据库的回顾性队列研究，样本量大但缺乏外部验证，对临床实践改变潜力有限。

title: Patient-specific 3D vascular reconstructions improve preoperative planning for right colectomy with complete mesocolic excision: A crossover study.
authors: Diallo E, Cazelles A, Bajul M, Saltel-Fulero A, Rebibo L, M'Harzi L, et al.
abstract: Complete mesocolic excision (CME) for right-sided colon cancer is technically demanding due to substantial variability in mesenteric vascular anatomy. Patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) vascular reconstructions may improve preoperative planning by enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of anatomical analysis. This study assessed the impact of 3D reconstructions on anatomical accuracy and interpretation time compared with conventional CT. This retrospective, single-centre comparative study used a cross-over design. Portal-venous phase CT scans were analysed using either conventional CT interpretation or patient-specific 3D vascular reconstructions (Visible Patient®, Strasbourg, France). Readers with different levels of experience assessed right colonic arterial and venous anatomy. Anatomical accuracy and interpretation time were compared using mixed-effects models accounting for reader- and patient-related effects. Thirty patients and fourteen readers (seven junior and seven senior) were included, yielding 840 imaging assessments. Anatomical accuracy was significantly higher with 3D reconstructions (adjusted OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.76-2.40; P<0.001), independently of reader experience and reading sequence. Median interpretation time was significantly shorter with 3D reconstructions compared with conventional CT (150 s [110-232] vs. 335 s [203-500], P<0.0001). In multivariable analysis, 3D reconstructions remained independently associated with reduced interpretation time, with a stronger effect in junior (-60%) than senior readers (-35%). Patient-specific 3D vascular reconstructions improve both the accuracy and efficiency of preoperative anatomical assessment for right-sided colon surgery compared with conventional CT interpretation. These findings support their integration into preoperative planning for CME, with potential benefits for surgical standardisation and training.
cn_title: 患者个体化3D血管重建提升右半结肠癌CME术前规划：交叉研究
insight: 个体化3D血管重建可提高右半结肠CME术前血管解剖判读准确性与效率，尤其利于低年资医师，支持其用于术前规划与培训。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性交叉设计、样本量小（30例），仅提示术前规划工具优化，尚不足以改变临床实践。

title: Simplified Chromatography-based Purification approach with utilizing Tangential Flow Filtration for Colorectal Cancer Biomarker: Carcinoembryonic Antigen.
authors: Rane AM, Badgujar SB, Shukla KK, Daftary RS, Prabhu SV, Santosh Kumar AW, et al.
abstract: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is a clinically important biomarker for cancer diagnosis and prognosis, particularly in colorectal cancer. This investigation introduces a simplified approach for the purification of native CEA antigen from the ascitic fluid of patients with colorectal cancer. Moreover, the technique allows the characterization of CEA though ensuring its structural and functional integrity is preserved. The CEA purification was achieved using perchloric acid precipitation, tangential flow filtration and sequential chromatography. The isolated CEA showed a relative molecular mass of ∼200 kDa and was analyzed using SDS-PAGE, size-exclusion FPLC and immunoblotting, confirming high purity comparable to reference form of native CEA protein. Peptide mass fingerprinting of trypsin-digested and deglycosylated CEA antigen identified it as CEACAM5_HUMAN (Uniprot ID: P06731). The proposed method demonstrates the adaptability for larger volume and practical approach for production of native form of CEA protein, also potential utility for future diagnostic applications, clinical research and bioanalytical studies.
cn_title: 基于切向流过滤的简化色谱法纯化结直肠癌生物标志物癌胚抗原
insight: 该研究建立了一种从结直肠癌患者腹水中纯化天然CEA的简化方法，为CEA的临床诊断应用和生物分析研究提供了实用工具。
grade_rationale: 方法学改进研究，非临床干预或结局研究，但为CEA纯化提供了可扩展的实用方案，对生物标志物研究有辅助价值。

title: Serrated polyp detection rates beyond adenoma detection rate for postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer: findings from the SCREESCO trial.
authors: Sekiguchi M, Westerberg M, Andreasson A, Bozorg SR, Forsberg AM
abstract: The association between serrated polyp detection rates, including proximal serrated polyp detection rate (PSPDR), and postcolonoscopy colorectal cancer (PCCRC) remains unestablished. We investigated PCCRC incidence and characteristics, and explored associations of PSPDR and adenoma detection rate (ADR) with PCCRC in colonoscopy- and fecal immunochemical test (FIT)-based screening within the Screening of Swedish Colons (SCREESCO) trial. Data from participants who underwent colonoscopy in the colonoscopy and FIT arms were analyzed. PCCRC, defined as colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosed >6 months after a colonoscopy that did not detect CRC, was identified through linkage with cancer registries. Associations between PSPDR and PCCRC incidence were assessed using Cox models. Of 9982 and 5875 individuals in the colonoscopy and FIT arms, PCCRC was identified in 20 and 17 individuals, with 3-year PCCRC rates of 5.9% (3/51) and 3.5% (4/115), respectively. Compared with screening-detected CRC, PCCRC more often involved right-sided location and advanced stage. The 5-year cumulative incidence of PCCRC was 0.16% (95%CI 0.10%-0.27%) and 0.06% (95%CI 0.02%-0.15%) when colonoscopies were performed by endoscopists with low vs. high PSPDR (<10% vs. ≥10%), respectively. Among endoscopists with high ADR, 5-year PCCRC incidence was 0.13% (95%CI 0.04%-0.32%) vs. 0.06% (95%CI 0.02%-0.16%) for those with low vs. high PSPDR, respectively. Within this group, PCCRC incidence over 8 years decreased as PSPDR increased (hazard ratio per percentage-point increase, 0.90; 95%CI 0.82-1.00; P = 0.04). Despite the limited number of PCCRC events, this study suggests that PSPDR provides complementary information beyond ADR for identifying colonoscopies with higher PCCRC incidence.
cn_title: SCREESCO试验：锯齿状息肉检出率与结肠镜后结直肠癌风险相关
insight: 在腺瘤检出率之外，近端锯齿状息肉检出率可补充识别结肠镜后结直肠癌高风险内镜医师，提示筛查质量指标应纳入锯齿状病变检出。
grade_rationale: 基于大型前瞻性筛查试验SCREESCO的二次分析，虽PCCRC事件数有限，但提示PSPDR可作为ADR之外的补充质控指标，具有改变内镜质控实践的潜力。

title: Akkermansia muciniphila attenuates macrophage efferocytosis to enhance anti-PD-1 efficacy in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer.
authors: Jiang YT, Li GQ, Zhou YW, Jiang ZD, Zhao YN, Zhang Y, et al.
abstract: Approximately 85% of colorectal cancers (CRCs) are microsatellite stable (MSS) and thus exhibit intrinsic resistance to anti-programmed death-1 (PD-1) therapy. In this study, we demonstrate that oral administration of Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk) suppresses tumorigenesis and reprograms the tumor microenvironment in MSS CRC mouse models. Akk attenuates macrophage efferocytosis through the TLR2/NF-κB pathway, an effect that leads to the accumulation of apoptotic cancer cells, which activates the cGAS-STING pathway and potentiates type I interferon production. cn_title: Akkermansia muciniphila通过抑制巨噬细胞胞葬作用增强MSS结直肠癌抗PD-1疗效
insight: 揭示肠道益生菌Akk经TLR2/NF-κB抑制巨噬细胞胞葬、激活cGAS-STING增强MSS肠癌抗PD-1疗效，为微卫星稳定型肠癌免疫增敏提供菌群干预新靶点。

title: Putrescine alters the composition of interstitial dendritic cell subsets by suppressing Cybb-dependent oxidative phosphorylation.
authors: Zhang Y, Tan Z, Li D, Lian H
abstract: Putrescine, a core polyamine, is closely linked to intestinal immune homeostasis and the pathogenesis of intestinal disease, yet its role in shaping dendritic cell (DC) subset differentiation in the intestinal lamina propria and the mechanism behind it remains undefined. Here, we first performed integrated analysis of seven public human single-cell RNA sequencing datasets to profile dendritic cell subsets across colorectal cancer tissues with varied MMR phenotypes. We fed mice a 1% (w/v) putrescine diet to raise intestinal putrescine levels and examined the effects on lamina propria DC subsets using flow cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptomics, and O2K-based metabolic assays. cn_title: 腐胺通过抑制Cybb依赖性氧化磷酸化重塑肠道树突状细胞亚群
insight: 揭示腐胺经Cybb/氧化磷酸化调控cDC1分化，为肠癌免疫微环境代谢干预提供新靶点，但尚需人体验证。
