title: The impact of National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer accreditation on patient volume and geographical scope in a community hospital.
authors: Klein EN, Schroeder-Hageman TM, Rossiter KM, Barrat CD
abstract: The National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer, developed by the American College of Surgeons Commission on Cancer, was established to standardize and improve the quality of rectal cancer care. While prior research has focused primarily on clinical outcomes, limited evidence exists on how National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer accreditation affects patient volume and geographical reach in a community hospital setting. This project evaluates the impact of National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer accreditation on rectal cancer patient volume and the geographic distribution of patients seeking care. Retrospective observational study conducted from July 2016 through December 2024 at a single community-based hospital. Monthly and annual rectal cancer patient volumes and patient zip codes were collected and analyzed to determine changes over time. The average monthly rectal cancer patient volume increased from 1.0 patient per month preaccreditation to 4.58 patients per month postaccreditation. However, the segmented Poisson regression did not yield a statistically significant change across all periods. The geographic catchment area expanded from 22 zip codes to 79 zip codes after accreditation. Average patient distance traveled increased by 6 miles, but the change did not reach statistical significance. National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer accreditation was associated with an increase in patient volume and a broader geographic scope of patients seeking care at a community hospital; however, this change cannot be disentangled from the hiring of 2 fellowship-trained colorectal surgeons. Accreditation may serve as a signal to patients and referring providers of high-quality, disease-specific care, potentially enhancing the institution's competitive standing and patient draw in the health care marketplace.
cn_title: 直肠癌国家认证项目对社区医院患者量与地理覆盖的影响
insight: 认证与社区医院直肠癌患者量及就诊半径扩大相关，但混杂于专科医师招聘，提示认证可作为质量信号影响转诊格局。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性观察研究，样本量小且无统计学显著性，仅提示认证的潜在信号价值，不足以改变实践。

title: Prediction residuals in spatial transcriptomics reveal microenvironmental heterogeneity in cancer.
authors: Iesmantas T
abstract: Predictive models, as applied in computational pathology, are typically evaluated by accuracy, while their residuals are discarded as errors. In this paper we show that these residuals contain structured biological information. We introduce and validate a conditional discordance framework that uses foundation model prediction residuals to identify tissue regions where morphology and transcriptome diverge. The framework, applied to Xenium spatial transcriptomics data from 18 breast carcinoma sections across 2 cohorts, revealed spatially organized prediction errors with biological associations that varied across patients. In discovery, discordant regions showed higher EPCAM/KRT19 expression and lower expression of several stromal/macrophage markers, while cell mixture associations differed between patients. In two sections of P07, discordant regions enriched in tumor cells showed greater underprediction of transcription associated with EMT after composition adjustment, without a robust increase in observed program expression. Gene predictability is associated with spatial autocorrelation. Observed expression directions agreed across cohorts for 71 of 90 bridge genes; validation pathway profiles were more similar within patients, although the permutation test allowed only nine assignments (p=1/9). Application to four colorectal specimens supported broader use of the framework. The framework shows that prediction residuals carry biological information about microenvironmental heterogeneity, without identifying a universal EMT state.
cn_title: 空间转录组预测残差揭示肿瘤微环境异质性
insight: 该研究提出条件不一致框架，利用预测残差识别形态与转录组背离区域，揭示微环境异质性，为肠癌肝转移空间生物学提供新分析工具。
grade_rationale: 方法学创新但样本量小（18例乳腺癌+4例结直肠），无外部验证，尚不足以改变临床实践。

title: FBB-HFNet: Foreground-background-boundary aware hierarchical fusion network for polyp segmentation.
authors: Shen P, Liu M, He S
journal: Computerized Medical Imaging and Graphics : the Official Journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
abstract: Accurate polyp segmentation is a critical step in the early diagnosis of colorectal cancer. Existing methods commonly suffer from two limitations: insufficient exploitation of intra-layer channel subspaces, and the inability to explicitly handle highly ambiguous boundary pixels under reverse-attention paradigms. To address these issues, we propose FBB-HFNet, a hierarchical feature fusion network that integrates a grouped channel attention enhancement block (GCAEB) and a foreground-background-boundary attention block (FBBAB). The GCAEB partitions encoder features into parallel subspaces and applies independent channel attention to capture complementary channel-subspace cues. The FBBAB explicitly decomposes the predicted probability map into three confidence maps, corresponding to foreground, background, and boundary confusion, from which a deterministic estimator constructs a prototype for each region, and then adaptively aggregates context through a learnable regional prototype attention, effectively alleviating foreground-background confusion near polyp contours. Extensive experiments on five public benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed method achieves competitive or superior performance against current state-of-the-art methods.
cn_title: FBB-HFNet：前景-背景-边界感知分层融合网络用于息肉分割
insight: 提出一种新型息肉分割深度学习网络，通过显式建模前景-背景-边界混淆提升分割精度，为结直肠癌早期诊断的计算机辅助系统提供更可靠的技术基础。
grade_rationale: 方法学论文，在五个公开基准上验证性能，但尚未进入临床验证阶段，实践改变潜力有限。

title: Immunosenescence in colorectal cancer: Interplay of microbiota, inflammaging, and metabolic reprogramming.
authors: Wu D, Zhang P, Zeng C
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major cause of cancer-associated morbidity and mortality worldwide, with significantly higher incidence and lethality in elderly individuals. Growing evidence implicates immunosenescence, the age-dependent functional decline of the immune system, as a key contributor to CRC initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. In this review, telomere attrition, impaired DNA repair, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, and epigenetic remodeling are discussed as interconnected molecular processes that contribute to immunosenescence. These processes disrupt immune homeostasis and promote chronic inflammation. Moreover, functional alterations in macrophages, natural killer cells, neutrophils, and T lymphocytes further enable immune evasion and immunosuppressive niche formation. Furthermore, the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) orchestrates inflammaging and reprograms the CRC microenvironment via pro-inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and growth factors. Gut-specific factors, including microbiota dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, and microbial metabolites, further accelerate immune aging and tumorigenesis. In addition, metabolic reprogramming interacts bidirectionally with immunosenescence. By integrating molecular, cellular, microbial, and metabolic insights, this review offers a comprehensive understanding of immunosenescence in CRC.
cn_title: 结直肠癌免疫衰老：微生物群、炎性衰老与代谢重编程的交互作用
insight: 系统阐述免疫衰老通过SASP、菌群失调和代谢重编程驱动结直肠癌进展，提示靶向衰老微环境可能成为老年肠癌及肝转移的新策略。
grade_rationale: 综述整合多维度机制但无原始数据，不直接改变临床实践，但为免疫衰老靶向干预提供理论框架。

title: Development and preclinical characterization of an MMAE-conjugated anti-EpCAM antibody-drug conjugate for colorectal cancer.
authors: Ko HL, Nguyen QNS, Baek SE, Kim DB, Park YH, Kim SH, et al.
abstract: The epithelial cell adhesion molecule (EpCAM) is frequently overexpressed in colorectal cancer (CRC) and thus represents an attractive therapeutic target. However, the clinical efficacy of EpCAM-targeting antibodies has been limited by suboptimal binding properties and reliance on immune effector mechanisms. Here, we describe the development and characterization of anti-EpCAM #126, a fully human monoclonal antibody isolated from the OPAL phage-display library, and its corresponding antibody-drug conjugate (ADC). Anti-EpCAM #126 exhibited substantially higher binding affinity than adecatumumab, primarily owing to a markedly lower dissociation rate. High-density peptide microarray analysis and alanine-scanning mutagenesis identified NGSKLGRRAK (residues 74-83) within the EpCAM extracellular domain as the dominant epitope, with S76, R81, and K83 serving as key contact residues. Binding was conformation-dependent and markedly decreased following trypsin-mediated proteolytic cleavage of the epitope region. Anti-EpCAM #126 demonstrated robust staining of CRC xenograft and patient-derived tumor tissues and exhibited low cytokine release in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and mouse models. Following the confirmation of efficient receptor-mediated internalization, anti-EpCAM #126 was conjugated to monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) through a protease-cleavable valine-alanine linker, generating an ADC with a controlled average drug-to-antibody ratio of 4.31 while retaining nanomolar EpCAM-binding affinity. The resulting ADC exhibited potent cytotoxicity against EpCAM-expressing CRC cell lines and achieved 84.96% tumor growth inhibition in a patient-derived xenograft model at 10 mg/kg, whereas the unconjugated antibody showed no antitumor activity. These findings suggest that anti-EpCAM #126-MMAE is a high-affinity, epitope-specific ADC with promising preclinical efficacy against EpCAM-positive CRC.
cn_title: 抗EpCAM抗体偶联MMAE的结直肠癌临床前开发与表征
insight: 开发高亲和力抗EpCAM-MMAE ADC，在CRC模型中显示强效抗肿瘤活性，为EpCAM阳性肠癌（含肝转移）提供新靶向治疗候选。
grade_rationale: 临床前研究，尚未进入临床试验，但为ADC转化提供新候选，暂不改变实践。

title: Preoperative circulating musclin as a candidate biomarker of postoperative skeletal muscle vulnerability in colorectal cancer.
authors: Kim Y, Nam JS, Shin SJ, Kim Y, Kang J, Ahn CW
journal: European Journal of Surgical Oncology : the Journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
abstract: Postoperative skeletal muscle deterioration is associated with impaired recovery and adverse outcomes after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery, but preoperative circulating markers of subsequent muscle loss remain insufficiently defined. We evaluated whether circulating musclin was associated with postoperative skeletal muscle status and longitudinal skeletal muscle index (SMI) change. This retrospective single-center study included 106 adults undergoing CRC surgery, of whom 95 had postoperative computed tomography (CT) data. Postoperative CT was obtained at a median of 198 days (IQR, 151-220; range, 73-685 days) after preoperative CT. CT-derived body composition was quantified at the third lumbar vertebra, and serum musclin and natriuretic peptides (NPs) were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The primary outcome was postoperative SMI; greater than 5% SMI loss, percentage SMI change, and longitudinal musclin change were also evaluated. Higher preoperative musclin was associated with higher postoperative SMI in the fully adjusted model (B = 1.872; 95% CI, 0.765-2.979; p = 0.001). Greater than 5% SMI loss occurred in 27 of 95 patients, and higher preoperative musclin was associated with lower odds of this outcome (OR = 0.529; P = 0.038) and with a more favorable percentage SMI change (B = 3.941; P = 0.004). Absolute musclin change was positively associated with postoperative SMI in the baseline-adjusted analysis (B = 5.067; P < 0.001). Musclin-NP interaction terms were not significant. Preoperative circulating musclin was associated with postoperative skeletal muscle status and longitudinal SMI change after CRC surgery. These findings support further prospective evaluation of musclin as a candidate circulating marker of postoperative skeletal muscle vulnerability.
cn_title: 术前循环musclin作为结直肠癌术后骨骼肌脆弱性候选生物标志物
insight: 术前循环musclin与结直肠癌术后骨骼肌指数及纵向变化相关，提示其可作为术后肌肉流失的候选循环标志物，为肠癌围手术期营养与康复干预提供新思路。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性研究，样本量小（106例），仅提示关联，尚需前瞻性验证，暂不足以改变临床实践。

title: Integrated narrative and cognitive therapy enhances psychological and functional recovery after ultra-low sphincter-preserving surgery for low rectal cancer: A randomized controlled trial with exploratory oncologic outcomes.
authors: Pan S, Wang G
journal: European Journal of Surgical Oncology : the Journal of the European Society of Surgical Oncology and the British Association of Surgical Oncology
abstract: Ultra-low sphincter-preserving surgery (ULSPS) for low rectal cancer often results in persistent bowel and sexual dysfunction alongside significant psychological distress, which may adversely affect recovery and may be associated with longer-term oncologic outcomes. Evidence on integrated psychosocial interventions in this context remains limited. To evaluate whether a structured six-month psychosocial intervention integrating narrative therapy and cognitive behavioral therapy improves psychological and functional recovery after ultra-low sphincter-preserving surgery for low rectal cancer, and to explore its associations with inflammatory markers, postoperative recovery metrics, and exploratory oncologic outcomes. In this single-centre, randomized controlled trial, 172 patients with AJCC stage I-III low rectal cancer undergoing ULSPS were assigned (1:1) to standard ERAS-based care or an integrated six-month psychosocial program combining narrative therapy and Beck cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT). Primary outcomes included depression (BDI-II), anxiety (BAI), bowel function (LARS), and sexual function (IIEF-5, FSFI). Secondary endpoints comprised inflammatory markers, recovery metrics, and exploratory oncologic outcomes, including disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS). Analyses were performed using linear mixed-effects models, Kaplan-Meier methods, and Cox regression with prespecified covariates. The intervention group demonstrated significantly greater reductions in depression and anxiety, with between-group differences exceeding prespecified clinically meaningful change thresholds. Improvements in bowel and sexual function were clinically and statistically significant, accompanied by lower postoperative CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α. Recovery metrics favored the intervention (shorter hospital stay, earlier bowel recovery). In exploratory survival analyses, 2-year disease-free survival was 89.5% versus 74.4% (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.24-0.96), and overall survival was 92.4% versus 79.1% (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.19-0.93). These oncologic findings should be interpreted cautiously because DFS and OS were secondary exploratory outcomes, the number of events was modest, follow-up was relatively short, and the study was conducted at a single centre. An integrated narrative-CBT intervention was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in emotional and functional recovery after ULSPS for low rectal cancer. Favorable DFS and OS estimates were observed as exploratory secondary findings but should be considered hypothesis-generating rather than definitive evidence of oncologic benefit. These findings support further evaluation of structured psychosocial programs as adjuncts to ERAS-based perioperative care pathways.
cn_title: 整合叙事与认知行为治疗促进超低位保肛术后心理与功能康复的随机对照试验
insight: 心理社会干预可改善超低位保肛术后情绪与排便性功能，并初步显示生存获益信号，提示围手术期心理干预值得纳入肠癌综合管理并进一步验证。

title: Single-cell transcriptomic and immune microenvironment analyses reveal a TIMP1-associated OLFM4⁺ tumor epithelial program linked to colorectal cancer progression and immune evasion.
authors: Leng R, Cui X, Wu X, Zhao Y, Sun L, Jin H, et al.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by marked epithelial heterogeneity and dynamic tumor-microenvironment interactions. However, epithelial states associated with progression across the normal-adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely defined. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from normal colorectal mucosa, adenoma, and tumor tissues were analyzed using inferCNV, Monocle, Slingshot, CytoTRACE, CellChat, and SCENIC. An OLFM4⁺ tumor cell risk score (OTRS) was constructed using Cox and LASSO regression, and TIMP1 function was evaluated in vitro. Eight major cell types and nine tumor epithelial subtypes were identified. C3 OLFM4⁺ cells showed elevated transcriptional activity, stemness, metabolic activity, and greater representation in carcinoma than adenoma tissues. Trajectory analyses positioned these cells in an early-to-intermediate transitional state. CellChat predicted prominent fibroblast-C3 OLFM4⁺ interactions, including a putative WNT2B-FZD/LRP axis, while SCENIC identified XBP1, NFIA, PPARG, HDAC2, and UBE2K as subtype-associated regulators. The C3 OLFM4⁺-derived OTRS stratified prognosis; high OTRS was associated with poorer survival, macrophage-enriched infiltration, higher stromal, immune, and TIDE scores, and differential predicted drug sensitivity. TIMP1 knockdown suppressed malignant behaviors in CRC cells. C3 OLFM4⁺ cells represent a stem-like, metabolically active tumor epithelial state associated with CRC progression, fibroblast-derived WNT signaling, immune-evasion-related features, and unfavorable prognosis. The OTRS model may support prognostic and therapeutic assessment, while TIMP1 contributes to malignant CRC cell behavior.
cn_title: 单细胞转录组与免疫微环境分析揭示TIMP1相关OLFM4⁺肿瘤上皮程序促进结直肠癌进展与免疫逃逸
insight: 该研究鉴定出OLFM4⁺肿瘤上皮亚群及其预后评分OTRS，揭示TIMP1在CRC恶性行为中的作用，为肠癌预后分层和免疫逃逸机制研究提供新视角。
grade_rationale: 基于单细胞转录组与生信建模的转化研究，有体外验证但缺乏临床队列外部验证，暂不足以改变实践。

title: A retrospective epidemiological study of screening-derived solid cancer incidence proxy rates in South Korea before and after COVID-19 using Korean National Health Insurance Service data.
authors: Jung H, Jung M
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted cancer screening and diagnostic pathways globally. Aggregate screening-derived indicators require cautious interpretation because they do not represent confirmed cancer registry incidence but might reflect program participation, referral patterns, and denominator composition. To evaluate pre- and post-COVID-19 changes in selected solid cancer screening-derived incidence proxy rates in South Korea, and to estimate model-based proxy rates through 2028. This retrospective ecological longitudinal study analyzed publicly available aggregate annual cancer-screening statistics from the Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) and Korean Statistical Information Service (KOSIS) for six solid cancer programs (stomach, liver, colorectal, breast, cervical, and lung cancer). Annual proxy rates per 100,000 screened or eligible persons were calculated. Pre-COVID (2010-2019) and post-COVID (2020-2024) means were compared using Welch t-tests with Mann-Whitney U sensitivity analyses. Ordinary least-squares (OLS) forecasts were generated for 2025-2028. Interrupted time-series analysis was not feasible owing to an insufficient post-COVID observation window. Post-COVID changes in proxy rates were heterogeneous across selected programs. Breast cancer proxy rates increased by 17.1% (Welch p = 0.002) and liver cancer proxy rates by 83.6% (Welch p = 0.002); the liver cancer increase reflects denominator restriction to a high-risk population rather than a true epidemiological surge. Stomach cancer decreased by 23.3% (Welch p = 0.001), cervical cancer by 56.9% (Welch p = 0.005), and colorectal cancer by 25.8% (Welch p = 0.007). Lung cancer data were available only from 2019 to 2024 (program inception) and were interpreted descriptively. Aggregate South Korean national screening data show pandemic-era temporal associations with heterogeneous changes in selected solid cancer program proxy rates. These findings support an indirect screening-disruption and ascertainment interpretation rather than causal proof of a direct COVID-19 effect on solid cancer incidence.
cn_title: 韩国COVID-19前后筛查来源实体癌发病率替代率回顾性流行病学研究
insight: 疫情期韩国结直肠癌筛查替代率下降25.8%，提示筛查中断与检出延迟，需关注后续肠癌及肝转移负担反弹。
grade_rationale: 基于全国医保聚合数据的生态学研究，样本量大但为间接替代指标、无个体验证，实践改变潜力有限。

title: Guidelines for Colonic Diverticular Disease-2026, Second Edition: Management of Diverticular Bleeding and Acute Diverticulitis.
authors: Ichita C, Nagata N, Aoki T, Ishibashi F, Kishino T, Kessoku T, et al.
abstract: Colonic diverticular disease is becoming increasingly common in Japan, paralleling population aging and changes in lifestyle and medication use. The predominance of right-sided diverticulosis in Asian populations, in contrast to the left-sided predominance in Western populations, influences clinical presentation and management. In Japan, diverticulitis has become a clinically important problem, and diverticular bleeding is currently the most frequent cause of acute lower gastrointestinal bleeding (LGIB). The Japanese Gastroenterological Association updated its clinical guidelines for diverticular bleeding and diverticulitis in 2026. Key domains including epidemiology, diagnostic and therapeutic strategies, and priority clinical and future research questions were addressed. Evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, and recommendations were formulated via a modified Delphi process with external review. These guidelines aim to provide Japanese and Asian evidence-based consensus that complements Western guidelines. Recommendations for acute LGIB and diverticular bleeding are as follows: risk stratification with the Shock Index and Oakland and NOBLADS scores guides triage; pre-colonoscopy contrast-enhanced computed tomography is the widely used diagnostic modality; routine colonoscopy within 24 h is not suggested for all patients; endoscopic band ligation or direct clipping is suggested post-detection of stigmata of recent hemorrhage; and early oral refeeding is suggested. Recommendations for diverticulitis are as follows: post-resolution colonoscopy is suggested to exclude colorectal cancer; outpatient treatment and withholding of antibiotics are suggested in selected uncomplicated cases; and primary anastomosis may be favored over Hartmann's procedure in selected complicated cases.
cn_title: 2026年日本结肠憩室病指南第二版：憩室出血与急性憩室炎的管理
insight: 该指南强调亚洲右半憩室优势及憩室出血为下消化道出血首位病因，其风险分层与抗生素降阶梯策略对肠癌鉴别诊断及肝转移患者合并憩室炎的外科决策有参考价值。

title: Improving Postpolypectomy Surveillance Decisions Using an Automated Analysis of Colonoscopy and Histopathology Reports: 2-Center Validation Study.
authors: Zecevic A, De Martino S, Lee JSC, To V, Bhardwaj V, Sibal R, et al.
abstract: Postpolypectomy surveillance intervals derived from colonoscopy findings and histopathology should be guideline-based, yet these are frequently not adhered to, contributing to under- and oversurveillance. This motivates a more structured and automated approach to improve adherence. We developed and evaluated an automated, implementable, guideline-aligned decision support tool that extracts colorectal polyp features from free-text colonoscopy and histopathology reports and produces auditable surveillance recommendations. We extracted paired colonoscopy and histopathology reports from a National Health Service (NHS) trust and designed a 4-stage prompting pipeline using open-weight large language models to separate multispecimen histopathology reports into individual containers ("pots"), align endoscopic findings with specimens, and normalize each pot into a structured schema. The surveillance intervals were then computed by a deterministic rule engine encoding guideline rules. We evaluated extraction performance on 100 procedures (215 pots), assessed surveillance recommendation performance on a same-site cohort (n=100), and performed external validation on a cohort from a second trust (n=100). A separate retrospective audit compared automated recommendations and observed routine scheduling against a clinician-derived reference based on full electronic health record review in 127 patients. Key extraction fields showed end-to-end accuracy (specimen type=0.995; location=0.981; diagnosis=0.981; excision completeness=0.949), with mean report-level pot comprehensiveness of 0.968 (SD 0.112). Overall surveillance recommendation accuracy was 0.96 (95% CI 0.90-0.98) at Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust (GSTT) and 0.93 (95% CI 0.86-0.97) at Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust (SWB) and showed strong class-level performance (no follow-up This hybrid approach using open-weight large language models for structured extraction and guideline-encoded rules for decision-making can generate accurate, lightweight, and auditable postpolypectomy surveillance recommendations. Such a tool has the potential to improve safety netting and guideline adherence in NHS colonoscopy workflows.
cn_title: 基于大语言模型自动分析结肠镜与病理报告优化息肉切除后监测决策：双中心验证研究
insight: 该研究用开源大模型+规则引擎自动生成指南一致的息肉切除后监测建议，双中心准确率达93%-96%，为肠癌筛查监测流程的标准化与依从性提升提供可落地工具。
grade_rationale: 双中心外部验证、含真实世界审计对照，方法学扎实且具直接流程落地潜力，但非RCT、样本量中等。

title: Whole Genome Sequencing-based tumor-informed circulating tumor DNA monitoring for early detection of recurrence in patients with solid tumors.
authors: George M, Schwartz GS, McHayleh W, Margulis V, Bando H, Yoshino T, et al.
abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) assays can transform patient management by enabling molecular residual disease (MRD) detection, prognosis prediction, and treatment monitoring. Here, we report clinical performance of Signatera™ Genome, a whole genome sequencing (WGS)-based ctDNA assay, in a diverse pan-cancer cohort at landmark and longitudinal settings post-definitive treatment. We performed a retrospective analysis of 386 patients with one of the following cancers: breast, colorectal, non-small cell lung, melanoma, or renal cell carcinoma. Signatera™ Genome assays, designed with high-quality variants selected from the matched tumor and normal WGS data, were used to detect ctDNA in the associated patients' longitudinal plasma samples collected post-operatively. The correlation between ctDNA-based MRD status and systemic, distant recurrence-free survival (systemic DRFS) was assessed using Cox regression analysis. In the pan-cancer cohort, landmark analysis at 3 months post-surgery revealed that patients with MRD-positivity had significantly inferior systemic DRFS compared to ctDNA-negative patients (HR: 23.7, p < 0.0001). Additionally, ∼30% improvement in 24-month systemic DRFS was observed among adjuvant-treated MRD-positive patients, whereas MRD-negative patients derived no clear benefit from adjuvant therapy. In the longitudinal setting, MRD positivity anytime post-definitive treatment surveillance significantly correlated with shorter systemic DRFS compared to serial MRD negativity (HR: 104.7, p < 0.0001). Tumor-specific analyses yielded similar findings. Notably, 62% (72/116) of patients had ctDNA detected in the ultra-sensitive range of < 100 ppm. Our findings underscore the robust clinical performance of the Signatera Genome assay for MRD detection across solid tumors. Its broad applicability and high specificity support its integration into clinical practice and prospective trials.
cn_title: 基于全基因组测序的肿瘤知情循环肿瘤DNA监测用于实体瘤复发早期检测
insight: WGS-based ctDNA MRD检测在泛癌种中显示强预后价值，尤其肠癌亚组，支持其用于术后复发监测和辅助治疗决策，但需前瞻性验证。
grade_rationale: 回顾性设计、泛癌种样本量中等（386例），虽HR显著但缺乏前瞻性验证，暂不足以直接改变实践。

title: Robotic surgery for locally advanced rectal cancer: A decade of outcomes from a tertiary referral centre.
authors: Arora P, Jindal A, Larby L, Martin-Roman L, Buckley L, Imogen H, et al.
abstract: Robotic surgery offers potential advantages for the surgical management of rectal cancer; however, robust data on its use in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) populations are limited. We aimed to evaluate the long-term oncological and perioperative outcomes of robotic surgery in a cohort of patients treated at a single tertiary referral cancer centre. In this retrospective study, 105 consecutive patients who underwent robotic surgery for rectal adenocarcinoma between July 2012 and May 2024 at a specialist UK centre were analysed. Patient demographics, tumour characteristics, perioperative outcomes (margin status, complications and conversion rate) and survival (disease-free survival [DFS] and overall survival [OS]) were assessed. The cohort was predominantly male (68.6%) with a median age of 63 (interquartile range 56-70) years. 89.5% of patients had LARC with 53.3% low rectal tumours and 13.3% requiring pelvic exenteration. Neoadjuvant therapy was used in 88.6%. An R0 resection was achieved in 86.7%. The conversion rate to open surgery was low at 0.9%. Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥ III complications occurred in 13.3%, with no 90-day mortality. After a mean follow-up of 53.7 months, the 5-year OS and DFS were 76% and 65%, respectively. Robotic surgery for LARC in a specialised referral setting is safe and feasible, achieving very low conversion rates and zero perioperative mortality. While the R1 and complication rate reflects the cohort's complexity, it is comparable to benchmarks for advanced pelvic malignancies. These findings endorse the robotic platform for treating challenging rectal cancers within a dedicated multidisciplinary framework.
cn_title: 机器人手术治疗局部晚期直肠癌：单中心十年结局分析
insight: 单中心十年数据证实机器人手术治疗局部晚期直肠癌安全可行，转换率极低且无围手术期死亡，支持其在复杂直肠癌多学科治疗中的应用。
grade_rationale: 回顾性单中心设计，样本量有限（105例），但随访时间长且聚焦局部晚期直肠癌，证据等级中等，尚不足以改变临床实践。

title: Fluorogenic RNA aptamers in cancer: emerging platforms for molecular imaging, biosensing, and precision oncology.
authors: Akbarin MM, Farjami Z, Álvarez HR
abstract: Fluorogenic RNA aptamers have emerged as powerful molecular tools for cancer imaging, biosensing, and biomarker detection due to their high specificity, low background fluorescence, and genetic encodability. These short RNA molecules activate fluorescence upon binding specific fluorogens, enabling real-time visualization of intracellular targets and dynamic molecular processes in living systems. Recent advances in RNA structural engineering, fluorophore optimization, and biosensor integration have significantly expanded the translational applications of fluorogenic aptamers in oncology. This mini-review summarizes the structural principles, fluorescence activation mechanisms, and cancer-related applications of fluorogenic RNA aptamers and related nucleic acid biosensors. Foundational studies describing the architecture of fluorogenic aptamer families, including Spinach, Broccoli, Mango, Pepper, Squash, and Beetroot, are discussed with emphasis on G-quadruplex-mediated fluorogen stabilization and fluorescence enhancement. Furthermore, recent developments in CRISPR/Cas-assisted fluorogenic biosensors, dual-color RNA imaging systems, fluorogenic DNAzymes, and amplification-driven aptamer platforms are highlighted. Direct applications across multiple malignancies, including brain, breast, colorectal, liver, lung, prostate, and skin cancers, demonstrate the growing utility of these technologies for tumor-associated RNA detection, epigenetic biomarker analysis, molecular imaging, and therapeutic monitoring. In addition, advances in fluorescence brightness, structural stability, and multiplex imaging strategies have improved the sensitivity and adaptability of fluorogenic RNA systems for complex biological environments. Despite current limitations related to RNA stability, intracellular delivery, and tissue penetration, fluorogenic RNA aptamers represent highly promising tools for next-generation precision oncology. Continued integration with nanotechnology, live-cell imaging, artificial intelligence, and molecular diagnostics is expected to enhance further their clinical and translational potential in cancer research and personalized medicine.
cn_title: 荧光RNA适配体在癌症中的分子成像与生物传感应用
insight: 系统总结了荧光RNA适配体在肿瘤分子成像与生物标志物检测中的前沿进展，为结直肠癌肝转移的活体分子成像与精准诊疗提供了可转化的新型工具平台。
grade_rationale: 该文为叙述性mini-review，非系统综述/Meta分析，未提供定量证据，但发表于肿瘤学前沿期刊，对技术转化有参考价值。

title: Trans-vaccenic acid reduces HT-29 colorectal cancer cell viability and is associated with changes in apoptosis-, lipid metabolism-, and survival-related gene and candidate miRNA expression.
authors: Ayaz L, Sancar H, Serttas R, Erdogan S
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, necessitating the identification of novel bioactive compounds with therapeutic potential. Trans-vaccenic acid (TVA), a primary ruminant-derived trans fatty acid, possesses diverse biological activities; however, its cellular effects in CRC and its association with miRNA expression and downstream targets remain to be fully characterized. In this study, HT-29 human CRC cells were exposed to increasing concentrations of TVA (0-800 µM). Cell viability was evaluated using the MTT assay, and apoptotic cell populations were quantified using Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry alongside Hoechst 33,342 nuclear staining. The expression levels of apoptosis-, lipid metabolism-, and cell survival-related genes (BAX, CASP3, CASP8, CASP9, MCL1, BCL2, SCD1, and GPR34), as well as candidate miRNAs predicted via miRWalk 2.0, miRDB, and TargetScan, were analyzed by RT-qPCR and ELISA. TVA reduced HT-29 cell viability in a dose-dependent manner, with an IC₅₀ value of 251.13 µM at 24 h. Hoechst staining revealed apoptotic nuclear changes and apoptotic body formation, while Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry confirmed a predominant increase in late apoptotic cells (p < 0.001). At the molecular level, TVA treatment significantly increased the expression of pro-apoptotic markers (BAX, CASP3, CASP8, and CASP9) and reduced anti-apoptotic (MCL1, BCL2), lipid homeostasis/tumor survival (SCD1), and oncogenic survival signaling (GPR34) markers (p < 0.05). Concurrently, TVA administration was associated with increased expression of candidate miRNAs (let-7e-5p, let-7b-5p, miR-519d-3p, miR-582-5p, and miR-381-3p; p < 0.05), accompanied by changes in the expression of their predicted target transcripts. TVA exerts cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic effects in HT-29 cells, accompanied by favorable shifts in lipid metabolism/survival gene expression and candidate miRNA profiles. While these correlative findings support the bioactive potential of TVA in CRC, further studies incorporating multiple cell lines and functional miRNA validation (e.g., mimic/inhibitor transfections) are required to establish direct mechanistic causality.
cn_title: 反式疫苗酸抑制HT-29结直肠癌细胞活力并调控凋亡、脂代谢及生存相关基因与候选miRNA表达
insight: 揭示膳食来源反式疫苗酸在肠癌细胞中诱导凋亡并重塑脂代谢/miRNA网络，为肠癌代谢-表观调控干预提供新线索，但仅为单细胞系体外相关性证据。
grade_rationale: 单细胞系体外研究、仅相关性机制、无功能验证，证据等级低，不具备实践改变潜力。

title: The potential of personalized cancer spheroids in precision therapy.
authors: Chakraborty D, Kundu S, Rawal SK, Mitra AG
abstract: The clinical implementation of precision oncology remains challenged by intratumoral heterogeneity, complex tumor microenvironment interactions, and the limited predictive value of conventional preclinical models. 3D cancer spheroids have emerged as physiologically relevant platforms that closely mimic in vivo tumor architecture, cellular heterogeneity, hypoxic gradients, and treatment resistance mechanisms. This review highlights the growing role of cancer spheroids in drug panel testing and their application in personalized therapeutic decision-making across diverse malignancies, including breast, colorectal, ovarian, lung, head and neck, and brain cancers. Patient-derived spheroids and multicellular co-culture models preserve critical tumor-stroma and tumor-immune interactions, enabling clinically meaningful evaluation of chemotherapeutic agents, targeted therapies, immunotherapies, radiosensitizers, and combination treatment strategies. Drug panels assessed using spheroid platforms encompass platinum-based agents, EGFR and VEGF inhibitors, PARP inhibitors, immune checkpoint inhibitors, kinase inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates, and emerging pathway-directed therapeutics. Accumulating evidence suggests that spheroid-based drug testing has the potential to recapitulate clinically relevant tumor characteristics and treatment responses and may serve as a useful preclinical approach for evaluating drug sensitivity, exploring resistance mechanisms, and assessing biomarker-associated responses within clinically relevant timeframes. Recent advances in high-throughput screening, microfluidic technologies, organ-on-chip systems, automated imaging, and artificial intelligence-driven analytics have further improved the scalability, reproducibility, and translational utility of these models. The review also discusses the current limitations, standardization challenges, and ethical considerations associated with spheroid-based drug testing. Collectively, personalized cancer spheroids represent a promising approach linking experimental oncology with precision medicine research, with potential applications in individualized drug testing and treatment optimization.
cn_title: 个性化癌症球体在精准治疗中的潜力
insight: 系统综述了患者来源3D肿瘤球体作为个性化药敏测试平台在多种实体瘤（含结直肠癌）中的应用潜力，为肠癌精准治疗及肝转移药敏筛选提供了临床前模型新思路。
grade_rationale: 叙述性综述，非系统Meta分析，无原始数据或外部验证，但全面总结了球体模型在精准肿瘤学中的转化价值，对研究设计有参考意义。

title: ITF2357 exerts anti‑tumor activity in colorectal cancer via the miR‑1938/ADAM12 axis.
authors: Wang T, Zhang L, Yakupu Z, Shi X, Maimaiti Y, Salikebai B, et al.
abstract: Histone deacetylase inhibitors (HDACi) have emerged as promising anticancer agents. This study aimed to investigate the antitumor efficacy and molecular mechanism of ITF2357 (Givinostat), a novel HDACi, in colorectal cancer (CRC). In vitro, CT26 cell viability, proliferation, colony formation, and cell cycle distribution were assessed. In vivo, a subcutaneous CT26 tumor model was established in female BALB/c mice to evaluate the antitumor effect of ITF2357. Multi-omics analysis (miRNA-seq, mRNA-seq, ATAC-seq) was performed to identify key regulatory molecules, followed by qRT-PCR, dual-luciferase reporter, and knockdown assays for mechanistic validation. ITF2357 significantly inhibited CT26 cell proliferation and induced G0/G1 phase arrest. In vivo, ITF2357 suppressed tumor growth without affecting body weight or liver and kidney tissues, suggesting no obvious systemic toxicity. Multi-omics analysis revealed that ITF2357 upregulated miR-1938, which directly targeted the 3'-UTR of ADAM12. ADAM12 knockdown phenocopied the anti-proliferative and cell cycle arrest effects of ITF2357. Clinically, high ADAM12 expression correlated with poor prognosis in CRC patients. ITF2357 exerts anti-CRC activity by upregulating miR-1938 to suppress ADAM12, leading to cell cycle arrest. These findings provide new mechanistic insights into the anti-CRC effects of ITF2357 and establish a foundation for exploring its therapeutic potential in CRC.
cn_title: ITF2357通过miR-1938/ADAM12轴抑制结直肠癌增殖

grade_rationale: 属细胞与小鼠模型的临床前机制研究，有多组学验证但无人体数据，暂不足以改变临床实践。

title: Harnessing microvesicles from plantaricin-enhanced stem cells to trigger apoptosis in colon cancer cells.
authors: Yaghoubinezhad AR, Halabian R, Nilchiani LS, Najafi A
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, necessitating the development of selective and cell-free therapeutic strategies. This study evaluated the pro-apoptotic potential of microvesicles (MVs) derived from plantaricin-preconditioned mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) against CRC cells. Human bone marrow-derived MSCs were preconditioned with a sub-IC Plantaricin-preconditioned MVs exhibited a reduced mean diameter (253 nm vs. 618 nm) and higher protein content (1107 vs. 983 µg/mL). These MVs significantly decreased HT-29 cell viability with a lower IC Plantaricin-enhanced MSC-derived MVs promoted an apoptosis-associated response in CRC cells, supporting their potential as a cell-free approach for further investigation in colorectal cancer.
cn_title: 植物乳杆菌素预处理间充质干细胞来源微囊泡诱导结肠癌细胞凋亡
insight: 植物乳杆菌素增强的MSC微囊泡可诱导结肠癌细胞凋亡，为肠癌提供无细胞治疗新策略，但尚处体外阶段，肝转移应用待验证。
grade_rationale: 仅为体外细胞实验，无动物模型或临床数据，距临床实践甚远。

title: Acceptability of a Peer-Led Faith-Based Intervention to Improve Breast, Bowel and Cervical Cancer Screening Uptake Among UK Muslim Women: A Qualitative Evaluation.
authors: Jarrar R, Robb KA, Murphy MK, Sadiq C, Matthews A, Haider F, et al.
journal: Health Expectations : an International Journal of Public Participation in Health Care and Health Policy
abstract: Early cancer detection through screening can improve treatment outcomes. However, screening uptake remains lower among some communities, including Muslim women, which puts them at risk of late diagnosis and poor outcomes. In 2020, we worked with 10 Scottish Muslim women to co-design a peer-led, faith-based and culturally tailored intervention to encourage uptake of breast, bowel and cervical cancer screening. The intervention was delivered twice online and qualitatively evaluated. The study was subsequently funded as a feasibility trial, and the intervention was delivered a further 16 times, both online and face-to-face. This paper reports findings from a qualitative evaluation exploring participants' perspectives on the acceptability and implementation of the intervention. The intervention is a 2-h workshop comprising four components: (1) a peer-led cancer screening discussion, (2) a doctor-led health education session, (3) testimonials from Muslim women, and (4) an Islamic perspective delivered by a female religious scholar. In 2024, women participated in online or in-person workshops in North-East England and Scotland. After each workshop, women were invited to participate in focus groups or interviews to provide feedback on the workshop. Qualitative data collection and analysis were guided by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability. Data were analysed using the Framework Analysis method. A convenience sample of 36 women was recruited. Participants described the workshop's content as comprehensive and providing new information. The workshop's informal atmosphere and use of different delivery methods enhanced information attainment. They appreciated the use of interpreters, who assisted non-English speakers. Bringing a medical and Islamic perspective together was novel to participants and made the workshop more impactful. Participants expressed more positive attitudes towards screening after the intervention. A peer-led, culturally-tailored and faith-based intervention for improving cancer screening uptake for Muslim women was deemed acceptable. However, more work is needed to assess the intervention's effectiveness and impact. The intervention was co-designed with 10 Muslim women. A public involvement group worked with the research team throughout the study; they provided their views on the intervention, recruitment, data collection and interpretation of findings. Some were trained as peer educators to help deliver the intervention. Two members of the community (FH and CS, who are also listed as authors) were also employed on the project as Community Recruitment Leads, facilitating participant recruitment and contributing to all stages of the research as valued members of the research team, ensuring the community's voice was embedded throughout.

title: Hairpin competition amplification driven single-CpG-site resolution DNA methylation analysis.
authors: Zhao G, Li H, Zhang R, Dai Y
journal: Analytical Methods : Advancing Methods and Applications
abstract: DNA methylation is an important epigenetic modification and has been widely used as a biomarker for disease diagnosis, particularly in cancer screening. However, conventional quantitative methylation-specific PCR (qMSP) often lacks single-CpG-site resolution because the methylation states of neighboring CpG sites within primer or probe binding regions can interfere with amplification efficiency. In this work, we report a novel Hairpin Competition qMSP (HC-qMSP) strategy for precise DNA methylation analysis at single-CpG-site resolution. In this method, degenerate bases were introduced at non-target CpG positions within the primer and probe binding regions to eliminate interference from adjacent CpG sites. Meanwhile, a specially designed hairpin primer was introduced so that the extension product forms a hairpin structure that competes with the reverse primer during amplification, enabling selective amplification of methylated templates while suppressing unmethylated sequences. Under optimized conditions, the HC-qMSP assay achieved a discrimination sensitivity down to 0.1%, and showed good linearity across a wide dynamic range. The method was further validated using colorectal cancer tissues and stool samples, successfully distinguishing cancer samples from normal controls. Owing to its simplicity, low cost, and compatibility with conventional real-time PCR platforms, HC-qMSP provides a promising approach for precise DNA methylation analysis and potential clinical diagnostic applications.

title: WIN-MTB-2024002 - WIN International Molecular Tumor Board: A 52-year-old female with unmeasurable Stage IIIc colon cancer.
authors: El-Deiry WS, Hernando-Calvo A, Magidi S, Bresson C, Ikeda S, Abdel-Razeq H, et al.
abstract: Copyright: © 2026 El-Deiry et al. This is an open access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original author and source are credited. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with a complex molecular profile that impacts tumor behavior and treatment response. This case report discusses a 52-year-old female diagnosed with Stage IIIc colon cancer, exhibiting KRAS, TP53, IDH1, and APC mutations, as well as a tumor microenvironment with high PD-L1 expression and elevated VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. Despite surgical resection and adjuvant treatment which included FOLFOX, FOLFIRI with bevacizumab and local radiation, the patient’s disease was difficult to track due to small, non-FDG-avid lymph nodes in the aortocaval region and persistent circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). Following a review by an international Molecular Tumor Board (MTB), maintenance therapy options were discussed, including the personalized combinations of regorafenib, sulindac, and metformin, or fruquintinib, sulindac, and metformin, based on the patient’s molecular alterations. Alternatively, 5-FU with or without bevacizumab was suggested. In the event of relapse, the MTB recommended the combination of regorafenib, sulindac, and metformin, with the addition of trametinib and ivosidenib. The combination of regorafenib, ipilimumab, and nivolumab (RIN) was also considered due to the patient’s high PD-L1 expression. Further clinical trial options, such as pan-RAF inhibitors, NK cell agonists, and TAS-102 with bevacizumab, were also discussed. Additionally, the potential combination of PD-1 and TGFβ inhibitors was explored. This case underscores the critical role of molecular profiling in tailoring personalized treatment strategies for advanced CRC, providing novel avenues for managing recurrent disease, even in the absence of measurable disease.

title: A Decade of QOPI in Spain: From Quality Measurement to Continuous Improvement in Oncology Practice.
authors: García-Foncillas J, Gratal P, Blasco Cordellat A, Burriel C, Jiménez FJ, Alba M, et al.
abstract: We evaluated 10 years of QOPI implementation in Spain to characterize quality performance across successive stages of participation, assess sustainability over time, compare performance with contemporaneous QOPI benchmarks, identify persistent certification gaps, and examine quality performance across repeated certification and reassessment cycles. We conducted a longitudinal descriptive study of QOPI implementation in Spanish oncology practices between 2015 and 2025. Analyses included within-practice changes in QOPI quality measures among certified practices, comparing the last available pre-certification assessment with the first post-certification assessment, including disease-specific measures for breast, colorectal, and lung cancer; descriptive comparisons between first participation and post-certification assessments, benchmarking against the contemporaneous QOPI Aggregate, and findings from external certification and recertification surveys. Within-practice longitudinal analyses among certified practices showed higher post-certification performance in several patient-centered measures, including emotional well-being assessment (75.56% to 85.20%), infertility risk discussion (70.33% to 78.67%), appropriate pain management (83.57% to 89.15%), and pain assessment (83.56% to 89.50%). Certified practices maintained broadly high performance over time, although lower post-certification performance was observed in some chemotherapy and other documentation measures. Benchmarking showed a shift: pain assessment, emotional well-being assessment, appropriate pain management, and infertility counseling moved from below to above the contemporaneous QOPI Aggregate after certification. External surveys identified recurrent opportunities for improvement in treatment verification and patient information and education. A decade of QOPI implementation in Spain was associated with sustained high-quality performance, higher scores in selected patient-centered measures after certification, and the identification of persistent opportunities for improvement. Repeated measurement, benchmarking, certification, and reassessment may support organizational change and continuous quality improvement.

title: Oncologic Outcomes and Adjuvant Chemotherapy Use in Early- Versus Late-Onset Colon Cancer: A Propensity Score-Matched Analysis.
authors: Oh SY, Park IJ, Kim YI, Park EJ, Lee JL, Yoon YS, et al.
journal: Diseases of the Colon and Rectum
abstract: The incidence of early-onset colon cancer is increasing, and younger patients are often treated more intensively on the assumption of worse prognosis. To determine whether early-onset presentation is independently associated with prognosis, and to compare adjuvant chemotherapy use and effect between age groups. Retrospective cohort study with 1:3 propensity score matching and exact matching on stage. A single tertiary referral center. Patients who underwent curative resection for stage I to III colon cancer between 2012 and 2020. Early onset was defined as diagnosis before age 50. Curative resection with or without adjuvant chemotherapy. Recurrence-free survival was the primary outcome; overall survival and adjuvant chemotherapy use and effect were secondary. Of 5,032 patients, 749 (14.9%) had early-onset disease; 656 were matched to 1,968 late-onset patients. Five-year recurrence-free survival did not differ between the groups (88.0 vs 86.1%; p = 0.09), and early onset was not independently associated with recurrence or death after adjustment for tumor factors and adjuvant chemotherapy, both in the matched (adjusted hazard ratio 0.85; 95% confidence interval 0.66-1.10) and entire cohort (0.79; 0.62-1.00). Among early-onset patients, recurrence-free survival was independently associated with T4 classification, nodal category, and poor differentiation. Nonetheless, early-onset patients received adjuvant chemotherapy more often (60.2 vs 53.5%; p = 0.003), including in low-risk Stage II disease (37.7 vs 14.3%; p < 0.001). Retrospective single-center design with potential residual confounding; few early-onset patients did not receive chemotherapy. Early-onset presentation was not significantly associated with recurrence-free survival after multivariable adjustment in the matched cohort. Early-onset patients nonetheless received adjuvant chemotherapy more frequently and more intensively, including in low-risk Stage II disease. The observational design and the small number of untreated early-onset patients limit conclusions regarding age-specific chemotherapy benefit. See Video Abstract.

journal: Tidsskrift for Den Norske Laegeforening : Tidsskrift for Praktisk Medicin, Ny Raekke
abstract: Condylomas are usually benign lesions associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) infection, but extensive disease can cause substantial morbidity. Immunosuppression can contribute to disease progression. A man presented with a two-year history of extensive condylomas involving the anal and perianal regions, penis, groin, suprapubic region, tongue and neck. Medical evaluation had been delayed due to health anxiety. Surgical treatment comprised excision of all lesions, split-thickness skin grafting, circumcision and a diverting colostomy. Histopathological examination revealed high-grade dysplasia, carcinoma in situ and squamous cell carcinoma in penile and anal lesions. HPV genotyping showed the highest viral titres for HPV types 82 and 6. Most countries offer HPV vaccines that provide protection against oncogenic HPV types as well as those associated with condylomas. In Norway, the HPV vaccine primarily targets the most common oncogenic HPV types. This case illustrates the potential severity of condylomas and the stigma and health burden associated with the condition. It also highlights possible limitations of current HPV vaccination practice in Norway.

title: Asynchronous Recovery of Body Composition After Curative Surgery for Gastric and Colorectal Cancer: A Prospective Longitudinal Study.
authors: Kang JY, Kim SH, Shin DI, Kim MJ, Jeong WK, Baek SK, et al.
abstract: Postoperative recovery of body composition in patients with gastric cancer (GC) and colorectal cancer (CRC) is a complex and dynamic process. However, longitudinal recovery patterns across multiple physiological domains remain incompletely characterized. This study aimed to describe longitudinal changes in body composition over 12 months after curative surgery in patients with GC and CRC. This prospective longitudinal study evaluated serial changes in body composition parameters, including body weight, skeletal muscle index (SMI), phase angle (PhA), and the extracellular water to total body water ratio (ECW/TBW), from the preoperative period to 12 months after curative surgery in 138 patients, comprising 61 patients with GC and 77 patients with CRC. Distinct and time-dependent recovery patterns were observed across body composition domains. Body weight and SMI gradually declined after surgery, reaching their lowest levels at approximately 3 months postoperatively, followed by partial recovery at 6 and 12 months; however, complete restoration to preoperative values was not achieved in several subgroups. In contrast, PhA declined abruptly on postoperative day 1, while ECW/TBW peaked at the same time point, representing the most prominent early postoperative changes in these parameters. Descriptive subgroup patterns suggested less complete recovery of SMI, PhA, and ECW/TBW among elderly, low skeletal muscle mass, advanced-stage, and chemotherapy-treated patients. Patients with low skeletal muscle mass showed persistently lower SMI values, whereas advanced-stage and chemotherapy-treated patients appeared to show slower normalization of PhA and ECW/TBW. Postoperative changes in body composition appeared to occur asynchronously across multiple physiological domains in patients with gastric and colorectal cancer. Several clinically vulnerable subgroups, including older patients, patients with low skeletal muscle mass or advanced-stage disease, and patients who received chemotherapy, showed descriptive patterns suggestive of less complete recovery. Serial body composition assessment over an extended follow-up period may help characterize postoperative changes and provide a basis for future hypothesis-driven studies.

title: FCVGAN: A Novel Generative Framework Integrating Fuzzy C-Means Clustering with Conditional VAE-GAN for Polyp Segmentation.
authors: Marzoug N, Akhloufi MA
abstract: Early detection of colorectal cancer is of paramount importance. Polyp segmentation using deep learning models can play an important role in this process; however, these models require large annotated datasets that are difficult to obtain in medical imaging. In this work, we propose FCVGAN (Fuzzy C-Means Conditional Variational Autoencoder Generative Adversarial Network), a mask-conditional generative framework that combines Fuzzy C-Means clustering, a Conditional VAE, and a SPADE-based GAN with a multi-scale discriminator. We evaluate two augmentation strategies across four polyp datasets: per-dataset training and transfer learning from Kvasir-SEG. The segmentation experiments repeated across five independent seeds show that transfer augmentation is the strategy that achieved the highest mean Dice score on three of the four datasets, while per-dataset augmentation performed best on Kvasir-Sessile. Compared with the corresponding baselines, transfer augmentation improved the mean Dice score by 2.4%, 0.8%, 16.0%, and 6.2% on Kvasir-SEG, CVC-ClinicDB, Kvasir-Sessile, and ETIS-Larib, respectively. The statistical analysis also showed large effect sizes for transfer augmentation over the baseline across all datasets. When performing the generation quality analysis, per-dataset training achieved a better average FID. However, the images generated with transfer learning showed lower similarity to the training data, which suggests that visual fidelity alone is not a complete indicator of augmentation effectiveness. The ablation study across the five configurations also showed that the contribution of the FCVGAN components depends on the dataset, with the full FCVGAN model providing the most balanced performance across the evaluated datasets. Overall, FCVGAN provides an effective framework for synthetic polyp augmentation, while transfer learning offers a practical strategy for supporting multiple target datasets using a single trained generator.

title: Targeting the Microbiota-Metabolism-Immunity Axis: Active Components of Traditional Chinese Medicine in Colitis-Associated Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Chen Q, Zhang H, Fu L, Liu F, Yang Q, Zhang G, et al.
abstract: Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) develops in the setting of long-standing intestinal inflammation and remains a major complication of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Although effective control of inflammation may reduce cancer risk, approaches that specifically prevent the progression from chronic colitis to neoplasia remain limited. Disruption of the gut microbiota-metabolism-immunity axis is increasingly implicated in this process, as microbial dysbiosis and altered metabolite production can compromise epithelial barrier integrity, sustain inflammatory signaling, and disturb mucosal immune homeostasis. This review examines how active components derived from traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), particularly flavonoids, alkaloids, saponins, and polysaccharides, influence this interconnected network in CAC-related models. Rather than treating these constituents as a single group, we compare the mechanistic patterns and evidence base associated with each class. Flavonoids and alkaloids have been studied mainly in relation to inflammatory signaling and epithelial barrier protection, whereas saponins are more often linked to regulation of the immune microenvironment. Polysaccharides have been studied most frequently in relation to microbiota remodeling, short-chain fatty acid production, and mucosal immune balance. These distinctions are not absolute, and substantial overlap exists across component classes. Moreover, most evidence is derived from animal or cell-based studies, with marked variation in experimental models, compound characterizations, dosing, and outcome assessments. The microbiota-metabolism-immunity axis provides a coherent framework for interpreting the multi-level actions of TCM-derived components, but their causal mechanisms and clinical relevance to human CAC require further validation.

title: CWH43 Suppresses Ferroptosis-Associated Vulnerability Through Redox Adaptation in Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Tsai KY, Wei PL, Lee CC, Batzorig U, Huang CY, Chang YJ
abstract: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death that has emerged as a potential vulnerability in cancer cells under therapeutic stress. However, the mechanisms by which colorectal cancer cells modulate ferroptosis susceptibility remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated the role of CWH43, a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchor biogenesis-related protein whose role in chemotherapy response has been unclear, in regulating redox balance and ferroptosis-associated vulnerability in colorectal cancer. Integrative analyses of clinical datasets, transcriptomic profiling, and functional experiments were performed using gain- and loss-of-function approaches in CRC cell models. We found that elevated CWH43 expression was associated with adverse clinical outcomes and reduced responsiveness to chemotherapy. Functionally, CWH43 attenuated ferroptosis-associated vulnerability by reducing intracellular reactive oxygen species and lipid peroxidation. Mechanistically, CWH43 promoted redox-adaptive programs involving activation of NRF2-dependent antioxidant signaling, upregulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, increased intracellular glutathione availability, and suppression of lipid peroxidation. Genetic or pharmacological disruption of SLC7A11 restored ferroptosis susceptibility and sensitized CWH43-overexpressing colorectal cancer cells to therapeutic stress, whereas ferrostatin-1 partially restored cell viability following erastin-containing treatments. Collectively, these findings identify CWH43 as a regulator of redox adaptation that modulates ferroptosis-associated vulnerability in colorectal cancer, providing insights into stress-adaptive survival mechanisms and chemotherapy resistance in cancer cells.

title: SLC35D1 Is Associated with Colorectal Cancer Progression, EMT-Related Phenotypes, and Immune Infiltration.
authors: Chang YJ, Tsai KY, Zumbi CN, Lee CC, Prince GMSH, Batzorig U, et al.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common malignancies worldwide, and the prognosis of patients with metastatic disease remains poor. Solute carrier proteins participate in diverse cellular processes, yet the biological and clinical relevance of the SLC35D family in CRC remains largely unexplored. This study systematically investigated the expression patterns and clinical significance of SLC35D family members and further evaluated the functional role of SLC35D1 in CRC. Bioinformatic analyses using TCGA and other publicly available datasets and analytical platforms were performed to evaluate the expression patterns and clinical significance of SLC35D family members in CRC. Associations of SLC35D1 expression with patient survival, immune cell infiltration, immune checkpoint markers, and cancer-related transcriptional programs were examined. Loss- and gain-of-function experiments in CRC cells were performed to assess the effects of SLC35D1 on cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT-related phenotypes. SLC35D1 expression was significantly decreased in CRC tissues, SLC35D2 showed a nonsignificant downward trend, and SLC35D3 was significantly increased. Lower SLC35D1 expression was associated with poorer clinical outcomes in the TCGA cohort, although this prognostic association was not reproduced in the independent GSE39582 cohort. Bioinformatic analyses further revealed associations between SLC35D1 expression and immune cell infiltration, immune checkpoint markers, and several cancer-related transcriptional programs. Although the association between SLC35D1 and the EMT-related signature was modest, pathway-enrichment analyses suggested a potential relationship with EMT-related processes. Consistent with these observations, loss- and gain-of-function studies showed that SLC35D1 expression was associated with changes in CRC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT-related molecular phenotypes. Our findings identify SLC35D1 as an understudied SLC35D family member associated with CRC progression and clinical outcome. Functional studies showed that modulation of SLC35D1 expression was associated with changes in malignant phenotypes in CRC cells, whereas its relationships with EMT-related programs and the tumor immune microenvironment warrant further mechanistic investigation. These findings suggest that SLC35D1 may have prognostic relevance in CRC, although its prognostic value requires further validation in independent clinical cohorts.

title: Capsaicin Induces G2/M Cell-Cycle Arrest and Impairs Autophagy in Caco-2 Cells: An Exploratory Study.
authors: Sudan H, Passaponti S, Romagnoli R, Cresti L, Gentile M, Frosini M, et al.
abstract: Capsaicin, the principal bioactive compound of chilli peppers, has emerged as a promising natural molecule with anticancer potential in several malignancies, including colorectal cancer. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects in colorectal cancer cells remain incompletely understood. In the present study, we investigated the effects of capsaicin on Caco-2 human colorectal adenocarcinoma cells, focusing on cell viability, proliferation, migration, cell-cycle regulation, and autophagy. Capsaicin (50-200 µM) reduced cell viability in a dose- and time-dependent manner and significantly inhibited proliferation and migratory capacity. Capsaicin induced G2/M cell-cycle arrest, accompanied by increased p21 expression and reduced p53 phosphorylation. Notably, capsaicin-induced cytotoxicity was not associated with activation of caspase-dependent apoptosis and was instead associated with marked accumulation of autophagic structures and increased LC3B-II/LAMP-1 co-localization. Chloroquine co-treatment failed to further increase LC3B-II or p62 accumulation, indicating that autophagic degradation was already impaired. Although lysosomal abundance remained unchanged, capsaicin significantly reduced mature cathepsin-D protein, demonstrating compromised lysosomal degradative capacity and defective autophagic flux. In addition, capsaicin upregulated occludin expression, suggesting enhanced tight-junction integrity and reduced migratory potential. Collectively, these findings, at least explorative, demonstrate that capsaicin reduces Caco-2 cell viability and induces G2/M cell-cycle arrest, accompanied by p21 upregulation and impaired lysosomal degradative capacity, highlighting disruption of the autophagy-lysosomal pathway as a potential mechanism underlying its anticancer activity in Caco-2 cells.

title: Recent Advances in Small-Molecule-Based Nanovectors for the Treatment of Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Kibungu CW, Mongalo NI, Makhafola TJ
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden, while conventional systemic therapies are limited by toxicity, drug resistance, suboptimal tumour exposure, and pharmacokinetic constraints. Recent advances in nanotechnology have produced diverse nanosystems including liposomes, dendrimers, polymeric nanoparticles, metallic nanoparticles, mesoporous silica systems, and other hybrid platforms that can improve drug solubility, stability, biodistribution, controlled release, and tumour-directed delivery. Plant-derived small molecules provide an additional source of structurally diverse anticancer candidates, but their clinical development is often constrained by poor aqueous solubility, rapid metabolism, limited bioavailability, and non-specific toxicity. This review critically examines recent progress in nanoscale delivery systems for CRC and evaluates their potential for delivering plant-derived and other bioactive small molecules. Particular emphasis is placed on passive and active targeting, physicochemical determinants of delivery, platform-specific advantages and limitations, preclinical evidence, and the barriers to clinical translation. The review also highlights the distinction between plant-derived and fungal-derived natural products and identifies opportunities for integrating natural products with responsive and ligand-functionalized nanocarriers.

title: Exploratory Analysis of the Effects of Thymoquinone Alone and in Combination with 5-Fluorouracil on Inflammatory Mediators in Colorectal Cancer Cells: An In Vitro and In Silico Study.
authors: Kurowska N, Madej M, Książek M, Strzałka-Mrozik B
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide. Chronic inflammation plays a pivotal role in CRC development and progression, with cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and interleukin-8 (IL-8) representing key mediators of tumor-promoting inflammation. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of thymoquinone (TQ), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), and their combination on the expression of COX-2, IL-6, and IL-8 at both the mRNA and protein levels in colorectal cancer cell lines (SW1116 and RKO) and normal colon epithelial cells (CCD-841CoN). Although numerical changes in inflammation-associated mediator expression were observed following TQ monotherapy, none of the TQ-monotherapy comparisons versus the untreated control reached statistical significance after correction for multiple comparisons. Notably, combined TQ/5-FU treatment significantly reduced COX-2 protein levels in SW1116 cells compared with the untreated control. Differences between transcript and protein responses were observed across the investigated cell lines and treatment conditions. However, since both endpoints were assessed at a single time point, the mechanisms underlying these differences cannot be conclusively determined from the present data. Exploratory molecular docking analysis was additionally performed to examine potential direct interactions of TQ with COX-2, IL-6, and IL-8. The predicted docking scores ranged from -5.1 to -6.6 kcal/mol, with the most favorable predicted interaction observed for COX-2. These computational findings are hypothesis-generating and should be interpreted independently of the experimentally observed changes in target expression. Collectively, the present findings demonstrate treatment- and cell-line-dependent response patterns in inflammation-associated mediators, while providing no statistically significant evidence of an effect of TQ monotherapy versus the untreated control under the present experimental conditions.

abstract: Drug repurposing offers an efficient strategy to identify novel anticancer agents from marketed compounds. We screened a library of ~1400 approved drugs using a PPARE-PPAR-α luciferase reporter assay to uncover modulators of lipid metabolism that induce cancer cell death without direct binding to PPARα. This primary screen identified 224 compounds inhibiting reporter activity by >50%, of which 26 demonstrated ≥50% cytotoxicity in KAIMRC1 breast cancer and HCT116 colorectal cancer cells at 10 µM after 48 h incubation. AI-based DrTarget analysis classified these hits, with Group 1 comprising four previously unrecognized anticancer agents: antibiotics cefditoren pivoxil, tebipenem pivoxil, broxyquinoline, and cosmetic ingredient 1-hexadecanol. title: Differences in Somatic Mutations Between Early-Onset and Late-Onset Colorectal Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC, diagnosed <50 years) is increasing globally and presents with advanced clinicopathological features, yet its mutational landscape compared to late-onset CRC (LOCRC) remains poorly defined. We systematically searched PubMed and Embase (January 2016-December 2025) for studies comparing somatic mutations between EOCRC and LOCRC. Two reviewers independently screened 1880 records; 43 studies met inclusion criteria. Two public datasets (TCGA, China PanCancer) were also included. Meta-analyses were conducted using random-effects models with Review Manager. Subgroup analysis was restricted to microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors. Meta-regression evaluated study-level differences in tumor sidedness and stage distribution as sources of heterogeneity. The primary outcome was odds ratios (OR) for mutations in 10 driver genes. title: Second Primary Malignancies in Gastrointestinal Cancer Survivors: Epidemiology, Risk Factors, and Future Prediction Models.
authors: Yadav J, Balizzakiwa T, Goyal H
abstract: Advances in gastrointestinal (GI) cancer care have produced a growing population of long-term survivors at risk of second primary malignancies (SPMs). SPM definitions vary across studies, and SPMs remain underrepresented in cancer forecasting and prediction tools for GI cancer survivors. We conducted a narrative review across major GI cancer subtypes, summarizing site-specific SPM risk, key etiological pathways, and available prediction tools. Approximately one in ten colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors develops an SPM at ten years (pooled SIR ~1.15), a figure specific to CRC that does not generalize to other GI sites. Gastric cancer survivors carry excess risk of thyroid (O/E 2.00), esophageal, small intestinal, and pancreatic (O/E 1.60) malignancy, amplified by radiotherapy. Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma survivors show markedly elevated risk of upper aerodigestive tract tumors, consistent with field cancerization. Lynch syndrome (~16% second CRC risk at 10 years) and familial adenomatous polyposis (near-100% lifetime CRC risk without colectomy) confer some of the highest lifetime risks of metachronous GI malignancy reported to date. Most forecasting frameworks treat cancer incidence as a single event and do not adequately capture survivor-specific transitions, competing mortality, or germline susceptibility. GI cancer survivors form a distinct group whose risk is often overlooked. Harmonizing SPM definitions, extending multistate and competing-risk modeling, and integrating hereditary-risk stratification are near-term priorities for individualized surveillance.

title: Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma in Adults: Age-Stratified Stage Distribution, Clinical Outcomes, and Exploratory Tumor-Normal Genomics.
authors: Xu H, Zhang H, Li W, Zheng S, Song X, Wang J, et al.
abstract: Nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (NA) is generally benign, but recurrent disease and rare malignant transformation remain clinically relevant beyond adolescence. We examined adult clinical presentations, records of malignant transformation, and age-related differences in stage distribution. We retrospectively reviewed 289 surgically treated patients from January 2006 through June 2026. Radkowski stage distributions were compared between patients aged > 30 and ≤30 years using exact tests. Detailed clinical records were reviewed for 16 adults, and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) annotation summaries were examined for one tumor-blood pair. Twenty-five patients (8.7%) were older than 30 years; stage was available for 287 patients. In the detailed adult subgroup, a prior pathology-slide record described focal malignant transformation with a Ki-67 index of approximately 50% in one recurrent tumor. Two other patients had database transformation entries without accompanying pathological documentation. Four recurrences and three deaths were recorded, all in stage IIIB disease. Three men had colorectal or rectal cancer histories. Low-, intermediate-, and advanced-stage tumors accounted for 36.0%, 36.0%, and 28.0% of adult cases, compared with 17.6%, 57.3%, and 25.2% of younger cases ( Adult NA included recurrent stage IIIB disease and a documented record of focal malignant transformation. Stage distributions differed between age groups. These clinical observations support pathological reassessment of recurrent tumors. The single-case genomic findings remain descriptive annotations.

title: Preoperative CT Nodal Staging Versus Pathology in Colon Cancer: A Retrospective Multicentre Diagnostic Accuracy Study.
authors: Cwaliński T, Jagielski M, Kazanowski M, Piątkowski J, Ciesielski M, Januszkiewicz M, et al.
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) informs preoperative staging in colon cancer, yet its diagnostic accuracy for lymph node involvement relative to pathological staging remains uncertain. We examined nodal concordance and multicentre variation in Poland. This retrospective diagnostic accuracy study included adults who underwent upfront resection for nonmetastatic colon cancer at five centres between January 2022 and August 2025. All underwent preoperative CT; recorded cN categories were dichotomised as cN0 versus cN+ (any positive cN category), and pathological pN was the reference. We estimated accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, and kappa with 95% confidence intervals. A centre-adjusted exploratory analysis examined the association between cT3-4 and occult pN+ among cN0 patients. Of 662 otherwise eligible patients, 590 had evaluable cN and pN. CT and pathology agreed in 386 (65.4%; 95% CI, 61.5-69.2; κ = 0.276; 95% CI, 0.199-0.353). Occult pN+ occurred in 73 of 335 cN0 patients (21.8%; 95% CI, 17.7-26.5); 131 of 255 cN+ patients were pN0 (51.4%; 95% CI, 45.3-57.4). Sensitivity was 62.9% and specificity 66.7%. Centre-level cN/pN completeness ranged from 73.5% to 100%. cT3-4 was associated with occult pN+ after centre adjustment (OR, 3.10; 95% CI, 1.71-5.62). Sensitivity analyses were materially consistent. Routine CT nodal classification showed limited concordance with pathology. The cT3-4 association is exploratory and does not establish a prediction or treatment selection rule; cN alone should not determine treatment.

title: From Bile Dysmetabolism to Lipid-Metabolic Remodeling of the Distal Colon: A Vectorial Concept of Colorectal Carcinogenesis (Part I).
authors: Sukhanova MA, Akulov ZA, Berikkhanov ZGM, Shestakov AL, Kotelnikov AG, Nikolaev AM, et al.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is traditionally viewed as the result of the sequential accumulation of molecular alterations and the clonal expansion of transformed cells. However, the state of morphologically non-neoplastic mucosa preceding the development of neoplasia remains considerably less well characterized. This narrative review aims to integrate evidence on biliary and lipid metabolism, intestinal transit, microbial metabolism, and field cancerization and to formulate a testable model of early metabolic remodeling in the distal colon. We propose that a chronically altered biliary-metabolic environment, combined with prolonged luminal and mucosa-associated exposure, may promote lipid-metabolic remodeling of morphologically non-neoplastic mucosa. This state is considered not as a new disease entity but as a potential tissue phenotype capable of altering the barrier, metabolic, and regenerative properties of the epithelium. Subsequent exposure to nitrogen-containing products of microbial metabolism may sustain repeated cycles of injury and regeneration, thereby creating conditions for clonal selection. Following the emergence of a neoplastic clone, the same local environment may potentially assume a different biological role and become part of a metabolic niche that supports further clonal expansion. The proposed model extends the concept of field cancerization by incorporating a metabolic dimension and generates a series of spatial and temporal predictions amenable to experimental and prospective clinical testing. Validation of this model may provide a basis for investigating morphologically non-neoplastic mucosa as potential tissue at risk and for developing earlier preventive and diagnostic approaches.
