cn_title: BHLHE40作为转录变阻器：解码微环境信号调控肿瘤可塑性
insight: 系统梳理BHLHE40在微环境信号整合中的双向调控作用，提示其可作为结直肠癌进展与治疗抵抗的潜在靶点，但肝转移特异性证据仍待补充。
grade_rationale: 叙述性综述整合泛癌与机制证据，无原始数据或外部验证，尚不足以直接改变临床实践。

title: Colorectal neoplasia detected during colonoscopic surveillance in Li-Fraumeni syndrome: a retrospective case series.
authors: Takagi A, Tajika M, Hori M, Ito N, Tanaka T, Hosoda W, et al.
abstract: Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS), caused by germline pathogenic variants in TP53, predisposes affected individuals to multiple early-onset malignancies. Although the risk of colorectal cancer (CRC) is increasingly recognized, evidence regarding colonoscopic surveillance remains limited. We present a series of seven genetically confirmed patients with LFS who underwent colonoscopic surveillance at our institution. All patients were women with a history of multiple primary malignancies. Adenomas were identified at the initial colonoscopy in two patients. Among the remaining five patients with negative baseline examinations, four subsequently had colorectal neoplastic lesions detected within 2-3 years. Overall, colorectal neoplasia was detected in five patients, including three advanced adenomas and one CRC diagnosed at 32 years of age. A serrated lesion was observed in one patient. The median age at first detection of colorectal neoplasia was 32.5 years. This case series demonstrates that colorectal neoplasia may be detected at a young age in patients with LFS, including within a relatively short interval after a negative colonoscopic examination. These findings underscore the importance of careful and regular colonoscopic surveillance in this high-risk population.
cn_title: Li-Fraumeni综合征结肠镜监测中检出结直肠肿瘤的回顾性病例系列
insight: LFS患者在32岁左右即可检出进展期腺瘤或肠癌，且阴性筛查后2-3年内可现新病灶，提示需对TP53胚系突变者提前并加密结肠镜监测。
grade_rationale: 单中心7例回顾性病例系列，样本极小且无对照，仅能提出监测假说，不足以改变指南。

title: Resistance Phenotypes and Treatment Sequencing After Immune Checkpoint Blockade in MSI-H/dMMR Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: A Review.
authors: Sagawa T, Hirakawa M, Nagashima H, Fujikawa K
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair-deficient metastatic colorectal cancer, but clinically relevant progression still occurs and treatment after progression remains undefined. We performed a clinically oriented narrative review, updated August 8, 2026, and separated direct prospective evidence, retrospective post-ICI evidence, extrapolation from general metastatic colorectal cancer trials, case-level evidence, and biological rationale. In the absence of prospective post-dual-ICI sequencing studies, we propose an evidence-informed conceptual framework. Apparent early progression should prompt confirmation of MSI/MMR status and exclusion of pseudoprogression before classification as early global progression, late systemic progression, or oligoprogression. BRAF V600E is common in MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer and is not an absolute predictor of ICI failure, but it is a major treatment-defining branch after progression. Repeat tissue biopsy or circulating tumor DNA profiling should be selective, used when findings can alter management and without delaying urgent therapy. ctDNA-based molecular residual disease is prognostic after curative-intent colorectal cancer resection, including metastasectomy, but is not validated to direct treatment of radiographically evident post-ICI progression. Oligoprogression warrants multidisciplinary consideration of local therapy, while ICI rechallenge remains investigational. Most recommendations are retrospective or extrapolated; transparent evidence boundaries and prospective post-dual-ICI studies are essential.
cn_title: MSI-H/dMMR转移性结直肠癌免疫检查点抑制剂治疗后的耐药表型与治疗序贯：综述
insight: 系统梳理MSI-H/dMMR mCRC免疫治疗后进展的耐药表型与序贯策略，提出以确认MSI状态、排除假性进展及BRAF分支为核心的框架，并指出亟需前瞻性研究。
grade_rationale: 叙述性综述，整合回顾性及间接证据提出概念框架，缺乏前瞻性验证，暂不足以直接改变实践。

title: Colitis-associated colorectal carcinogenesis: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential.
authors: Lu Y, Wang X, Yin C, Wang J, Guo S, Wang Z, et al.
abstract: Chronic colitis is a major risk factor for colorectal cancer (CRC), particularly for colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC), where persistent inflammation drives the transition from mucosal injury to malignant transformation. Accumulating evidence indicates that gut microbiota dysbiosis, epithelial barrier disruption, microbial translocation, chronic immune activation, and aberrant inflammatory signaling collectively contribute to CAC initiation and progression. Sustained inflammation promotes oxidative stress, DNA damage, genetic/epigenetic alterations, and tumor microenvironment remodeling, ultimately facilitating tumor development and immune evasion. These processes form an interconnected pathogenic network linking microbial, inflammatory, genetic, immune, and stromal alterations. This review comprehensively summarizes the key drivers and molecular mechanisms of CAC, covering microbiota and barrier dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress and DNA damage, genetic and epigenetic alterations, and tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune dysregulation. We further review recent advances in diagnostic biomarkers, disease monitoring, chemoprevention, targeted therapies, and emerging interventions, including the potential utility of specific chemokine axes as biomarkers and therapeutic targets. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational challenges of linking mechanistic insights to diagnostic and therapeutic advances, including biomarker validation, stage-specific interventions, and patient stratification across disease progression. By integrating these interconnected mechanisms and therapeutic strategies, this review provides a comprehensive framework for understanding CAC pathogenesis and identifies opportunities for precision prevention, early detection, and multimodal treatment.
cn_title: 结肠炎相关结直肠癌发生：分子机制与治疗潜力
insight: 系统梳理炎症驱动肠癌的多层次分子网络，为CAC精准预防、早期诊断及靶向干预提供整合框架，对炎症相关肠癌及转移机制研究有借鉴意义。
grade_rationale: 发表于综述性期刊的叙述性综述，整合机制与转化进展但无原始数据，不直接改变临床实践。

title: The multifaceted role of 3-methyladenine in cancer therapy.
authors: Laila UE, Wang B, Mumtaz M, Gulshad K, Niaz M, Qureshi MM, et al.
abstract: 3-Methyladenine (3-MA), an early autophagy inhibitor, blocks autophagosome formation mainly by inhibiting class III phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) vacuolar protein sorting 34, while its concurrent inhibition of class I PI3K can produce opposing effects on autophagic flux depending on nutrient status. This Review examines the context-dependent roles of 3-MA across cancer types. When autophagy serves a pro-survival function, 3-MA-mediated inhibition tends to attenuate this protective response, thereby potentiating the cytotoxicity of chemotherapeutics, targeted drugs, and natural compounds, and helping to overcome acquired resistance. However, in some settings-such as colorectal cancer without therapeutic pressure-autophagy suppression may instead promote epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis. The pharmacokinetic shortcomings and off-target effects of 3-MA have motivated the design of nanocarriers for tumor-specific co-delivery, aiming to improve bioavailability and avoid paradoxical autophagy induction. Ultimately, the lasting contribution of 3-MA may be its utility as a mechanistic probe that uncovers key autophagy regulatory nodes, paving the way for next-generation selective modulators and biomarker-driven strategies.
cn_title: 3-甲基腺嘌呤在癌症治疗中的多面作用
insight: 3-MA作为自噬抑制剂在结直肠癌中可能促进EMT和转移，提示自噬抑制策略需考虑肿瘤阶段和治疗压力，为肝转移研究提供新视角。
grade_rationale: 综述性文章，非原始研究，但系统总结3-MA的上下文依赖作用，对自噬相关研究有参考价值，未直接改变临床实践。

title: Histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses do not indicate timing of prophylactic hysterectomy: a retrospective analysis of endometrial biopsies in Lynch syndrome carriers.
authors: van Leeuwen L, Eikenboom EL, Groenendijk FH, van Leerdam ME, Spaander MCW, van Doorn HC, et al.
abstract: Women with Lynch syndrome are at increased risk of endometrial cancer. Gynecological surveillance is advised, but also prophylactic hysterectomy is an option. This study aimed to gain more insight in tumorigenesis in Lynch carriers to be able to personalize prophylactic hysterectomy timing. To this aim endometrial cancer surveillance in Lynch syndrome carriers was assessed using data from the Dutch Lynch syndrome database linked to the Dutch National Pathology Databank (PALGA). Eligible participants were Lynch syndrome carriers under surveillance, who underwent hysterectomy and had ≥ 1 endometrial biopsy within five years prior to surgery. Pathology reports, describing the histopathological features of the samples, were collected and, if available, samples were revised by a specialized pathologist. Additionally loss of expression of ARID1A, PTEN, PAX2, and mismatch repair (MMR) proteins was studied. Pathology reports from 32 Lynch syndrome carriers were analyzed: 16 had normal endometrium at hysterectomy, five had hyperplasia without atypia, six had endometrial intra-epithelial neoplasia (EIN), and five had endometrial cancer. Prior to hysterectomy, hyperplasia with or without atypia or endometrial cancer was reported in 3% of biopsies in the histopathological normal group, 26% in endometrial hyperplasia without atypia group, 26% in the EIN group, and 36% in the endometrial cancer group. Upon revision, combined neoplastic development of tissue and loss of protein expression were observed in 12% of the normal group, 36% of endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, 36% of EIN, and 50% of endometrial cancer group. So, increasing tissue disorganization and loss of protein expression appeared to correlate with progression to (pre)malignancy. However, no specific marker or consistent pattern emerged that could guide clinical decisions on prophylactic hysterectomy for individual patients. These findings highlight the complexity of endometrial cancer development in Lynch syndrome and underscore the need for further research to improve surveillance strategies and optimize timing of prophylactic surgery.
cn_title: Lynch综合征携带者子宫内膜活检的组织病理与免疫组化无法指导预防性子宫切除时机
insight: 组织学与蛋白表达缺失虽随病变进展加重，但无一致标志物可个体化指导Lynch综合征预防性子宫切除时机，提示需多组学与更大样本研究。
grade_rationale: 回顾性小样本（32例）探索性研究，无外部验证，未提供可操作决策标志物，不足以改变临床实践。

title: Comorbidity patterns and their associations with performance status and treatment receipt in breast and colorectal cancers in a multiethnic Asian setting: a latent class analysis.
authors: Hoo YY, Ng HS, Danaee M, Koczwara B, Ramalingam S, Subramaniam S, et al.
journal: Supportive Care in Cancer : Official Journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer
abstract: Comorbidity is usually summarised as a count or index, which treats different combinations of conditions equally. Whether distinct comorbidity patterns have different implications for management decisions in cancer is unclear. We applied latent class analysis (LCA) to identify comorbidity patterns and examined their associations with performance status and cancer treatment in individuals with breast or colorectal cancer. Data from two Malaysian cohorts comprising adults with breast or colorectal cancer were analysed. Comorbidities, verified against medical records, were grouped into 20 categories. LCA was used to identify comorbidity patterns. Outcomes included ECOG performance status (0-1 vs ≥ 2) and receipt of treatment (surgery, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, anti-HER2, CDK4/6 inhibitors, hormone therapy). Among 1117 individuals, 695 (62.2%) had ≥ 1 comorbidity. Hypertension, dyslipidaemia, diabetes and obesity were most prevalent. LCA identified three classes: low (n = 723), cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) (n = 368) and multisystem (n = 26). All in the multisystem group and half in the CKM group had modified Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3. The CKM group was older than the low-comorbidity group (62 vs 51 years) but did not differ in performance or treatment status. The multisystem group however had poorer performance status (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 4.04, 95%CI = 1.50-10.84), lower odds of receiving chemotherapy (aOR = 0.10, 95%CI = 0.04-0.25) and anti-HER2 therapy (aOR = 0.14, 95%CI = 0.02-0.86). Comorbidity patterns revealed differences that counts alone would have missed. The CKM class had similar performance status and treatment receipt to the low-comorbidity class despite cardiovascular and renal comorbidity, highlighting risks not reflected by performance status. The multisystem class requires validation.
cn_title: 多族裔亚洲乳腺癌与结直肠癌患者的共病模式及其与体能状态和治疗接受度的关联：潜在类别分析
insight: 共病模式比单纯计数更能揭示治疗差异：多系统共病者体能差、化疗和抗HER2治疗接受度低，提示肠癌合并多病需个体化评估。
grade_rationale: 基于两个马来西亚队列的潜在类别分析，样本量中等、回顾性设计且多系统类仅26例需验证，尚不足以改变实践。

title: FOLFOX-Associated Ventricular Fibrillation Arrest in a Patient With Colon Cancer.
authors: Al Osta S, Ahmed M, Xu WD, Jalaly N
abstract: Fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity is uncommon but may cause life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias. A 43-year-old man with stage IIIB colon cancer developed chest discomfort and out-of-hospital ventricular fibrillation arrest approximately 72 hours after his first folinic acid (leucovorin), fluorouracil (5-FU), and oxaliplatin (FOLFOX) cycle. Electrocardiography showed anterior ST-segment elevations, but coronary angiography demonstrated nonobstructive left and right coronary arteries. Echocardiography showed a left ventricular ejection fraction of 25% to 30%, which improved to approximately 50% on cardiac magnetic resonance imaging without myocardial edema or late gadolinium enhancement. FOLFOX was discontinued, guideline-directed medical therapy was initiated, and an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was placed for secondary prevention. This case highlights a rare, severe presentation of fluoropyrimidine cardiotoxicity after the first treatment cycle despite no prior cardiac history. Ventricular fibrillation may occur early during FOLFOX therapy. Prompt recognition and multidisciplinary cardio-oncology management are essential.
cn_title: FOLFOX治疗相关室颤心脏骤停一例
insight: 报道FOLFOX首次周期后罕见致死性室颤，提示肠癌化疗需早期心脏监测与多学科心脏肿瘤管理。

title: Burden of hospitalizations in four adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer survivor populations in the United States, 2006-2020.
authors: Wernli KJ, Haupt EC, Smitherman AB, Osuji T, Shen E, Chawla N, et al.
journal: Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention : a Publication of the American Association for Cancer Research, Cosponsored By the American Society of Preventive Oncology
abstract: We describe hospitalization rates in adolescent and young adult (AYA) cancer survivors 2-5 years (Y2-Y5) from diagnosis. Observational study of AYA cancer survivors diagnosed 2006-2020 was conducted in two healthcare systems [Kaiser Permanente Southern California (n=7889) and Northern California (n=7338)] and two states [California (47,302) and Utah (n=7935)]. Hospitalizations were ascertained from electronic health records and statewide administrative records and stratified by whether pregnancy-related. Hospitalization rates were calculated by cohort. We estimated patient factors associated with hospitalizations using a Poisson model. Most AYA survivors were women (~64% of all cohorts), mean age ~31 years at diagnosis, and non-Hispanic white (range 35.1-81.2%) or Hispanic (range 14.3-40.6%). Overall, 21-24% of AYA survivors experienced >1 hospitalization. Unadjusted hospitalization rates declined from Y2 [range 155.1-243.4 per 1000 person-years (PY)] to Y5 (range 105.8-132.0 PY) (p-trend<0.0001 in all cohorts). Factors associated with increased non-pregnancy related hospitalizations were [range of relative risks (RR)]: non-Hispanic Black race/ethnicity (RR 1.46-1.66 vs non-Hispanic white); public insurance (RR 1.57-1.93 vs commercial/military); receipt of chemotherapy (RR 1.51-1.81), and cancer type-breast (RR 1.69-1.97), cervical (RR 2.30-3.31), colorectal (2.76-3.66), acute lymphoblastic leukemia (RR 2.89-5.19), acute myeloid leukemia (2.11-5.05), and sarcoma (RR 2.70-4.96) (vs thyroid). While hospitalizations decline as time from diagnosis elapses across health system settings and states, nearly 1 in 5 AYA cancer survivors experience hospitalization in early survivorship. Hospitalization rates remain elevated in some AYA patient subgroups in early survivorship, highlighting the need to identify AYAs at risk to mitigate unanticipated hospitalizations and costs.

title: A Novel Quantitative Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading System for Predicting Pathological Response Following Neoadjuvant Therapy in Rectal Cancer.
authors: Erkaya M, Sommovilla J, Oruc M, Trunzo JA, Rosen DR, Karahan S, et al.
journal: Diseases of the Colon and Rectum
abstract: While pathological and magnetic resonance imaging-based tumor regression grading systems are widely utilized following neoadjuvant therapy for rectal cancer, existing endoscopic approaches rely on qualitative assessment without quantitative weighting of individual features. Although individual endoscopic features associated with response have been described, no weighted scoring system exists to integrate these features into an objective assessment tool. This lack of a statistically weighted grading framework leads to subjective clinical impressions and significant interobserver variability in documentation and interpretation, limiting standardized patient selection for organ preservation strategies. To develop a quantitative, point-based endoscopic tumor Regression Grading system to standardize post-neoadjuvant therapy endoscopic assessment and predict pathological complete response. Retrospective cohort study. Single tertiary care center. Patients with locally advanced rectal cancer treated with total neoadjuvant therapy and surgical resection between 2018 and 2025 who had complete pre- and post-total neoadjuvant therapy endoscopic documentation were included. Two experienced colorectal surgeons independently evaluated endoscopic images in blinded fashion, scoring predefined endoscopic features. A statistically weighted, point-based scoring algorithm was developed, with quantitative point values assigned proportional to the strength of association with American Joint Committee on Cancer pathological response. The system incorporated mucosal healing features (whitening, telangiectasia, scarring, erythema), adverse features (ulceration, necrosis), mass regression levels, and stricture characteristics, classifying patients into 3 tiers: Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading 1 (complete), Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading 2 (near complete), or Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading 3 (partial/incomplete). Predictive performance of the Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading system for pathological complete response, 3-tier risk stratification, and interobserver reliability, evaluated using diagnostic performance metrics and receiver operating characteristic analysis. Seventy-six patients (mean age 58 ± 12 years; 58% male) were eligible. The 2 endoscopists demonstrated excellent interobserver agreement for the overall response assessment (weighted κ = 0.9) with 88.2% exact agreement. Univariate analysis identified whitening of the mucosa as the strongest predictor of complete response (odds ratio 47), followed by telangiectasia (odds ratio 23), scarring (odds ratio 16), and erythema (odds ratio 16). Ulceration and necrosis were powerful negative predictors (odds ratio 0.03 each). Each incremental level of mass regression (from no regression to < 50% to 50-99% to 100% regression) increased the odds of complete response 9.6-fold (all p < 0.01). The Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading system demonstrated strong discrimination for predicting pathological complete response (area under the curve 0.85, 95% confidence interval 0.76-0.93) with a sensitivity of 83.3%, specificity of 76.1%, and accuracy of 78.9%. The Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading 1 category identified patients with 69.4% pathological complete response probability, while Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading was associated with 85.7% probability of pathological partial or incomplete response. Retrospective single-center pilot study requiring external validation. The Endoscopic Tumor Regression Grading system is the first statistically weighted, point-based scoring algorithm for endoscopic response assessment following neoadjuvant therapy. By quantitatively integrating multiple concurrent endoscopic features weighted by their predictive strength, this system addresses the limitations of qualitative grading, provides objective 3-tier risk stratification, and facilitates standardized patient selection for organ preservation strategies. See Video Abstract.

title: ctDNA retesting to guide anti-EGFR therapy in later-line metastatic colorectal cancer.
authors: Mešinová S, Streško M, Šebest L, Repiská V, Danišovič Ľ, Lohajová Behulová R
abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) represents a promising tool for dynamic molecular profiling in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), enabling monitoring of clonal tumor evolution and the detection of mechanisms of acquired resistance during treatment. The relevance of ctDNA has increased, particularly in the context of anti-EGFR therapy, where the emergence of RAS gene mutations constitutes a key resistance mechanism. The aim of this study was to evaluate the clinical utility of reassessing mutational status using ctDNA prior to rechallenge with anti-EGFR therapy in later treatment lines in patients with mCRC. A total of 17 patients with confirmed RAS and BRAF wild-type status in tumor tissue before initiation of first-line therapy were included in the analysis. All patients received anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody-based therapy in the first line and subsequently underwent ctDNA analysis from peripheral blood prior to initiation of third-line treatment using the Idylla™ qPCR platform. RAS gene mutations were detected in ctDNA in 4 patients, while 13 patients retained a wild-type status. Patients without detectable mutations achieved longer progression-free survival in the third-line setting compared with patients harboring RAS mutations. Overall survival from the start of third-line therapy was also prolonged in the wild-type ctDNA group. These findings suggest that the absence of resistant RAS clones in ctDNA may predict greater clinical benefit from anti-EGFR rechallenge. Liquid biopsy-based retesting may therefore represent an important tool for treatment individualization in later lines of mCRC therapy. This study also illustrates the translational potential of ctDNA analysis, linking dynamic molecular characterization of tumor evolution with clinically relevant treatment decision-making and the implementation of personalized oncology approaches.

title: Short-Term Outcomes of Transanal Total Mesorectal Excision for Rectal Cancer: A Multicenter Propensity Score-Matched Analysis Comparing Patients With and Without Preoperative Neoadjuvant Therapy.
authors: Shima T, Hamamoto H, Matsuda T, Takemasa I, Tanaka K, Mukai T, et al.
abstract: To evaluate the association between preoperative neoadjuvant therapy and short-term outcomes of transanal total mesorectal excision for rectal cancer. We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent transanal total mesorectal excision at 26 Japanese institutions between 2012 and 2019. Patients who received neoadjuvant therapy were matched 1:1 with patients who did not. Perioperative, postoperative, and pathological outcomes were compared. After matching, 294 patients (147 per group) were analyzed. Operative time was longer in the neoadjuvant therapy group than in the non-neoadjuvant therapy group (median, 510.0 vs. 382.0 min), with an adjusted mean difference of 129.25 min (95% CI, 87.90-170.59; Neoadjuvant therapy was associated with longer operative time during transanal total mesorectal excision, whereas no statistically significant association with severe postoperative morbidity was detected. Sensitivity analyses likewise did not identify a statistically significant association, supporting the technical feasibility of transanal total mesorectal excision after neoadjuvant therapy in experienced centers.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Hypofractionated Radiotherapy Combined with Immunotherapy for Liver Metastases: A Single-Center Retrospective Analysis.
authors: Qin L, Wei Y, Tao L, Jiang H, Qian D, Geng Q, et al.
abstract: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-dose hypofractionated radiotherapy (LDHRT) for liver metastases when combined with immunotherapy. Patients with liver metastases receiving immunotherapy were enrolled in this study at Changzhou Second People's Hospital from January 2019 to May 2025 (Ethics Approval No. [2021]KY117-01). LDHRT (12 Gy in 3 fractions) was administered to the liver metastases using volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). The tumor response was evaluated according to the RECIST 1.1 standard. Clinical and imaging data were collected to assess changes in tumors inside and outside the radiation field before and after LDHRT, as well as the median progression-free survival (PFS) for lesions within the radiation field. A total of 51 patients were included, with the median age of 69 (range 47-84) years; 86.3% (44/51) were male, and 94.1% (48/51) had an ECOG performance status (PS) score ≥1. Additionally, 54.9% (28/51) had received ≥3 lines of prior therapy. Due to the continuous progression of liver metastases under systemic treatment, LDHRT was administered for the liver metastases. The study found a high local control rate within the radiation field as the objective response rate (ORR) and disease control rate (DCR) within the radiation field were 17.6% and 86.3%, respectively. However, the efficacy for lesions outside the radiation field was significantly inferior, with an ORR of 0% and a DCR of 35.3%. The median PFS for lesions within the radiation field was 4.23 months. Patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) showed better PFS than those with gastric cancer liver metastases (GCLM). The most common adverse events were fatigue (16/51, 31.4%), abnormal liver function (11/51, 21.6%), and hypothyroidism (7/51, 13.7%). No patients discontinued treatment due to treatment-related adverse events. LDHRT combined with immunotherapy provided favorable local control and was generally well tolerated in patients with liver metastases. No apparent abscopal effect was observed, suggesting that single-lesion LDHRT was insufficient to reverse systemic immunosuppression.

title: Association between use of non-aspirin non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and detection of colorectal polyps and cancer in a screening setting.
authors: Nafisi S, Randel KR, Hoff G, Schult AL, Botteri E
abstract: While substantial evidence supports a protective effect of aspirin against colorectal polyps and cancer, the evidence for non-aspirin non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NA-NSAIDs) remains limited. We studied the association between the use of NA-NSAIDs and the detection of colorectal polyps and cancer among screening participants. We selected participants in the Bowel Cancer Screening trial in Norway-a randomized trial comparing once-only sigmoidoscopy and the biennial faecal immunochemical test (FIT). Using multivariable logistic regression, we estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the association between NA-NSAID use in the 4 years before the screening invitation and detection of colorectal cancer (CRC), adenomas, advanced adenomas, and advanced serrated polyps. Long-term use was defined as ≥2 years of use. Of 64,889 participants (24,159 sigmoidoscopy, 40,730 FIT), 35,867 (55.3%) were NA-NSAID users, 314 (0.5%) had CRC, 6,208 (9.6%) had adenomas, and 659 (1.0%) had advanced serrated polyps. NA-NSAID users had lower odds of CRC (OR 0.80; 95% CI 0.64-1.00), adenomas (OR 0.94; 95% CI 0.89-1.00), and advanced adenomas (OR 0.87; 95% CI 0.80-0.95) than those with no NA-NSAID prescription. For non-selective NA-NSAIDs, the results were similar to those for any NA-NSAIDs (CRC: OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.63-0.99; adenomas: OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88-0.99; advanced adenomas: OR 0.87, 95% CI 0.79-0.95). COX2-selective NA-NSAIDs were not associated with CRC or adenomas. Among the long-term NA-NSAIDs users, the ORs were 0.59 (95% CI 0.27-1.26) for CRC, 0.65 (95% CI 0.54-0.79) for adenomas, and 0.59 (95% CI 0.44-0.80) for advanced adenomas. No association was observed between any NA-NSAID use and advanced serrated polyps. The results were consistent across trial arms and sexes. Our findings suggest that use of NA-NSAIDs, in particular non-selective NA-NSAIDs, might be associated with a reduced risk of adenomas and CRC, but not advanced serrated polyps.

title: Harnessing conversational generative artificial intelligence and natural language processing to address the colorectal cancer screening adherence gap: the Azores endeavour.
authors: Goiana-da-Silva F, Tude-Graça D, Correia FPG, Renard R, Pereira J, Portas T, et al.
abstract: Organised colorectal cancer (CRC) screening reduces mortality, yet participation routinely falls short of policy targets, a gap most acute in structurally disadvantaged, insular, and rapidly ageing populations. The Azores, an outermost European Union archipelago, exemplifies this challenge: CRC accounts for 10% of regional cancer diagnoses and is the second leading oncological cause of potential years of life lost, with 2024 mortality (24.9 per 100,000) exceeding mainland Portugal. Despite a mature organised screening programme (ROCCRA), archipelago-wide participation stands at just 30.3%, with roughly one in five residents who consent and receive a home test kit never returning it. This perspective article argues that conversational artificial intelligence based on large language models (LLMs), the current generation of natural language processing (NLP) technology, capable of understanding and responding to patient concerns in real time, represents a promising approach for bridging this gap. Because the barriers identified in the literature are well, inherently dialogic, an interactive, multi-channel conversational cascade is better suited to address cognitive and operational friction than static reminders. Specifically, this paper synthesises presumed drivers of non-adherence, inferred from the literature and considered likely to apply to the Azorean context, reviews the evidence supporting conversational and voice-enabled outreach in cancer screening, and uses regional data to model the potential impact of a well-targeted voice AI deployment. Beyond the Azores, this framework illustrates how NLP-enabled conversational AI could support more responsive, equitable, and scalable public health screening programmes in geographically dispersed and underserved populations.

title: Oncolytic virus VT1092M synergizes with immune checkpoint inhibitors against intraperitoneal metastases of colorectal cancer.
authors: Hu Z, Yuan X, Li S, Liu W, Liu J, Zhou H, et al.
abstract: Intraperitoneal metastasis is a frequent progression in colon cancer, highlighting the critical need for enhanced therapeutic approaches. Oncolytic virus (OV) therapy has emerged as a promising immunotherapeutic strategy. The combination of OVs with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) has demonstrated an enhanced anti-tumor response. We generated the intraperitoneal-subcutaneous bilateral colon cancer xenograft model to simulate intraperitoneal metastatic colon cancer, and evaluated the systemic antitumor efficacy of the oncolytic HSV-1 virus VT1092M in combination with ICIs (anti-PD-L1 antibody and anti-CTLA-4 antibody). Intraperitoneal administration of VT1092M markedly suppressed intraperitoneal cancer progression and enhanced the superior antitumor efficacy of ICIs immunotherapy in murine intraperitoneal metastatic colon cancer. Notably, treatment of VT1092M combined with anti-CTLA-4 antibody could eliminate both intraperitoneal metastases and subcutaneous tumors, while also inhibiting the formation of peritoneal blood vessels and malignant ascites. The synergistic combination of VT1092M and anti-CTLA-4 elicited potent intraperitoneal and systemic antitumor immunity, culminating in durable, tumor-specific memory that significantly prolonged survival in mice with colorectal intraperitoneal metastases compared to either monotherapy. title: Phase angle assessed by bioelectrical impedance analysis in patients with colorectal cancer: a systematic review.
authors: Mei Y, Wang T, Liu S, Wang H, Han Z
abstract: Malnutrition, altered body composition, and sarcopenia are common among patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and are associated with poor treatment tolerance and adverse clinical outcomes. PhA, derived from BIA, reflects cellular membrane integrity and body cell mass and has been increasingly investigated as a potential marker of nutritional status and prognosis in oncology. However, the clinical relevance of PhA in patients with CRC has not yet been systematically synthesized. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched for observational studies published between January 2000 and October 2025 that assessed PhA in adult patients with CRC. Data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment using the AXIS tool were performed independently by two reviewers. Due to substantial heterogeneity in study design, outcome definitions, and PhA cut-off values, a narrative synthesis was conducted. A total of 10 studies involving 1,439 patients were included. Lower PhA values were consistently associated with adverse clinical outcomes. Four studies reported significantly shorter overall or progression-free survival among patients with low PhA. Four studies demonstrated associations between low PhA and unfavorable short-term outcomes, including postoperative complications, prolonged hospital stay, cancer-related complications, and early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Several studies also reported positive associations between PhA and indicators of nutritional status, body composition, muscle mass, muscle strength, and hydration balance. One longitudinal study showed that postoperative increases in PhA were accompanied by improvements in body composition parameters and reduced early chemotherapy-related toxicity. Current evidence indicates that BIA-derived phase angle is associated with nutritional status, body composition, treatment tolerance, and survival outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer. However, heterogeneity in measurement protocols and cut-off values limits direct clinical application. Standardized assessment methods and prospective studies are needed to establish CRC-specific reference values and to determine whether interventions that improve PhA can translate into improved clinical outcomes.

title: Complement C3 is associated with cancer-induced frailty: genetic and clinical evidence.
authors: Zhang C, Zhao T, Li W, Shi Z, Bao Z
abstract: Frailty is a degenerative geriatric syndrome characterized by declining muscle mass and function, unintentional weight loss, and fatigue. It is a key risk factor for many geriatric diseases and poor postoperative outcomes. Currently, pathogenesis remains unclear, and apart from nutritional support and exercise, no pharmacological interventions are available. Notably, the frailty phenotype is also a major feature in patients with advanced-stage cancer, and both frailty and advanced cancer are characterized by dysregulation of nutritional and energy metabolism. Consequently, cancer serves as a novel accelerated model for investigating the mechanisms underlying frailty development. The phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) framework was employed to systematically analyze the causal relationship between 264 cancer types and frailty, and to identify candidate cancer types directly causally associated with frailty. A large-scale analysis was conducted to assess the causal relationship between "candidate cancer- Icelandic peripheral blood proteome-frailty" and to further explore the characteristics and patterns of the key proteins mediating cancer-induced frailty using the two-sample Mendelian randomization method. Finally, the correlation between key candidate proteins and frailty was verified using peripheral blood from a 100-case colorectal cancer (CRC) cohort. The PheWAS analysis identified 21 cancer types with significant causal associations with frailty among the 264 cancers examined. An in-depth analysis of the top 5 cancer types revealed that the mechanisms by which they induce frailty exhibit both prominent shared features and distinct characteristics. Shared signaling pathways included stress responses, immune processes, and metabolic pathways. Among these, immune-related pathways involving complement component C3 (C3), lipocalin-2 (LCN2), and coagulation factor V (F5) emerged as key shared mechanisms across multiple cancer types. Finally, validation in an independent clinical cohort of patients with CRC ( This study systematically elucidated the causal relationships between cancer and frailty, identified multiple candidate proteins that may drive frailty progression, and demonstrated that complement C3 is associated with frailty development. Furthermore, we propose that cancer serves as a novel accelerated model for investigating the mechanisms underlying frailty. These findings provide new insights into the biological mechanisms underlying frailty and identify a series of promising molecular targets for future mechanistic studies and therapeutic interventions.

title: A dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework for exploratory classification of colorectal cancer histopathology and hepatocellular carcinoma clinical records.
authors: Guo X, Lai J, Wu L, Chen D
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain major diagnostic challenges because classification often depends on modality-specific evidence that is stored in separate public datasets. This study evaluates a dual-branch CNN-LSTM framework using two independent and unpaired data sources: colorectal histopathological image patches and structured HCC clinical-biochemical records. The study is therefore positioned as an exploratory investigation of representation learning across heterogeneous medical datasets. The CNN branch extracts spatial and glandular texture features from curated CRC image patches, whereas the LSTM branch treats fixed-order clinical attributes as a structured feature sequence to learn inter-feature dependencies in the HCC records. Under internal public-dataset testing with bootstrap uncertainty estimation, the full CNN + LSTM + MLP framework achieved an accuracy of 0.978 (95% CI, 0.971-0.984), Macro-F1 of 0.977 (95% CI, 0.971-0.984), and Macro OVR AUC of 0.997 (95% CI, 0.996-0.998). Ablation and baseline comparisons showed lower performance for CNN only (accuracy 0.938), LSTM only (0.875), clinical encoder only (0.890), CNN + LSTM (0.966), CNN + clinical MLP (0.958), late fusion (0.952), EfficientNet-B0-style fusion (0.970), ViT-tiny-style fusion (0.960), XGBoost (0.910), random forest (0.900), and logistic regression (0.875). The full model also exceeded the EfficientNet-B0-style baseline in Macro AUC by 0.003 (95% CI, 0.002-0.004; paired bootstrap P = 0.007; McNemar exact P = 0.011). Grad-CAM and SHAP analyses are used to interpret branch-specific decisions, while the findings remain limited to internal public-dataset validation.

title: Early-treatment coagulation activation and radiographic progression during VEGF/VEGFR inhibitor therapy: A multicancer real-world cohort study.
authors: Liu Y, Liu B, Liu S, Zhang T, Lv T, Han S, et al.
abstract: Coagulation activation is common in cancer, but its link to treatment durability is unclear. We investigated whether early-treatment coagulation activation correlated with radiographic progression during vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)/vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR) inhibitor therapy. This single-center, retrospective, multicancer cohort study developed a coagulation activation score (0-2) based on the last available D-dimer (>500 ng/mL) and fibrinogen (>4.0 g/L) measurements taken within 100 days after baseline. Multivariable Cox models calculated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for subsequent radiographic time to progression among patients who were progression-free at the 100-day landmark. Of 1400 eligible patients, 1089 had evaluable early-treatment measurements, and 909 were included in the landmark analysis. Compared to a score of 0, adjusted HRs were 1.29 (95% CI 1.02-1.62) for score 1 and 1.51 (95% CI 1.07-2.12) for score 2. Score 2 also correlated with lower odds of durable clinical benefit (adjusted odds ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.38-0.84), while objective response and best tumor shrinkage did not show a consistent gradient. These associations remained significant in time-dependent and timing-restricted analyses. Exploratory subgroup analyses revealed the strongest association in colorectal cancer patients treated with bevacizumab (score 2 vs. 0: HR 2.23, 95% CI 1.21-4.11); however, no association was observed in lung cancer patients treated with bevacizumab. No significant interaction with documented immune checkpoint inhibitor exposure was detected. The score did not enhance discrimination beyond clinical variables and baseline coagulation markers. Early-treatment coagulation activation was associated with reduced treatment durability during VEGF/VEGFR inhibition. Prospective validation in specific cancer-drug contexts is necessary.

title: Advancing colorectal cancer management through clinical proteomics: from genotype to proteotype toward clinical translation.
authors: Ramachandran P, Chen CSY, Lee CS, Aye TT, Kunjukunju A, Elias MH, et al.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the leading causes of cancer death worldwide, with outcomes depending on the stages at diagnosis. Genomic and transcriptomic classifications are largely inferential because the genotype-phenotype relationship is non-linear and is influenced by post-translational regulation, protein turnover, and the tumor microenvironment (TME). Proteomics measures this functional layer directly. This review surveys proteomic technologies for CRC emphasizing mass spectrometry, affinity- and aptamer- based multiplex platforms, post-translational modification proteomics, spatial proteomics, AI-driven structural and predictive analysis, and multi-omics integration. Each platform is evaluated based on clinical questions, the supporting evidence and the barriers to implementation. Literature was drawn primarily from PubMed/MEDLINE and Scopus (2020-2026), emphasizing advanced and translational applications. Alongside approved blood cfDNA and stool-RNA molecular tests, proteomics is a functional complementary technology that may improve biological interpretation, assay triage and treatment response prediction, although prospective clinical utility remains to be established. The decisive barriers are standardized biospecimens, validation evidence, clinical utility data and interoperable public data sharing. (169 words).

title: Synchronous Bilateral Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma With Multifocal Recurrence and Prolonged Disease Control Under Sequential Multimodal Therapy: A Case Report.
authors: Chacón-Medina OJG, Custodio-Cabello S, Palka-Kotlowska M, Rosero-Rodriguez A, García-Ruíz C, Gallego-Nieto S, et al.
abstract: Synchronous bilateral renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is an uncommon clinical presentation that raises important diagnostic, surgical, and oncological management challenges. Colonic serosal metastases from RCC represent a particularly rare site of spread. We report the case of a 67-year-old man with synchronous bilateral clear cell RCC (ccRCC) who underwent staged nephrectomies in 2022, followed by early multifocal recurrence necessitating completion left nephrectomy, bilateral adrenalectomy, and segmental colectomy for serosal colonic involvement in October 2023. Pathology confirmed metastatic ccRCC at all resected sites. Adjuvant pembrolizumab was initiated post-resection but failed to prevent rapid systemic progression with bone and pulmonary metastases. Following adjuvant immunotherapy failure, the patient received three sequential lines of targeted therapy in the metastatic setting: sunitinib (first line), everolimus (second line), and cabozantinib (third line). Cabozantinib achieved a durable metabolic response, with complete resolution of nodal disease and partial response of bone and pulmonary lesions, despite prior multiline exposure. Treatment was complicated by medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw, requiring temporary discontinuation; cabozantinib was reintroduced at a reduced dose (20 mg/day), which was associated with maintained disease control and acceptable tolerance. At the time of reporting, the patient remained on reduced-dose cabozantinib with chronic hemodialysis and hormonal replacement, maintaining an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status of 0. This case illustrates the biological heterogeneity and unusual metastatic tropism of ccRCC, and underscores the clinical value of individualized multidisciplinary management; combining aggressive metastasectomy, palliative radiotherapy, and sequential targeted systemic therapy, in achieving meaningful long-term disease control while preserving quality of life.

title: Review Article: Socioeconomic and Racial or Ethnic Inequalities Across the Colorectal Cancer Continuum: From Disparities to Action.
authors: Bardou M, Martel M, Barkun AN, Chapelle N
abstract: Socioeconomic and racial or ethnic inequalities affect colorectal cancer (CRC) across the care continuum. Although increasingly documented, whether current interventions effectively reduce these inequalities remains uncertain. To review socioeconomic and racial or ethnic inequalities in CRC incidence, screening and diagnosis, treatment, surveillance and survival and assess interventions designed to reduce them. We conducted a narrative review of adult studies published in English between January 2000 and March 2026. MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, and ISI Web of Knowledge were searched for studies addressing socioeconomic or racial and ethnic disparities in CRC, using a saturation approach. Socioeconomic disadvantage and belonging to some racial or ethnic minority groups were associated with higher CRC incidence within high-income countries, lower screening participation, later diagnosis, less timely or guideline-concordant treatment, poorer surveillance and worse survival. In the USA, five-year survival was 60.6% among Black patients versus 66.7% among White patients, with little improvement in this gap over several decades. Inequalities at successive stages may contribute to cumulative disadvantage. Intervention evidence was markedly uneven across the continuum. Mailed stool-test outreach and patient navigation increased screening among underserved populations, whereas evidence for interventions specifically reducing inequalities in treatment, surveillance, and broader survivorship was sparse. Improving overall CRC prevention and care cannot be assumed to reduce inequalities. The major evidence gap has shifted from documenting disparities towards demonstrating how to reduce them, particularly beyond screening. Equity should become an explicit outcome of CRC research, implementation, healthcare quality assessment and clinical guidelines.

title: RAS pathway mutations orchestrate chromatin reconfiguration and transcriptional rewiring in colorectal cancer.
authors: Gao Z, Kundu S, Xing P, Davila EC, Polavarapu VK, Akcan E, et al.
abstract: RAS pathway mutations occur in ~ 40% of colorectal cancers (CRCs), with KRAS- and BRAF- mutant tumors exhibiting distinct mutational, transcriptional, and epigenetic landscapes. Advances in next-generation sequencing enable integrated analyses of multi-omics data, providing insight into their regulatory relationships. To define the molecular programs driven by RAS pathway mutations, we generated isogenic CRC cell models and profiled chromatin accessibility using ATAC-seq. We performed ATAC-seq in isogenic HCT116 and RKO models. Mutation-associated changes in genes, regulatory elements, and signaling pathways were identified, together with inferred transcription factor (TF) binding activity. Clinical datasets were analyzed to assess whether features identified in the cell models were recapitulated in patient tumors and whether they were associated with clinical outcomes. Isogenic CRC models segregated by RAS pathway mutation status at both epigenetic and transcriptomic levels. Mutation alterations modulated WNT signaling, accompanied by changes in RUNX2 and TCF7L2 expression and binding activity. Comparison between the HCT116 and RKO models identified 85 genes, eight of which displayed reproducible expression patterns across three independent clinical cohorts. TCF7L2 were associated with RAS pathway mutations in patient tumors, with elevated expression level predicting worse overall survival independent of cofactors. We identified RAS pathway mutation-driven regulatory reprogramming with convergent effects on WNT signaling. TCF7L2 emerged as a key TF, with elevated expression in BRAF-mutant tumors independently associated with poor clinical outcomes. These findings highlight a clinically relevant epigenetic mechanism linking RAS pathway mutations to CRC cell survival maintenance.

title: Routine versus postoperative CRP/CT guided selective diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer: a comparative randomized controlled trial.
authors: Moaz AM, Barakat KE, Elshazly W, Zaki Y, Badawy A, Hegazy BK, et al.
abstract: Diverting ileostomy is routinely used to protect the anastomosis after laparoscopic low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer, but it exposes most patients to stoma-related morbidity even though only a minority develop a true anastomotic leak. This trial evaluated whether a postoperative C-reactive protein (CRP) and computed tomography (CT) guided selective ileostomy strategy could reduce the rate of ileostomy formation compared with routine diversion. In this RCT, 200 patients with stage II or III middle or lower third rectal cancer undergoing laparoscopic LAR were randomized 1:1 to a CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy group (n = 100) or a routine diverting ileostomy group (n = 100). In the CRP/CT group, serum CRP was measured daily from postoperative day 1; a threshold of 114 mg/L on day 3 or a rise greater than 15 mg/L per day triggered confirmatory contrast-enhanced CT, with ileostomy formed only if findings were suspicious for leak. The primary outcome was the stoma-free status throughout the 12-month follow-up. Baseline demographic and tumor characteristics were similar between groups (all p > 0.05). Ileostomy formation was markedly lower in the CRP/CT group than the routine group (22.0% vs. 100.0%, p < 0.001). Anastomotic leak rates did not differ (0% vs. 1.0%, p = 1.000), nor did overall complication rates (31.0% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.879). Operative time (148.4 ± 14.0 vs. 166.6 ± 13.1 min, p < 0.001) and intraoperative blood loss (168.9 ± 28.2 vs. 197.3 ± 39.7 mL, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in the CRP/CT group. Stoma-related complications were far less frequent with the selective strategy (3.0% vs. 30.0%, p < 0.001). The CRP/CT group reported significantly better global health status, physical functioning, and emotional functioning scores (all p < 0.001). A postoperative CRP/CT-guided selective ileostomy strategy reduces the need for diverting ileostomy after laparoscopic low anterior resection for rectal cancer while improving operative outcomes and quality of life; however, confirmed leakage was infrequent in both groups. This approach may serve as an alternative to routine diversion in appropriately monitored surgical units. This trial was retrospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07722533) on July 17, 2026.

title: FGFR pathway inhibition enhances PD-1 blockade and modulates antitumor immunity in colorectal cancer models.
authors: Shang Z, Jing C, Liu J, Zhang B, Rúbies Bedós M, Papakyriacou I, et al.
abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) has demonstrated limited efficacy in microsatellite stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC). The fibroblast growth factor receptor (FGFR) signaling pathway contributes to tumor immune evasion, yet its role in CRC remains insufficiently understood. We investigated the immunomodulatory effects of FGFR inhibition in combination with PD-1 blockade in murine CRC models. In vitro co-culture systems were used to evaluate T cell activation upon FGFR3 blockade. RNA sequencing and bioinformatics analyses, including The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) dataset evaluation, were conducted to elucidate molecular mechanisms and clinical relevance. Combined FGFR inhibition and PD-1 blockade significantly reduced T cell exhaustion and promoted macrophage repolarization toward an antitumor phenotype. Transcriptomic profiling revealed upregulation of immune-related pathways and activation of immune-stimulatory genes. In vitro, FGFR3-specific monoclonal antibody treatment enhanced IFNg release following PD-1 blockade. Moreover, analysis of TCGA data demonstrated that high FGFR3 expression correlates with worse prognosis in CRC patients. Our findings suggest that FGFR pathway inhibition may enhance the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade and provide a rationale for further investigation of FGFR-targeted combination strategies in MSS CRC.

title: Proximity of pre-mRNA 3' end processing and transcription termination is associated with enhanced gene expression.
authors: Stępień A, Pulimamidi D, Plens-Gałąska M, Lalonde M, Kopczyńska M, Ostatek K, et al.
abstract: Two key factors required for pre-mRNA 3' end processing, CPSF73 and PCF11, are linked to poor cancer prognosis, yet their oncogenic roles remain unclear due to their dual function in transcription termination. Using a colorectal cancer (CRC) progression model, we show that primary tumor cells depend on high CPSF73 and PCF11 levels, whereas metastatic cells are less sensitive. This dependency is not explained by alternative polyadenylation (APA) or transcription-replication conflicts. Instead, we identify an uncoupling of 3' cleavage and transcription termination during CRC progression. Primary tumor cells exhibit a global shift toward proximal termination alongside distal APA usage, while metastatic cells partially revert to normal termination patterns and favor proximal APA. Notably, the distance between 3' cleavage and termination is nearly halved in primary tumor cells compared with normal cells and becomes particularly short in oncogenes. Reduced cleavage-termination distance correlates with increased gene expression both within and across cell states. These findings identify a previously unrecognized link between transcription termination architecture and gene expression regulation.

title: EAES-SAGES clinical practice guideline update: multi-society recommendations on key controversies in the management of diverticular disease.
authors: Huo B, Al Khaldi M, Shehata D, Calabrese EC, Reinke C, Carrano F, et al.
abstract: We identified areas of controversy in the management of patients with diverticular disease to develop key questions addressing the management of symptomatic uncomplicated diverticular disease (SUDD), uncomplicated diverticulitis, and complicated diverticulitis. We performed a systematic review to identify randomized trials and cohort studies addressing our key questions. Informed by an updated evidence synthesis, an international, multidisciplinary panel of gastrointestinal surgeons, gastroenterologists, patient partners, and methodologists applied the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) evidence-to-decision framework during panel consensus meetings to derive recommendations for the management of patients with diverticular disease. The systematic review identified 27 studies representing very low to moderate certainty evidence. The panel made the following recommendations: 1. In patients with SUDD, we suggest rifaximin or mesalamine over standard supportive care (conditional recommendation); 2. In patients with uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine antibiotics (conditional recommendation); 3. In patients with persistent symptoms following an episode of recurrent uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest elective resection over observation (conditional recommendation); 4. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of uncomplicated diverticulitis, we suggest no routine follow-up colonoscopy (conditional recommendation); 5. In patients who have recovered from a first episode of diverticulitis complicated by an abscess, we suggest elective resection over surveillance (conditional recommendation). The panel judged that a significant proportion of patients would place a high value in reducing the risk of recurrence at 1 year but also acknowledged the lack of evidence addressing prioritized outcomes including 30-day major complications, need for emergency surgery, stoma-free survival at 1 year, and quality of life at 1 year. Given that patient values and preferences may vary, clinicians are encouraged to apply patient-centered decision-making and discuss the alternatives. This clinical practice guideline update provides evidence-informed recommendations to support patients and clinicians in the management of diverticular disease.

title: Efficacy of prophylactic hemoclip placement for preventing delayed post-polypectomy bleeding in nonpedunculated colorectal lesions: updated meta-analysis and trial sequential analysis of randomized controlled trials.
authors: Wei Y, He H, Mabenga HS, Ngowi BJ, Jin Z
abstract: Evidence regarding prophylactic hemoclip (HC) for preventing delayed post-polypectomy bleeding (DPPB) remains inconsistent. This meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA) aimed to evaluate HC after thermal resection of nonpedunculated colorectal polyps. MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 28 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing HC with non-HC after thermal resection of nonpedunculated colorectal polyps ≥ 5 mm. The primary outcome was DPPB. Secondary outcomes included DPPB for proximal large (≥ 20 mm) nonpedunculated colorectal polyps (LNPCPs), other adverse events, and procedure time. Random-effects models, subgroup analyses, GRADE, and TSA were applied. Ten RCTs involving 4,588 patients were included. HC reduced DPPB overall (3.4 vs. 6.5%; RR 0.51; 95% CI 0.34-0.76; P < 0.001; I Prophylactic HC closure reduces DPPB after thermal resection of nonpedunculated colorectal polyps ≥ 5 mm, including proximal LNPCPs. Clinical use should consider lesion characteristics, procedural factors, and individualized bleeding risk.

title: Compartment-specific PPARδ activity controls the outcome of cancer-immune cell competition and immunotherapy efficacy.
authors: Bunk P, Ergin I, Maher T, Shah V, Bonney JR, Kumar LBSS, et al.
abstract: Most patients with solid tumors fail to sustain antitumor immunity, in part because immune cells cannot outcompete cancer cells inside the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we show the lipid-sensing transcription factor PPARδ is a compartment-specific determinant of cancer-immune fitness balance and immunotherapy efficacy. Activating PPARδ in cancer cells promotes their growth and impairs antitumor immunity, whereas activating it in immune cells drives tumor suppression and overrides tumor-promoting effects of cancer-intrinsic activation. title: Decoding spatial mTOR signalling reveals distinct roles in the tumour microenvironment.
authors: Zuhair R, Eastwood M, Bradbury M, Cross A, Hester J, Issa F, et al.
abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprises a variety of cell types that interact with malignant cells, influencing both cancer progression and the patient response to therapy. Given the intricate interactions among these components, assessing how signalling pathways contribute to cancer progression by acting on different components of the TME is particularly complex. Multiplexed imaging allows simultaneous assessment of signalling in multiple of these components. Here, we utilise a highly multiplexed dataset of 61 markers across 746 colorectal tumours to investigate how complex mTOR signalling in different tissue compartments influences patient prognosis. We found that mTOR pathway signalling in immune cells correlates with favourable patient survival. Advanced spatially-aware analysis of signalling activities using graph neural networks revealed that the positive association between immune mTOR signalling and patient survival was more pronounced in tumours with features of a more differentiated morphology. Integrative analysis using TCGA data and spatial transcriptomics confirmed a role for immune mTOR signalling in immune activation, accompanied by reduced TGF-β signalling. Our work highlights the importance of adopting a personalised approach to targeting mTOR in cancer patients and establishes a framework for studying cell type-specific signalling in the TME.
cn_title: 解码空间mTOR信号揭示肿瘤微环境中不同细胞类型的作用
insight: 免疫细胞mTOR信号与结直肠癌良好预后相关，且受肿瘤分化形态影响，提示靶向mTOR需考虑细胞类型特异性。
grade_rationale: 基于大规模多重成像和空间转录组学的观察性研究，虽未直接改变实践，但为mTOR靶向策略提供重要启示。

title: Prevalence and clinical characteristics of colorectal adenocarcinoma in young adults in Mexico: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Arriaga-Izabal D, Morales-Lazcano F, Angulo-Zamudio UA, Canizalez-Román A, León-Sicairos N
abstract: The prevalence of colorectal cancer in young adults is increasing worldwide but there is limited data from Latin American countries. In Mexico, the burden and clinical profile of colorectal adenocarcinoma in young patients are not well characterized. Our study aimed to estimate the prevalence of colorectal adenocarcinoma and describe its clinical characteristics, in young adult patients in Mexico. The PubMed and Web of Science databases were systematically searched from database inception to September 2024. The prevalence of colorectal adenocarcinoma in young adults in Mexico was evaluated, comparing the clinical characteristics of early-onset and late-onset cases. A pooled meta-analysis was carried out, using random effects models. Heterogeneity was assessed through the I² statistic, meta-regression, and subgroup analyses. The risk of bias was evaluated using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Studies Reporting Prevalence Data. The pooled prevalence of colorectal adenocarcinoma in young adults was 10% (95% CI 6-15 %) in patients ≤40 years of age and 19% (95% CI 18-21 %) in those under 50 years of age. Meta-regression indicated a growing trend in the under 40 age group over time and the predominating clinical factors were male sex (52%), rectal involvement (44%), stage IV disease at diagnosis (32%), and a greater number of poorly differentiated tumors. Colorectal adenocarcinoma in young adults is an emerging public health concern in Mexico that requires specific strategies targeting prevention and early detection.
cn_title: 墨西哥年轻成人结直肠腺癌患病率及临床特征的系统综述与Meta分析
insight: 墨西哥年轻成人结直肠腺癌患病率高达10%（≤40岁）和19%（<50岁），且晚期和低分化比例高，提示需针对年轻人群加强预防和早期筛查。
grade_rationale: 基于系统综述/Meta分析，但为区域性流行病学数据，对全球实践改变潜力有限。

title: Navigating technical variations and outcomes in indocyanine green-guided lymph node mapping for colorectal cancer.
authors: Saeidishahri S, Wagner L, Emile SH, Wexner SD
abstract: Indocyanine green is a fluorescent dye used in a wide range of specialties, including colorectal surgery. Although indocyanine green fluorescence imaging has been well established for assessing colorectal anastomotic perfusion, its role in lymph node mapping in colorectal cancer remains unclear. This narrative review aimed to provide an overview of the mechanism of action of indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging and its role in lymph node mapping in colorectal cancer. PubMed/MEDLINE was searched through July 2026 for studies evaluating the use of indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging for lymphatic mapping and lymph node identification in colorectal cancer. Findings were narratively summarized. Indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging may improve visualization of lymphatic drainage and support a more complete lymphadenectomy. Meta-analyses have reported pooled lymph node detection rates of 91% and 86.8%, with substantial variation by tumor location, disease stage, and mapping technique, with generally lower detection rates in rectal than in colon cancer. Pooled sensitivities of 63%, 64.3%, and 71% were reported, corresponding to false-negative rates of 37%, 35.7%, and 29%, respectively. Although indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging was associated with an increased lymph node harvest and occasionally modified resection strategy, data on long-term survival remain limited and inconsistent. Heterogeneity in indocyanine green dose and concentration, injection route and timing, imaging platforms, and outcome definitions limits comparison across studies. Indocyanine green-fluorescence imaging might be a valuable tool for intraoperative lymphatic mapping and enhancing lymphadenectomy; however, substantial methodologic heterogeneity precludes definitive conclusions regarding its diagnostic accuracy for nodal metastatic status. Standardized protocols and high-quality prospective studies are needed to define its optimal role and long-term oncologic impact.
cn_title: 吲哚菁绿荧光成像引导结直肠癌淋巴结示踪的技术差异与结局
insight: 系统梳理ICG淋巴结示踪的技术异质性与诊断准确性局限，提示需标准化方案及前瞻研究验证其对肠癌手术决策与肿瘤学结局的真实价值。
grade_rationale: 叙述性综述汇总多项Meta分析，证据异质性大且缺乏长期生存数据，尚不足以改变现有实践。

title: Macrophage-derived WNT regulates tumor immune microenvironment to reduce colitis-associated colon cancer.
authors: Bhanja P, Chugh RM, Rehman S, Krepel S, Mitra A, Gupta-Saraf P, et al.
abstract: Prolonged colonic inflammation and ulcerative colitis lead to colon cancer. The rapid growth and treatment-resistant nature of these tumors are primarily influenced by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which is led by tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). However, factors influencing or regulating the immunosuppressive nature of TAMs have not been sufficiently studied. In this manuscript, we use a mouse model of colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CRC) to demonstrate that WNT expression in TAMs regulates their immunosuppressive function by inhibiting Glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta (GSK-3β) within the macrophages, possibly through an autofeedback loop. GSK3β is a positive regulator of PD-1 and PD-L1 expression in macrophages and promotes an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therefore, GSK-3β inhibition alters the immunosuppressive nature of the immune microenvironment and effectively controls tumor growth. In Csf1r.iCre; Porcn
cn_title: 巨噬细胞源性WNT调控肿瘤免疫微环境抑制结肠炎相关结肠癌
insight: 揭示TAM来源WNT通过GSK-3β自反馈环路塑造免疫抑制微环境，为结肠炎相关肠癌提供靶向TAM-WNT/GSK-3β的免疫治疗新思路。

title: A self-amplifying IL-1β-CCL2 circuit between macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts drives colorectal cancer progression.
authors: Wang Y, Bao W, Li J, Jiang R, Jiang C, Li S
abstract: Reciprocal interactions between immune and stromal cells are increasingly recognized as major determinants of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression. However, the specific macrophage and fibroblast states cooperating to establish and sustain a tumor-promoting microenvironment remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify a self-reinforcing inflammatory circuit linking monocyte-derived IL-1β
cn_title: 巨噬细胞与癌相关成纤维细胞间IL-1β-CCL2自放大环路驱动结直肠癌进展
insight: 揭示单核来源巨噬细胞IL-1β与CAF来源CCL2构成自强化环路驱动CRC进展，为靶向肿瘤微环境炎症轴提供新干预靶点。

title: Socioeconomic inequalities in treatment for colorectal liver metastases in England: A competing risk analysis using National Cancer Registration Dataset.
authors: Saito MK, Quaresma M, Charvat H, Belot A, Issa E, Rachet B
abstract: There has been a wide variation, as well as socioeconomic inequalities, in liver resection rate for people diagnosed with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) in England. Currently, service specification in England requires providers to follow locally agreed referral pathways. However, decisions about patient referral to specialist multi-disciplinary teams (MDTs) may depend on local primary site-specific MDTs. We aimed to assess socioeconomic inequalities in the probability of undergoing liver resection/ablation (liver treatment), among patients diagnosed with synchronous/metachronous liver metastases (sLM/mLM). We identified patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer from 2015 to 2022 using the National Cancer Registration Dataset, and those with CRLM using the administrative dataset. We conducted a competing-risk analysis using flexible parametric regression models to estimate liver treatment-specific hazard up to one year after CRLM diagnosis by SES. We also derived cumulative probabilities of receiving treatment (CPr The population-level CPr Socioeconomic inequalities in liver treatment receipt persisted for sLM. Referral of all patients with CRLM to hepato-pancreato-biliary (HPB) specialists is recommended, irrespective of SES of patients. Potential policy lever could be promoting proactive HPB specialist involvement in local colorectal multi-disciplinary meetings to reduce variation in referral.
cn_title: 英格兰结直肠癌肝转移治疗的社会经济不平等：基于国家癌症登记数据的竞争风险分析
insight: 揭示英格兰CRLM肝切除/消融存在社会经济梯度，提示应推动所有CRLM患者转诊HPB专科并让HPB专家参与结直肠MDT以减少差异。
grade_rationale: 基于全国癌症登记大数据（2015-2022）的竞争风险分析，样本量大且具政策转化潜力，但为回顾性观察设计。

title: Fertility after colorectal surgery for endometriosis comparing conventional laparoscopy and robotic assisted laparoscopy Should all patients benefit from robotic approach?
authors: de Labrouhe E, Dabi Y, Dahan M, Ferrier C, Touboul C, Darai E, et al.
journal: Journal of Gynecology Obstetrics and Human Reproduction
abstract: The first objective was to present fertility outcomes following surgery for deep endometriosis with colorectal involvement at an expert endometriosis center, and to compare conventional laparoscopy with robotic-assisted laparoscopy. Secondary objectives included an analysis of pregnancy and obstetric outcomes. We conducted a retrospective, monocentric cohort study involving patients who underwent surgery for endometriosis between February 2019 and January 2023, with colorectal resection and wishing to become pregnant either before surgery or in the immediate postoperative period. Among the 72 patients wishing to conceive, 23/34 patients (68%) in the robotic-assisted laparoscopy group achieved pregnancy, compared to 25/38 patients (66%) in the conventional laparoscopy group (not significant (NS)). Spontaneous pregnancies occurred in 11/23 patients (48%) and 9/25 patients (36%), respectively (NS). Among those who achieved pregnancy, 18/23 patients (78.3%) in the robotic-assisted laparoscopy group and 21/25 patients (84%) in the conventional laparoscopy group had at least one live birth (NS). Our findings suggest that surgery for deep endometriosis with colorectal involvement, whether performed via robotic-assisted or conventional laparoscopy, yields similar postoperative fertility outcomes.
cn_title: 深部浸润型子宫内膜异位症结直肠切除术后生育结局：机器人辅助与传统腹腔镜比较
insight: 在结直肠受累的深部子宫内膜异位症中，机器人辅助与传统腹腔镜术后生育结局相当，提示机器人路径不应被普遍推广，对肠癌微创手术技术评价亦有方法学借鉴。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性小样本（72例）且两组生育结局无统计学差异，不足以改变临床实践。

title: Effect of changes in baseline cancer mortality rates and survival functions on the estimated risks of radiation-induced cancer.
authors: Hirouchi J, Kujiraoka I, Noguchi Y, Manabe K, Takahara S
journal: Journal of Radiological Protection : Official Journal of the Society for Radiological Protection
abstract: One of the uncertainty factors in estimating radiation-induced cancer risk is temporal changes in baseline cancer and all-cause mortality rates, which reflect advances in medical and diagnostic technologies, increased diagnostic frequency, and improvements in lifestyle, hygiene standards, and public health. Assessments of radiation-induced cancer risk have generally been performed using constant baseline data and therefore do not consider the effects of temporal changes in these data. To determine the effect of changes in baseline data on risk estimation, we calculated lifetime attributable risks (LARs) for individuals from six countries and different regions under two conditions: using constant baseline data and using baseline data that changed over time . The LARs were calculated for all solid cancers, oesophagus cancer, stomach cancer, colon cancer, lung cancer, and breast cancer. The LARs calculated using changing baseline data were comparable to those calculated using constant baseline data in 2021, and were, on average, approximately 1.7-fold higher (ranging from 0.8-to 4fold) than those calculated using constant baseline data in 1955. Furthermore, comparison of the effects of baseline data changes with that of other uncertainty factors indicated that the effect of baseline changes was greater than that of the minimum latency period but smaller than those of the fitting parameter of the risk models and the dose and dose-rate effectiveness factor.
cn_title: 基线癌症死亡率与生存函数变化对辐射诱发癌症风险估计的影响
insight: 基线数据随时间变化显著影响辐射致癌风险估计，提示流行病学风险模型需纳入动态基线；对肠癌放射相关风险研究有方法学参考价值。
grade_rationale: 基于多国数据的建模分析，属方法学探讨，非临床干预研究，对临床实践影响有限。

title: Pleiotropic roles of microbial bile acid metabolism in intestinal health and diseases.
authors: Qi M, Liu X, Gonzalez FJ
abstract: Perturbation of microbial-derived bile acid (BA) metabolism is strongly linked to the pathogenesis of intestinal diseases, including inflammatory bowel disease, enteric infections, and colorectal cancer. Recent advances in artificial intelligence-assisted pipelines have enabled the identification of BA modification reactions, which have uncovered novel targets and the mechanisms contributing to intestinal diseases. In this review, we summarize recent studies on microbial enzymatic pathways and modifications of BAs, and their roles in promoting or preventing intestinal diseases. The mechanisms altering gut microbiota populations and microbial BA metabolic landscapes that influence intestinal diseases are further examined along with how microbial-derived BAs modulate intestinal immune responses. Based on these advances, we suggest different dietary patterns that reshape the gut microbiota community and BAs to prevent intestinal diseases. We further discuss current challenges in basic and translational research on microbial BA modifications in intestinal homeostasis and propose future directions to drive progress in this field.
cn_title: 微生物胆汁酸代谢在肠道健康与疾病中的多效性作用
insight: 系统阐述微生物胆汁酸代谢在肠癌等肠道疾病中的多效性作用，为靶向胆汁酸-菌群轴预防结直肠癌及肝转移提供新思路。
grade_rationale: 综述性文章，非原始研究，但系统整合AI辅助发现与机制进展，对领域方向有指导意义，暂不改变临床实践。

title: Mutant KRAS favors a microbe that signals back.
authors: Jiao N, Zhu L, Zhu R
abstract: Tumor genetics and the microbiome both shape colorectal cancer, but their reciprocal interplay remains poorly defined. In this issue of Cell Host & Microbe, Jiao et al. show that mutant KRAS favors Bacteroides acidifaciens, which signals back through a SusF-ARHGEF2 axis to reinforce RAS-MAPK signaling.
cn_title: 突变KRAS促进产酸拟杆菌并形成正反馈信号环路
insight: 揭示KRAS突变与肠道菌群双向互作机制，为肠癌靶向KRAS及微生态干预提供新思路。
grade_rationale: Cell Host & Microbe述评，机制新颖但尚处临床前，暂不改变实践。

title: A self-assembled hydrophobic polymer tagged nanoplatform for membrane protein degradation and immunomodulatory drug delivery.
authors: Lee S, Park M, Jeon S, Byun H, Kim WJ
abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) has emerged as a powerful strategy for eliminating disease-driving proteins, yet its broader application remains constrained by limited target specificity and the lack of integrated therapeutic delivery functions. Here, we report Tri@N, a multimodal polymeric nanoplatform that extends hydrophobic polymer-based TPD to membrane-associated targets while simultaneously enabling immunomodulatory drug delivery. Tri@N is engineered to remain stable during systemic circulation but undergo intracellular disassembly in response to elevated GSH levels. This disassembly exposes hydrophobic polymer segments that function as a hydrophobic polymer tag, promoting EGFR destabilization and degradation through both proteasomal and autophagy-lysosomal pathways. In parallel, Tri@N releases niclosamide (NIC), which suppresses the STAT3/PD-L1 signaling axis.
