In HFF3 cells, the maximum cytotoxicity was observed at 72 h with 1.0 mg/mL free AgB (4.7 ± 0.2%) and nanocapsulated AgB (3.7 ± 0.1%), which were lower than the corresponding values in CT26 cells. title: Bioactive compounds from Perilla frutescens modulate multiple cell death pathways and signaling networks in cancer therapy.
authors: Xu H, Liu J, Wu H, Sabit H, Huang B, Zhou Y, et al.
abstract: Perilla frutescens, an edible medicinal plant from East Asia, produces diverse bioactive phytochemicals with anticancer activity, including perillaldehyde (PAH), rosmarinic acid (RA), luteolin, apigenin, and alpha-linolenic acid (ALA). These compounds exert multi-target anticancer effects through apoptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis. PAH triggers ferroptosis in gastric cancer via the System Xc-/GSH/GPX4 axis and P62-Keap1-Nrf2 pathway, while inducing protective autophagy in colorectal cancer through SRD5A1 and PI3K/AKT modulation. RA directly binds KRAS(G12C) and suppresses NSCLC via KRAS/AKT/ERK, and inhibits stress-induced TNBC metastasis through Src inactivation.

grade_rationale: 综述性文章，汇总临床前证据，无临床数据或外部验证，暂不具备改变实践的直接潜力。

title: B7-H3-mediated immune regulation in cancer: biological functions and therapeutic opportunities.
authors: Shreshtha S, Kaluarachchige L, Meyer OA, Schwarz GM, Basnyat AS, Zhang J, et al.
abstract: B7-H3 (CD276), a member of the B7 family of immunoregulatory ligands, has emerged as an important molecule at the intersection of tumor biology and cancer immunology. Although initially identified as a regulator of T-cell responses, accumulating evidence supports its predominantly immunosuppressive role. B7-H3 is highly expressed across diverse malignancies, including brain, prostate, lung, breast, colorectal, and pediatric cancers, while showing limited expression in most normal adult tissues. Its tumor-associated expression, including tumor vasculature, makes B7-H3 an attractive therapeutic target. Beyond immune regulation, B7-H3 promotes tumor progression through tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms involving PI3K/AKT, NF-κB, and STAT3 signaling, angiogenesis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity, and metabolic reprogramming. Within the tumor microenvironment, B7-H3 suppresses T-cell and natural killer cell activity and promotes immunosuppressive macrophage polarization, while its expression can be regulated by metabolic and epigenetic mechanisms. These multifaceted functions have stimulated the development of diverse B7-H3-targeted therapies, including monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR T-cell and Vδ1 T-cell therapies, nanobody-based platforms, and bispecific or trispecific immune cell engagers. Early clinical studies have demonstrated promising antitumor activity, although important challenges regarding efficacy, safety, tumor heterogeneity, and patient selection remain. In this review, we summarize the molecular regulation and biological functions of B7-H3, critically evaluate the current development of B7-H3-targeted therapies, and discuss key challenges and future directions for translating B7-H3-directed strategies into effective cancer treatments.
cn_title: B7-H3介导的肿瘤免疫调控：生物学功能与治疗机遇

title: Peri-interventional neutrophil extracellular traps and immune surveillance in hepatocellular carcinoma: mechanisms, biomarkers, and recurrence after liver resection or thermal ablation.
authors: Xu H, Yi J, Zhang W, Zhu S, Liu Z
abstract: Recurrence remains common after curative-intent liver resection or thermal ablation for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). These interventions transiently remodel the hepatic and treatment-bed immune microenvironment through overlapping but distinct processes, including tissue injury, vascular and coagulation activation, neutrophil recruitment, and, particularly during resection, hepatic ischemia-reperfusion. We organize the evidence using a peri-interventional two-component heuristic: chronic liver disease and tumor-associated inflammation may shape baseline susceptibility, whereas acute treatment injury may trigger intervention-specific neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) accumulation. title: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-based nanoformulations for cancer therapy: antitumor mechanisms, challenges, and future directions.
authors: Yang X, Jia S, Wu M, Zhou Y
abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)-derived compounds have anticancer potential because of their multi-component, multi-target actions and generally favorable toxicity profiles. Clinical translation, however, is limited by poor aqueous solubility, rapid systemic metabolism, and insufficient tumor-selective delivery. This review critically evaluates recent TCM-based nanoformulations developed to address these limitations and improve the therapeutic performance. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) and EQUATOR guidance, PubMed and Web of Science databases were searched for original studies published during the previous 5 years using terms including "TCM," "nanoformulation," and "anticancer." After screening 387 records, 81 studies covering 50 representative TCM compounds were included and assessed for the preparation methods, antitumor mechanisms, and translational barriers. Relative to free compounds, nanoformulations frequently improved solubility, stability, apparent bioavailability, or the targeting efficiency of TCM constituents. Reported mechanisms included apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest, ferroptosis, immunogenic cell death, and tumor-microenvironment remodeling across breast, lung, colorectal, and other cancer models. Nevertheless, most evidence was derived from TCM-based nanoformulations represent a promising strategy for integrating traditional herbal medicine with modern cancer therapy. Despite these promising findings, substantial challenges remain in standardization, reproducibility, pharmacokinetics, long-term safety, manufacturing, and clinical validation. Future studies should prioritize head-to-head comparisons, quantitative biodistribution, clinically relevant models, and scalable manufacturing.

title: Intratumoral microbiota-host gene associations characterize stage-associated microecological patterns in colorectal cancer.
authors: Chen Z, Gan W, Cao F, Yu F, Lin W, Wang X, et al.
abstract: Intratumoral microbiota are emerging as important ecological components of the colorectal cancer (CRC) microenvironment. However, their stage-associated patterns and coordination with host gene expression remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize stage-associated associations between intratumoral microbiota and the host transcriptome in CRC. We profiled 73 regional tumor specimens from 30 independent, treatment-naïve CRC patients using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing and mRNA sequencing. Microbial diversity, predicted functional profiles, co-occurrence networks, differential abundance, and microbiota-host transcriptome associations were analyzed. Regularized canonical correlation analysis and machine-learning modeling with SHAP-based feature interpretation were performed to identify stage-discriminative features. Candidate associations were evaluated in two independent public microbiome datasets. Mendelian randomization and immune-infiltration analyses were further conducted to explore the potential biological relevance of representative microbiota-gene associations. Disease stage was a major factor shaping intratumoral microbial composition. Advanced-stage CRC exhibited increased microbial α-diversity, distinct predicted functional profiles, and altered microbial co-occurrence patterns. Integrated microbiota-transcriptome analysis identified ten genus-level and six species-level candidate microbiota-gene association pairs. Core genera showed reproducible stage-discriminative signals in two independent public microbiome datasets. SHAP analysis identified the principal microbial and host transcriptomic features contributing to stage classification. Integrating microbial and host gene signatures improved classification performance, with the combined model achieving an AUROC greater than 0.90. The Intratumoral microbiota and host transcriptional profiles exhibit coordinated, stage-associated alterations in CRC. The identified microbiota-gene associations, particularly the

title: Case Report: Apparent progressive complete mismatch repair protein loss during platinum-based chemotherapy in metastatic rectal neuroendocrine tumour grade 2.
authors: Yang Y, Li G, Wang J, Wu W, Tang D
abstract: Mismatch repair (MMR) deficiency is uncommon in gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours (GEP-NETs), yet it represents a critical biomarker for immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) eligibility. Treatment-associated reduction or loss of MMR protein expression, often without corresponding MSI-H, has been reported in colorectal adenocarcinoma, but comparable changes have not been described in neuroendocrine tumours. Persistent discordance between immunohistochemistry (IHC)-based MMR protein assessment and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based microsatellite instability (MSI) testing is an emerging and clinically challenging phenomenon. We report a 55-year-old woman initially diagnosed with rectal NET Grade 1 on endoscopic biopsy; the tumour was upgraded to NET Grade 2 (Ki-67 approximately 20%) on the surgical resectionk specimen. Hepatic metastases were confirmed four months after resection. The first liver biopsy (January 16, 2026) demonstrated partial MMR protein loss by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2+, MSH6-, PMS2-), while concurrent NGS showed microsatellite stability (MSS) and a tumour mutational burden (TMB) of <1 mut/Mb. The patient received two cycles of surufatinib 250 mg orally once daily combined with intravenous carboplatin (500 mg, day 1) and etoposide (160 mg, days 1-3). Restaging CT demonstrated disease progression. A repeat liver biopsy (March 17, 2026) revealed complete loss of all four MMR proteins by IHC (MLH1-, MSH2-, MSH6-, PMS2-), while NGS again confirmed MSS and TMB <1 mut/Mb. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of apparent progressive complete MMR protein loss in the context of sequential platinum-based chemotherapy in metastatic rectal NET Grade 2, with persistent IHC-NGS discordance throughout. These findings raise an important question regarding how IHC-defined dMMR should be interpreted in the absence of NGS-confirmed MSI-H, and highlight the complexity of immunotherapy eligibility decisions in rare tumour types. Prospective data are needed to guide clinical practice.

grade_rationale: 单例个案报道，无外部验证，仅提出IHC-NGS不一致的临床疑问，不足以改变实践。

title: Prognostic value of the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio in patients with colorectal cancer undergoing chemotherapy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Zhang Y, Ding N, Cui Y, Yi C, Chen W
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden. Chemotherapy is central to the management of advanced or metastatic disease and is also used in perioperative settings, but outcomes vary substantially. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is an inexpensive and readily available marker of systemic inflammation; its prognostic association in chemotherapy-treated CRC warrants focused evaluation. This study adhered to PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to July 15, 2025. Studies evaluating pretreatment NLR in relation to overall survival (OS) or a secondary progression- or recurrence-related time-to-event outcome, including progression-free survival (PFS), disease-free survival (DFS), or recurrence-free survival (RFS), in chemotherapy-treated CRC patients were eligible. Study screening, data extraction, and quality assessment were independently conducted by two reviewers. Pooled hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using random-effects models. Subgroup and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed. Thirty-eight studies (41 cohorts; 11,346 patients) were included. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer OS (HR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.54-1.84; P < 0.0001) and poorer progression- or recurrence-related survival (HR = 1.61, 95% CI 1.43-1.81; P < 0.0001). The direction of association was generally consistent across exploratory subgroups defined by treatment category, age, geographic region, and NLR cut-off. Leave-one-out analyses did not identify a single study that changed the direction of either pooled association. Between-study heterogeneity and evidence of small-study effects warrant cautious interpretation. Elevated pretreatment NLR was associated with poorer survival outcomes in chemotherapy-treated CRC. NLR may be a readily available prognostic biomarker, but heterogeneous populations, variable outcome definitions and cut-off values, inconsistent covariate adjustment, and possible small-study effects currently limit its use for clinical decision-making. Prospective validation and methodological standardization are required before routine application. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420251136904.

title: Proteasuria: extending an existing term into a framework for concentration-based and catalytic protease diagnostics in urine, with emphasis on activity-based methods.
authors: Lesner A, Gruba N, Wysocka M
journal: Critical Reviews in Clinical Laboratory Sciences
abstract: Proteases are central to cancer pathobiology and attractive targets for noninvasive diagnosis. Diagnostic use of urinary proteases has developed along two methodologically distinct streams: measurement of protein abundance by immunoassay and increasingly by mass spectrometry, and direct measurement of enzymatic activity using peptide substrates. However, no common terminology unifies these approaches. This narrative review synthesizes evidence published between 2016 and 2026, concentrating on urine and, for the transferability of the methodology, on fecal water and serum. Saliva and seminal fluid are surveyed only to show that protease biomarkers there are measured by abundance alone. It adopts, from its existing use in nephrology, the term proteasuria as a unifying construct for the urinary protease diagnostic field, proposing a wider scope than the pathophysiological sense in which it was introduced. Two operational subtypes are defined: concentration-based and catalytic proteasuria. The distinction rests on the parameter measured rather than on the detection chemistry. Within the catalytic subtype single-enzyme detection using a selective substrate is distinguished from disease profiling using a multi-substrate panel. Evidence was identified by a PubMed search supplemented by citation and semantic search and screened by a single reviewer without protocol registration or formal risk-of-bias assessment. Concentration-based proteasuria is the clinically established stream, yet no urinary analyte has displaced cystoscopy, and approved assays remain insufficient as stand-alone rule-out or triage tests. The catalytic stream rests mainly on small single-center case-control studies reporting activity qualitatively; only one reports formal diagnostic performance, with a single elastase-specific substrate in 12 cases and 24 controls, and no head-to-head comparison with concentration-based assays has been published. Analytical validity is partial: substrate selectivity is established by combinatorial screening and confirmed with inhibitor and orthogonal controls, but precision, limits of quantification in urine and inter-laboratory reproducibility are not systematically reported, and no reference material or external quality-assessment scheme exists for this assay class. A largely independent exogenous stream of synthetic urinary biomarkers and activity-based nanosensors reports high accuracy, but all published diagnostic-accuracy data derive from animal models. On a translational-readiness scale the urinary catalytic stream is proof-of-concept, research-grade work, and any realistic target is therefore not cystoscopy but the margin at which established assays fail, principally low-grade noninvasive disease. The same reasoning identifies the detection of advanced adenoma, for which the fecal immunochemical test performs poorly, as the concrete benchmark for extending the framework to fecal protease profiling in colorectal cancer.

title: Oral and Fecal Microbial Dysbiosis as Non-Invasive Diagnostic Biomarkers for Gastrointestinal Cancers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy.
authors: Hu S, Chen Z, Li Y, Liao Q, Luo M, Song D, et al.
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) cancers, including esophageal (EC), gastric (GC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), impose a substantial global burden, with early detection remaining crucial for improving patient outcomes. The oral and gut microbiota are increasingly implicated in cancer development and hold promise as sources of non-invasive biomarkers. However, current evidence on microbiome-based diagnostics remains fragmented, and a systematic comparison of the diagnostic accuracy between oral and fecal sampling across multiple GI cancer types is lacking. To address this gap, a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Scopus up to December 31, 2025, identified 43 case-control studies (59 cohorts) comprising 4452 cancer patients and 5809 controls. title: Familial Cancers Associated With Cancers of the Breast, Prostate, Colorectum, and Lung in Sweden.
authors: Zitricky F, Sundquist K, Sundquist J, Hemminki A, Försti A, Hemminki K
abstract: Available epidemiological evidence shows that many cancers share familial risks, and this is increasingly confirmed by data on shared pathogenic germline gene variants between cancers. We decided to harness the world's largest resource on familial cancer to assess discordant familial risks for female breast (BC), prostate (PC), colorectal (CRC), and lung (LC) cancers with any of 22 different cancers in first-degree relatives (proband cancers). Familial relative risk was calculated as standardized incidence ratio (SIR) when either one proband or 2 or more (2+) probands were found in a family to distinguish low- and high-risk associations. Discordant familial associations of BC were significant for 12 1-proband and 5 2+ proband cancers. For PC, the numbers were 11 and 4; for CRC, they were 8 and 4; and for LC, they were 15 and 5. The results with large case numbers showed that BC, CRC, and LC associated with each other, but the familial association between PC and LC was negative. Many known or novel associations with possible genetic causes were found, including lobular BC with stomach cancer, PC with kidney cancer, CRC with squamous cell skin and thyroid cancers, and LC with gallbladder and endocrine tumors, the most common of which were parathyroid adenomas. Also, LC associations with esophageal and cervical cancers were unlikely to be due to smoking alone and require additional explanations. In conclusion, 2/3 of discordant associations could suggest low-risk genetic and environmental causation and 1/3 high-risk genetic causation, both waiting for experimental proof.

grade_rationale: 基于全国登记的大样本回顾性队列，但为探索性关联分析，未直接改变临床实践。

title: Cancer Risk in Haemodialysis Patients Compared With That in the General Population: A Multicenter Questionnaire-Based Study in Okinawa, Japan.
authors: Arakawa Y, Ishida Y, Higa A, Tana T, Moromizato T, Kohagura K, et al.
abstract: Dialysis patients face a heightened risk of cancer, particularly kidney cancer. The global aging of dialysis patients suggests that managing cancer may become a critical factor in future healthcare. Given that the chronic uremic state is a cancer risk factor, dialysis patients may face an elevated risk for all cancers. However, the epidemiology of nonkidney cancers, such as colorectal cancer, remains to be fully elucidated. This was a retrospective cohort study targeting 74 dialysis facilities in Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. The subjects were patients who received dialysis for a minimum of 90 days between 2015 and 2019 and were diagnosed with cancer after initiating dialysis during this period. The cancer incidence ratio for the study population (21 655 person-years) was then compared with that of the general Okinawan population using standardized incidence ratios. A total of 404 cancer cases were collected from 56 facilities (76%). The standardized incidence ratios for all cancers was 1.36, with the risk of kidney cancer increasing with longer dialysis vintage. Patients with a dialysis vintage of less than 2 years showed an increased risk of colorectal and lung cancer. The risk of breast cancer was similar to that of the general population. The present study revealed that not all cancer risks were increased among patients receiving haemodialysis. Screening for colorectal and lung cancer in the first 2 years after commencement of dialysis may be important. Further research is needed to determine the efficacy of this approach for patients receiving dialysis.

title: Exploring Structure-Activity Relationships: Discovering the Anticancer Potential of Dietary Bioactive Constituents: A Mini-Review.
authors: Kumar JDS, Sujatha K, Keerthana JV, Karthik BH, Srimathi R
abstract: Cancer is the leading cause of mortality worldwide. It encompasses a spectrum of malignancies that include lung, stomach, colon, prostate, liver, and skin cancers depending on the organ it affects. Epidemiological evidence indicates that regular consumption of cruciferous vegetables leads to a 10-20% reduction in the risk of lung, breast, and colorectal cancers and bioactive dietary constituents. The lipophilic character of phytochemicals facilitates membrane permeability and selective target engagement, underscoring their pharmacological relevance. Daily dietary intake introduces varying amounts of bioactive constituents that can act as preventive agents, thereby improving human health. In this review, we discuss the therapeutic potential of selected dietary natural products, focusing on cinnamaldehyde, eugenol, β-glucan, gingerol, shogaol, curcumin, and epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). Strong scientific literature studies support the role of these compounds in targeting key molecular pathways, including the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, caspase-3 activation, and Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription (STAT) signaling. Bioavailability, dosing, and safety profiles remain challenges, particularly in ensuring that these factors do not hinder therapeutic efficacy. Analyzing the pharmacophoric features and discussing their potential for structural optimization leads to the development of clinical candidates in the market. Combination therapy of plant-derived bioactive compounds with anticancer drugs has improved patient outcomes in many studies, leading to the development of natural product-assisted therapeutics in the future.

abstract: Melatonin has demonstrated antitumor activity in various cancer models, but its effects may depend on the therapeutic dose and cellular environment. title: Tumor Biology and Surgical Margin Patterns in Colorectal Liver Metastases: Association Between KRAS/BRAF Status and Type of Resection
authors: Ferrari C, D'Ambrosio GM, Molina V, Famularo S, Milana F, Patrone R, et al.
journal: Journal of Laparoendoscopic & Advanced Surgical Techniques. Part A
abstract: Surgical strategies for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) have progressively evolved toward parenchyma-sparing approaches, increasing the relevance of understanding the relationship between tumor biology and resection margin patterns. In parallel, KRAS and BRAF mutations have emerged as key determinants of tumor behavior in CRLM. The interaction between mutational status and surgical margin type, however, remains insufficiently characterized. This multicenter retrospective study included patients undergoing curative-intent liver resection for CRLM between 2016 and 2021 across 17 international HPB centers. Clinicopathological variables were compared according to mutational status and margin type. Among 1078 eligible patients, KRAS-mutated patients more frequently presented synchronous metastases, nodal involvement, and administration of perioperative chemotherapy compared with wild-type patients. Higher tumor burden was associated with both R1 parenchymal (R1P) and R1 vascular (R1V) resections. Within KRAS-mutated patients, synchronous disease and bilobar involvement were more frequently associated with R1P resections. KRAS/BRAF mutational status is associated with distinct clinicopathological patterns in patients undergoing liver resection for CRLM. Higher tumor burden and biologically aggressive disease features are more frequently associated with R1P and R1V resections, particularly among KRAS-mutated tumors.
cn_title: 结直肠癌肝转移肿瘤生物学与手术切缘模式：KRAS/BRAF状态与切除类型的关联
insight: 多中心研究揭示KRAS/BRAF突变与CRLM切缘类型相关，提示生物学特征应纳入手术决策，推动切缘策略个体化。
grade_rationale: 17中心大样本回顾性研究，揭示基因状态与切缘模式关联，但非干预性设计，尚不足以直接改变实践。

title: Integrated scRNA-Seq and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal CHPF and GPC1 as Markers of Cancer-Associated Fibroblast-Dominant Domains in Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Liu YJ, Ye QW, Zhang H, Yang N, Li Y, Li JP
abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in the colorectal cancer (CRC) tumor microenvironment (TME) is closely related to stromal organization and may influence treatment-related features. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic data from CRC tissues to examine cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-dominant spatial domains. GPC1 and CHPF were enriched in stromal regions and showed higher expression in CRC tissues than in normal tissues. In the analyzed cohorts, higher GPC1 and CHPF expression was associated with advanced clinicopathological features and poorer survival outcomes in univariate analyses. Single-cell analyses showed that GPC1 and CHPF were mainly expressed in fibroblasts and were enriched in an ADAM12-associated fibroblast subset with myofibroblast-like features, extracellular matrix-related genes, and hypoxia/glycolysis-related signatures. Cell-cell communication analysis suggested that this fibroblast subset was linked to higher inferred WNT signaling. Drug-response and immunotherapy-related analyses further showed that GPC1 and CHPF expression was associated with transcriptomic patterns related to treatment response. In mucinous adenocarcinoma (MA), the ADAM12-associated fibroblast program showed stronger inferred MIF-related signaling and was associated with macrophage M2-like features. Spatial mapping and multiplex immunofluorescence supported partial colocalization of GPC1, CHPF, and ADAM12 in CAF-rich stromal regions. In CAFs, GPC1 or CHPF knockdown reduced ADAM12, CAF activation markers, and WNT/MIF-related proteins, while ADAM12 knockdown weakened macrophage M2-like marker expression in a co-culture model. These findings suggest that GPC1 and CHPF mark an ADAM12-associated CAF program linked to stromal remodeling and immune-related features in CRC, especially in MA, but further studies are needed to define its functional role.
cn_title: 整合单细胞与空间转录组揭示CHPF和GPC1标记结直肠癌CAF主导空间域
insight: 该研究通过多组学整合识别出CHPF/GPC1标记的ADAM12相关CAF亚群，与基质重塑、免疫抑制及黏液腺癌微环境相关，为肠癌CAF靶向及免疫治疗分层提供新标志物。
grade_rationale: 研究基于单细胞与空间转录组整合及功能验证，但缺乏外部大样本验证和临床干预数据，尚不足以改变实践。

title: Association of the transanal approach with the accuracy of distal margin achievement in rectal cancer surgery.
authors: Shiraishi T, Endo M, Ozawa N, Komine C, Okada T, Kimura A, et al.
abstract: Adequate distal margin (DM) achievement is essential in oncological rectal cancer surgery. In conventional transabdominal surgery, however, the intraluminal location of the distal tumor edge must be translated to an externally applied transection line; this potentially causes discrepancies between intended and achieved margins. This study aimed to evaluate the discrepancy between the planned intraoperative DM and the margin achieved in rectal cancer resection, identify factors associated with DM discrepancy, and evaluate the association between the transanal approach, specifically transanal total mesorectal excision, and DM accuracy. This retrospective cohort study included 171 consecutive patients who underwent curative-intent laparoscopic or robot-assisted low anterior resection (LAR) or intersphincteric resection between July 2019 and June 2025. The intended DM in operative records was compared with the pathological DM measured in formalin-fixed specimens. The primary outcome was the absolute DM discrepancy. As the distribution was skewed, adjusted median regression was performed using the transanal approach, intended DM, tumor distance from the anal verge, maximum tumor size, surgical platform, and surgical era as covariates. The median absolute DM discrepancy was 4.0 mm and was smaller with than without the transanal approach (3.0 vs. 6.0 mm; p < 0.001). After adjustment, transanal approach omission was associated with greater absolute DM discrepancy (β, 3.938 mm; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.848-6.027; p < 0.001). Greater maximum tumor size was also associated with greater discrepancy (β per 1-mm increase, 0.075 mm; 95% CI 0.040-0.110; p < 0.001). This association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses restricted to LAR and after exclusion of scar-based pathological DM measurements. The transanal approach was associated with a smaller discrepancy between intended and achieved DMs after adjustment for tumor characteristics, surgical platform, and surgical era. Assessing the distal tumor edge and intended transection line within the same transanal operative field may facilitate more precise DM control.
cn_title: 经肛入路与直肠癌手术远端切缘准确性关联研究
insight: 经肛入路（taTME）可显著缩小计划与实际远端切缘的偏差，提示其有助于提高直肠癌保肛手术的肿瘤学精确性，对肝转移风险控制具潜在意义。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性队列，样本量中等（171例），虽调整混杂但证据等级有限，尚不足以直接改变指南。

title: TRIDENT: inTRaoperative Imaging DEvice based on endogeNous opTical properties to evaluate bowel oxygenation in left-sided colorectal resections. Observational first-in-human pilot safety trial.
authors: Lapergola A, Baratelli L, Shein GS, Philouze G, Kpekou S, Pardo A, et al.
abstract: Adequate tissue oxygenation at the anastomotic site is a key determinant of healing after colorectal surgery. Current intraoperative imaging technologies aimed at assessing bowel perfusion present several limitations, including the need for exogenous contrast agents, limited quantification capabilities, or suboptimal integration within the surgical workflow. Single Snapshot Imaging of Optical Properties (SSOP) is a contrast-free optical imaging technology capable of quantifying tissue oxygen saturation (StO In this prospective, single-center feasibility trial, patients undergoing elective left-sided colorectal resection with primary anastomosis were enrolled. After bowel exteriorization, surgeons identified the intended proximal transection line based on their clinical judgement. SSOP imaging was then performed to quantify tissue oxygenation along the exposed colon segment before resection. The primary endpoints of the study were assessing the overall intraoperative safety and workflow feasibility of the Trident system. The secondary endpoint was to obtain wide-field oxygen saturation (StO Between September 2023 and April 2024, 10 patients were enrolled (8 males; mean age 65.5 ± 11.8 years; mean BMI 27.5 ± 4.6 kg/m This first-in-human study demonstrated that SSOP imaging using Trident is safe, feasible, and compatible with standard surgical workflow during left-sided colorectal resections. The ability to provide real-time, quantitative, contrast-free mapping of bowel oxygenation may represent a promising tool for intraoperative perfusion assessment. Larger prospective studies are needed to evaluate whether SSOP-guided surgery can improve anastomotic outcomes (NCT05973227).
cn_title: TRIDENT：基于内源性光学特性的术中成像设备评估左半结直肠切除吻合口氧合的首例人体安全试验
insight: 该研究首次证实无造影剂SSOP成像在左半结直肠术中评估肠管氧合安全可行，为吻合口灌注实时定量监测提供新工具，有望指导吻合口位置选择并降低吻合口漏风险。
grade_rationale: 单中心、小样本（n=10）首例人体可行性试验，仅验证安全性与工作流可行性，尚不足以改变临床实践。

title: Implementation of a single-port robotic platform into your colorectal surgery practice: a SAGES colorectal committee task force review of evolving robotic technology and innovations.
authors: Sarin A, Dourado J, Seffren CM, Sidhu US, Pourghaderi P, Aminpour N, et al.
abstract: Robotic and endoscopic techniques continue to revolutionize minimally invasive surgery. Single-port (SP) robotic platforms mark a new era in minimally invasive colorectal surgery, combining single-incision/site access with full robotic articulation through a single access point. This manuscript, as a part of a four-part series, outlines specific technical considerations of the SP robotic platform including details of the platform, instrumentation, docking, and operative maneuvers. Subject matter experts from the SAGES Colorectal Committee SP Task Force performed a structured review of the currently FDA-approved SP robotic platform, assessing technical features, instrumentation, and workflow considerations for several key representative operations relevant to colorectal surgery. Three clinical areas of SP implementation included transanal robotic surgery, right colectomy, and low anterior resection (LAR). Task Force members (subject matter experts with early experience in SP robotic platforms) analyzed technical details, patient selection, and operative workflows. Representative procedural techniques were detailed with emphasis on instrumentation choice, docking strategies, and key operative steps specific to single-port colorectal surgery. The technical aspects of the SP platform include full robotic articulation through a single 25 mm port. A SP approach also enables triangulation and dexterity within confined spaces using three wristed instruments and a flexible 3-D camera. The current 360-degree boom rotation facilitates multi-quadrant manipulation without redocking. Current limitations may include continued reliance on bedside assistance for certain energy and stapling operative steps, although stapling capability has expanded with FDA clearance of an SP-compatible 45 mm stapler as of April 2025. Training of the entire operative team and gradual progression of case complexity is recommended as the surgeon implements this new technology into clinical practice. A SP robotic approach to minimally invasive colorectal surgical procedures is feasible for a range of colorectal surgery operations. In select procedures like SP TAMIS, SP right colectomy, and SP-LAR, the single-port platform appears to offer advantages related to reduced invasiveness and improved surgeon ergonomics compared to other minimally invasive approaches. Successful implementation requires structured training, careful patient selection, and adherence to evidence-based adoption principles.
cn_title: 单孔机器人平台在结直肠外科实践中的实施：SAGES结直肠委员会工作组综述
insight: 该综述系统阐述了单孔机器人平台在结直肠手术中的技术要点与操作流程，为肠癌微创手术的规范化开展和培训提供了实践指导，对肝转移同期手术的微创化亦有潜在启示。
grade_rationale: SAGES委员会专家共识，基于结构化综述与专家经验，非原始研究，但为新技术推广提供框架，实践改变潜力有限。

title: A health-system-scale, episode-resolved multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia.
authors: Castillon VJ, Xie AX, Boscenco S, Tse E, Ruthen N, Wang J, et al.
abstract: Cancer cachexia is a wasting syndrome with outsized impact on morbidity and mortality, yet its drivers and systemic consequences remain poorly defined. In this study, we repurposed longitudinal clinicogenomic data from 52,236 patients with cancer profiled by MSK-IMPACT (2010-2024) at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center to define episode-resolved trajectories of consensus-defined cachectic weight loss and linked these events to outcomes, serology and tumor genotypes. Cachectic episodes clustered near periods of disease progression and were associated with inferior outcomes in nearly all cancer types. Across diverse malignancies, cachectic weight loss episodes exhibited a consistent serologic signature characterized by lower albumin and hemoglobin and higher levels of liver enzymes. Numerous somatic tumor genotypes, including TP53 mutation across several diseases, were also associated with more frequent onset of cachectic episodes. Motivated by these observations, we developed a multivariate model to predict impending risk of cachectic weight loss in patients with lung, colorectal and prostate cancer, validated in an independent, external cohort from Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (n = 5,785). Routine clinicogenomic data are, therefore, a scalable resource for discovery in cancer cachexia.
cn_title: 健康系统规模、发作解析的癌症恶病质多模态图谱
insight: 基于5.2万例纵向临床基因组数据构建恶病质发作轨迹图谱，揭示其与疾病进展、血清标志物及肿瘤基因型的关联，并建立可外部验证的预测模型，为肠癌恶病质风险分层提供 scalable 工具。
grade_rationale: 大样本真实世界队列+外部验证，但为观察性研究且非肠癌专属，暂不足以改变实践。

title: TNFα-driven epigenetic upregulation of TIGIT creates a targetable vulnerability in tumors.
authors: Huang X, Xiong C, Yu M, Wang J, Liang P, Li G, et al.
abstract: T cell immunoreceptor with Ig and ITIM domains (TIGIT) is a key inhibitory receptor on cytotoxic lymphocytes, yet the mechanisms governing its context-dependent upregulation in tumors remain poorly defined. Here, we identify tumor necrosis factor-α (TNFα) signaling as an upstream driver of TIGIT expression. Integrated analyses of patient transcriptomic datasets revealed a consistent positive association between TNFα pathway activity and TIGIT expression across multiple cancer types, with strong concordance in melanoma and prognostic relevance in kidney renal clear cell carcinoma. Mechanistically, TNFα directly induced TIGIT expression in natural killer cells via TNFR2 signaling, increasing chromatin accessibility at distal TIGIT enhancers and promoting NF-κB and AP-1 recruitment together with BRD4 and P300. Functionally, combined anti-TNFα and anti-TIGIT treatment suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival more effectively than either monotherapy in murine melanoma and colon cancer models. These findings define a TNFα-TNFR2-enhancer axis controlling TIGIT expression and provide a mechanistic rationale for dual TNFα and TIGIT targeting in inflamed tumors.
cn_title: TNFα驱动TIGIT表观遗传上调及其联合靶向治疗策略
insight: 揭示TNFα-TNFR2-增强子轴上调TIGIT的机制，为炎症型肠癌（含肝转移）联合抗TNFα与抗TIGIT治疗提供依据。
grade_rationale: 多组学整合结合小鼠功能验证的机制研究，具转化潜力但尚无临床数据，暂不改变实践。

title: Older adults' experiences of adapting to changes after colorectal cancer surgery in Sweden: a qualitative study.
authors: Amirpour A, Holmgren AG, Nilsson U, Eckerblad J
abstract: To explore older adults’ experiences of adapting to physical, emotional and cognitive changes during the first month after colorectal cancer surgery. A qualitative descriptive study with an inductive approach was conducted in the Stockholm region, Sweden. Thirteen adults aged ≥60 years who had undergone planned colorectal cancer surgery participated in semi-structured interviews 1-month postoperatively. Data were analysed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s guidelines. Participants described recovery as a gradual and multifaceted process shaped by changes in their physical, cognitive and emotional capacities. Everyday activities required deliberate planning, pacing and continuous adjustment to fluctuating energy and function. These adaptations took place within a relational context, where support from family and healthcare professionals was experienced as both enabling and demanding. A heightened awareness of mortality emerged following the cancer diagnosis and remained present in daily life, influencing how participants prioritised and engaged in activities. Over time, participants navigated uncertainty through efforts to balance management and acceptance while striving to maintain autonomy and involvement in daily life. Recovery after colorectal cancer surgery in older adults is a dynamic and multidimensional process shaped by altered bodily capacity and awareness of mortality. Rehabilitation should extend beyond physical function to support everyday adaptation, autonomy and patients’ capacity to navigate uncertainty during the postoperative period. NCT05564195.
cn_title: 瑞典老年结直肠癌术后患者适应身心变化的质性研究
insight: 揭示老年肠癌术后康复是多维动态过程，需超越躯体功能，关注日常适应、自主性与不确定性应对，为术后康复模式优化提供依据。
grade_rationale: 单中心质性研究，样本量小（13例），无量化验证，但为康复实践提供患者视角，证据等级有限。

title: Auriculasin induces LACTB expression to regulate colorectal cancer cell apoptosis, ferroptosis, invasion, and in vivo tumor growth.
authors: Ke JS, Zeng L, Chen XJ, Qiu Y, Wu YZ, Du JB, et al.
abstract: Previous studies have found that auriculasin isolated from Flemingia philippinensis has a significant anticancer effect in colorectal cancer (CRC), but there are few studies on its mechanism. Treatment of CRC cells with auriculasin showed that auriculasin promoted LACTB expression in a dose-dependent manner, thereby enhancing reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and inhibiting cell viability. Auriculasin significantly enhanced CRC cell apoptosis and caspase-3/8/9 activities, and overexpression of LACTB also increased the caspase activities, but LACTB siRNA or N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC) significantly reduced the pro-apoptotic effects of auriculasin and LACTB. Auriculasin or LACTB overexpression significantly inhibited cell invasion, reducing the expression and secretion of matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-2/9, while LACTB siRNA or NAC restored cell invasion levels. cn_title: Auriculasin通过诱导LACTB表达调控结直肠癌细胞凋亡、铁死亡与侵袭
insight: 揭示天然化合物Auriculasin经LACTB-ROS轴诱导凋亡与铁死亡并抑制侵袭，为CRC提供新候选药物及LACTB相关机制线索。

title: Orally delivered metabolically reprogrammed probiotics for cascade-activated antitumor immunity in colorectal cancer.
authors: Wang L, Chen Y, Shang Y, Liu J, Zhao M, Jin L, et al.
abstract: Immunotherapy for colorectal cancer (CRC) remains limited due to the inherently low tumor immunogenicity and the profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Herein, capitalizing on the metabolic traits and anatomical accessibility of CRC, we propose a broadly applicable oral strategy based on metabolically engineered bacteria (EcN-HlpA-CGL [EHC]) for CRC immunotherapy. Mechanistically, cystathionine γ-lyase expressed by EHC disrupts redox homeostasis, triggering ferroptosis in CRC cells and thereby enhancing tumor immunogenicity. Concurrently, the intrinsic adjuvant activity of the bacteria amplifies the cancer-immunity cycle driven by immunogenic cell death and remodels the immunosuppressive TME. In vivo studies demonstrate that this orally delivered engineered bacterial platform not only suppresses the growth of orthotopic CRC tumors but also inhibits metastatic progression, indicating the induction of a potent systemic immune response. Immune profiling confirms robust systemic and gut mucosal immune activation following oral administration. Collectively, this oral metabolically engineered bacterial platform is precisely tailored to the features of CRC and offers a safe and effective immunotherapeutic strategy for this malignancy.
cn_title: 口服代谢重编程益生菌通过级联激活抗肿瘤免疫治疗结直肠癌
insight: 该研究利用口服工程化益生菌诱导铁死亡增强免疫原性并重塑微环境，为结直肠癌免疫治疗提供新策略，提示肝转移潜在应用。
grade_rationale: 临床前基础研究，机制创新但尚未进入临床试验，暂不具备实践改变潜力。

title: Association Between Preoperative Tea Drinking Habits and Postoperative Ileus in Colorectal Cancer Patients: A Propensity Score-Matched Study.
authors: Chen S, Jiang Y, Li H, Li C, Li L, Li J, et al.
abstract: ObjectiveThis study evaluated whether preoperative tea consumption reduces postoperative ileus risk after colorectal cancer surgery, given tea's anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort of 681 patients, tea drinkers (≥1 cup/day, n = 191) were compared to non-drinkers (n = 490). The primary outcome was Clavien-Dindo grade ≥2 POI within 30 postoperative days. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced baseline characteristics. Multivariable logistic and Cox regression analyses assessed associations, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses verifying robustness.ResultsAfter matching (191 pairs), tea drinkers showed significantly lower POI incidence (8.9% vs 15.7%). Tea consumption remained an independent protective factor (adjusted OR: 0.52, 95% CI: 0.29-0.93; HR: 0.54, 95% CI: 0.30-0.97). Enhanced protection was observed in males, patients ≤70 years, and open surgery cases. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness.ConclusionRegular preoperative tea consumption is associated with significantly reduced POI risk, supporting its consideration in prehabilitation protocols.
cn_title: 术前饮茶习惯与结直肠癌患者术后肠梗阻的关联：倾向性评分匹配研究
insight: 回顾性匹配研究提示术前规律饮茶与结直肠癌术后肠梗阻风险降低约一半相关，为术前预康复方案增添低成本候选干预，但需前瞻验证。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性队列，仅倾向性评分匹配控制混杂，证据等级有限，尚不足以改变临床实践。

title: Stage-dependent antitumor effects of Icaritin in AOM/DSS-induced colon cancer: association with CPEB1 restoration and suppression of CSC-associated Wnt/β-Catenin and Notch Signaling pathways.
authors: Chen Z, Hussain SA, Wang T
abstract: Cancer stem cells (CSCs) play a central role in colon cancer progression and are major contributors to metastasis, recurrence, and therapeutic resistance. CPEB1 (Cytoplasmic Polyadenylation Element Binding Protein 1) is a tumor suppressor, but its role in CSC-associated signaling during colon cancer progression remains insufficiently understood. The potential modulation of CPEB1 by Icaritin, a prenylated flavonoid, particularly in a stage-dependent context, has not been comprehensively investigated. To investigate the effect of Icaritin on CPEB1 expression, CSC-associated markers, apoptosis, inflammatory cytokines, and stemness-related signaling pathways during the early- and late-stage of colon cancer progression using an in vivo AOM/DSS-induced colon cancer model. In our study, colon cancer was induced in BALB/c mice using azoxymethane (AOM) and dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) administered in cycles (three cycles to model early-stage disease; six cycles to model advanced-stage disease). Tumor stage was confirmed by histopathological analysis, while western blotting was performed for CPEB1, CSC markers (CD133, ALDH1A1, Nanog, Sox2, CD44), apoptosis markers (Bcl-2, caspase-3, Bax), and key signaling pathway proteins (β-catenin, c-Myc, Notch1, Hes1). Serum cytokines IL-6, TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-10 were measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Ki-67 immunohistochemical staining was performed to evaluate tumor proliferative activity. Advanced-stage tumors exhibited significantly lower baseline CPEB1 expression and significantly higher CSC marker expression compared with early-stage tumors. Treatment with Icaritin was associated with a marked increase in CPEB1 expression in advanced-stage tumors, accompanied by a greater reduction in CSC marker expression and more pronounced reductions in the expression of β-catenin, c-Myc, Notch1, and Hes1. Apoptotic activation was more pronounced in advanced-stage models (as indicated by increased cleaved caspase-3 and Bax expression and decreased Bcl-2 levels). Cytokine modulation was also more substantial in advanced-stage disease, where IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β were markedly reduced, and IL-10 was significantly increased. Furthermore, Ki-67-positive proliferative activity was significantly elevated in advanced-stage tumors and was markedly reduced following Icaritin treatment. Icaritin exhibits enhanced anti-inflammatory, pro-apoptotic, and CSC-associated molecular modulatory effects in advanced-stage colon cancer and is associated with upregulated CPEB1 expression and greater suppression of CSC-associated markers and reduced expression of proteins associated with stemness-related signaling pathways compared with early-stage disease. The observed association between increased CPEB1 expression and suppression of CSC-associated signaling pathways suggests a potential role of CPEB1 restoration in Icaritin-mediated antitumor responses; however, direct CPEB1-dependent regulatory mechanisms remain to be established. The observed reductions in CSC-associated markers represent molecular changes and do not establish direct inhibition of CSC self-renewal or functional activity. Further mechanistic and functional CSC studies are warranted to clarify the direct regulatory relationship between CPEB1 restoration and the antitumor effects of Icaritin in colorectal cancer progression.
cn_title: 淫羊藿苷在AOM/DSS结肠癌模型中的阶段依赖性抗肿瘤作用及CPEB1与CSC相关Wnt/β-Catenin、Notch通路抑制的关联

title: CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in colorectal cancer: a proof-of-concept comparison with primary-tumor radiomics.
authors: Lin Z, Wang J, Chen H, Bao Q, Xu M, Yang S, et al.
abstract: Accurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in colorectal cancer remains challenging using conventional CT assessment. This proof-of-concept study compared CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics with primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative prediction of LNM. This single-center retrospective study included patients with pathologically confirmed colorectal cancer who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced CT and surgical resection. Patients were divided into training and validation cohorts. Radiomics features were extracted from the primary tumor and visible regional lymph nodes across multiple nodal stations. Three radiomics strategies were developed and compared: primary-tumor radiomics, multi-station lymph-node radiomics, and combined radiomics. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and five-fold cross-validation. Pairwise AUCs were compared using the DeLong test. A clinical-radiomic model was further constructed by integrating the optimal radiomics strategy with preoperative clinical variables. In the validation cohort, the multi-station lymph-node radiomics model outperformed the primary-tumor radiomics model for predicting LNM (AUC, 0.864 versus 0.637; p = 0.0055). The combined radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.840, without significant improvement over the lymph-node model (p = 0.2211). After integration with clinical variables, the clinical-radiomic model achieved an AUC of 0.879. CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics showed significantly higher validation performance than primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative LNM prediction in colorectal cancer. However, this single-center proof-of-concept model is not ready for direct clinical implementation and requires multicenter external validation before clinical translation. Question Can CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics improve preoperative nodal metastasis prediction beyond primary-tumor radiomics in patients with surgically treated colorectal cancer? Findings Multi-station lymph-node radiomics achieved higher validation performance than primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level prediction of pathological lymph-node metastasis in colorectal cancer. Relevance statement CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics may support individualized preoperative nodal risk stratification in colorectal cancer, but multicenter validation and prospective evaluation are required before clinical translation.
cn_title: 基于CT多站淋巴结影像组学术前预测结直肠癌淋巴结转移的概念验证研究
insight: 多站淋巴结影像组学显著优于原发瘤影像组学预测淋巴结转移，提示应重视转移淋巴结微环境影像特征，但需多中心外部验证。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性概念验证研究，样本与验证有限，虽AUC提升明显但尚不足以改变临床实践。

title: Increasing Detection of Early-Onset Rectal Neuroendocrine Neoplasms in the Era of Earlier Colorectal Cancer Screening.
authors: Al Khaldi M, Bayat Z, Kahana N, Perets M, Emile SH
abstract: BackgroundThis study aimed to evaluate contemporary national trends in the presentation, management, and outcomes of early-onset rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms (EORNETs).MethodsA retrospective cohort analysis of patients <50 years who underwent surgery for rectal neuroendocrine neoplasms was performed using the National Cancer Database (NCDB) (2004-2023). Patients undergoing surgery were categorized as local tumor excision or radical resection. Five-year overall survival (OS) was estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was used to identify factors associated with OS. The annual number of surgically treated cases increased from 234 in 2004 to 778 in 2023. 83.0% of tumors with known grade were low grade, and 90.6% of tumors with known clinical stage were stage I. title: Integrating Polygenic Risk Score, Sex, and Family History to Personalize the Initial Screening Age for Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Sun W, Liu D, Wang D, Liu J, Zhang Y, Liu F, et al.
abstract: While current colorectal cancer (CRC) screening guidelines consider family history to determine starting age for screening, they inadequately incorporate other important unmodifiable risk factors, including polygenic risk score (PRS) and biological sex. In 353,118 average-risk UK Biobank participants, we used family history-stratified Cox models to estimate associations of sex and PRS with CRC incidence, metastasis, and CRC-specific mortality. We translated risk differences into risk-adapted initiation screening ages using both risk advancement period (RAP) and absolute 10-year cumulative risk. Men had a higher risk of CRC compared to women, with HRs of 1.41 (95% CI, 1.33-1.50) for those without family history and 1.42 (95% CI, 1.26-1.61) for those with family history. For each one-standard deviation (SD) increase in PRS, the risk was 1.49 times higher (95% CI, 1.45-1.53) in participants without a family history and 1.42 times higher (95% CI, 1.34-1.51) in those with a family history. The increase in PRS was associated with elevated risks of both metastatic CRC at diagnosis and CRC-specific mortality, indicating delayed diagnosis in high-PRS individuals and highlighting the potential benefit of earlier screening. Consequently, risk-adapted initiation ages ranged from before 40 years for men with a family history in the high-PRS group to after 60 years for women without a family history in the low-PRS group. Our findings demonstrate that the integration of PRS, biological sex, and family history identifies substantial heterogeneity in CRC risk and risk-adapted screening initiation ages.

title: Supplementation with Akkermansia muciniphila Enhances the αPD-1 Efficacy in Mice Transplanted with Gut Microbiota from Patients with Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Zhao W, Yan D
abstract: The resistance of colorectal cancer (CRC) to PD-1 blockade has positioned it as a critical focus of global research efforts. The gut microbiota is a key regulator of anti-tumor immunity, but research on bacteria that are clearly associated with primary resistance to PD-1 blockade in colorectal cancer remains incomplete. In this study, C57BL/6 mice were subjected to antibiotic pretreatment to deplete endogenous gut microbiota. The mice were then gavaged with fecal suspensions from treatment-naïve CRC patients or healthy donors, subsequently implanted with MC38 tumor cells to establish the tumor model, and then treated with the drug. Gut microbial composition was analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, while tumor-infiltrating immune cells and cytokine profiles were characterized using flow cytometry and immunohistochemistry, respectively. CRC patient microbiota conferred resistance to anti-PD-1 therapy in mice, an effect completely reversed by oral Akkermansia muciniphila (Akk). Mechanistically, Akk reconfigured the tumor immune microenvironment, leading to a substantial increase in CD8+ T cell infiltration and function. Crucially, this potent local anti-tumor immunity was achieved without systemic immune activation. In summary, this study establishes that Akk amplifies the local CD8⁺ T cell response, sensitizing tumors to anti-PD-1 therapy, without inducing a systemic inflammatory response. These findings position Akk supplementation as a promising, targeted strategy to overcome PD-1 immunotherapy resistance of MSS-CRC with a favorable safety profile.

title: Provider Knowledge, Risk Perceptions, and Communication Readiness Drive Discussions about Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer: A National Survey of US Healthcare Providers.
authors: Butcher J, Fassler SA, Bedell J, Denison B, Dahlen H, Kadono M, et al.
journal: Diseases of the Colon and Rectum
abstract: The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer continues to increase among adults younger than 50 years, yet delays in diagnosis remain common. As an initial step of the Early-Onset Colorectal Cancer Awareness campaign, we evaluated U.S. healthcare providers' knowledge, attitudes, diagnostic practices, and perceived barriers related to the timely recognition and evaluation of early-onset colorectal cancer. This survey established baseline measures for a national early-onset colorectal cancer awareness campaign. We conducted a national cross-sectional survey of physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants practicing family medicine, internal medicine, emergency medicine/urgent care, and obstetrics and gynecology. The survey assessed early-onset colorectal cancer awareness, screening recommendations, evaluation of symptomatic younger adults, perceived barriers to diagnosis, and educational needs. Descriptive statistics summarized responses, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with guideline-concordant screening and diagnostic evaluation. A total of 277 providers completed the survey. Although 87% were concerned or very concerned about early-onset colorectal cancer and 82% reported increased concern over the preceding five years, providers identified substantial barriers to timely diagnosis. Approximately one-half reported that younger adults commonly experienced symptoms for four months or longer before seeking care. The most frequently cited barriers included patients expecting symptoms to resolve (84%), insurance and financial barriers (79%), reluctance to undergo colonoscopy (77%), and failure to recognize symptoms as serious (65%). Most providers (79%) identified additional guidance on early-onset colorectal cancer symptoms, risk factors, and diagnostic evaluation as the educational resource most likely to improve care. Despite widespread awareness of the increasing incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer, patient- and system-level barriers continue to delay diagnosis in younger adults. These findings identify opportunities for targeted education, clinical decision support, and health system interventions to promote timely evaluation of symptomatic patients and improve early detection of early-onset colorectal cancer. title: Diagnosis and Management of HIV-Associated Colitis.
authors: Fairen Oro C, Beresneva O
journal: Diseases of the Colon and Rectum
abstract: A 63-year-old male with a history of untreated HIV presented to the emergency room with acute on chronic watery diarrhea, weight loss, fatigue, fever and chills. His vital signs were within normal limits and his abdomen was soft, nondistended and tender to palpation in 4 quadrants without peritonitis. He did not have leukocytosis on presentation. CD4 count was 310. CT scan showed inflammatory changes in the rectum and sigmoid colon. Comprehensive infectious workup was negative for any pathogens including cytomegalovirus (CMV), cryptosporidium, chlamydia, gonorrhea, C. difficile, cryptococcus, tuberculosis (TB) and herpes simplex virus (HSV). Colonoscopy was performed and showed a continuous area of nonbleeding ulcerated mucosa in the rectum, sigmoid, descending and transverse colon (Fig. 1). Pancolonic biopsies revealed active colitis with focal areas of basal plasmacytosis and crypt branching in left colon, suggestive of acute on chronic colitis and possible ulcerative colitis (UC). Gastroenterology and infectious disease were consulted and patient was started on IV methylprednisolone for presumed UC flare. Over the next few weeks, the patient proceeded to develop melena as well as increased lower abdominal and pelvic pain with intermittent fevers despite IV steroid treatment. The patient was trialed on IV infliximab also without significant improvement. After several weeks of steroid and biologic treatment, he developed increased abdominal pain with tachycardia and hemodynamic instability. His examination was significant for peritonitis with abdominal distension concerning for fulminant colitis. Colorectal surgery was consulted and proceeded to do an emergent total abdominal colectomy and end ileostomy. Intraoperatively he was found to have a small anterior distal rectal perforation. The decision was made to drain this area widely with rectal drain and fecal diversion and start him on IV antibiotic therapy. His final pathology from the index operation showed ulceration and acute colitis. There was no chronic crypt architectural distortion such as crypt dropout, disarray, crypt branching or basal plasmacytosis that are often seen in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). There was also increased apoptotic bodies and mitoses that were not consistent with IBD. After reviewing the clinical presentation, his disease progression, and final pathology, the treating team diagnosed the patient with HIV-associated colitis.

title: Effect of a Single Subanesthetic Dose of Esketamine on Gastrointestinal Recovery After Laparoscopic Colorectal Cancer Surgery: A Randomized, Outcome-Assessor-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
authors: Zhang Z, Liu J, Xiang P, Feng Y, Chen X, Li X, et al.
abstract: Postoperative gastrointestinal dysfunction (POGD) and Postoperative gastrointestinal intolerance (POGI) remain a critical challenge in abdominal surgery, particularly for colorectal cancer patients undergoing laparoscopic procedures. Current evidence suggests anesthetic agents may influence gastrointestinal recovery, yet the impact of esketamine remains underexplored. This trial aimed to investigate whether intraoperative esketamine administration accelerates gastrointestinal function recovery. In this single-center, randomized, outcome-assessor -blind trial, 104 patients (aged 18-75, ASA I-III) scheduled for elective laparoscopic colorectal cancer surgery were allocated to receive either intravenous esketamine (0.2 mg/kg) or saline (control) 30 minutes before surgery completion. Primary outcome was time to first flatus; secondary outcomes included I-FEED scores, defecation time, oral intake tolerance, and postoperative complications assessed within seven days after surgery. The esketamine group demonstrated significantly shorter time to first flatus (52 [50.25-53.75] vs 60 [58.59-61.41] hours; P < 0.001) and first defecation (87 [81.96-92.04] vs 95 [92.65-97.35] hours; P = 0.04) compared to controls. I-FEED scores were markedly lower (median 1 [0.25-2] vs 2.5 [1-3]; P < 0.001), with reduced nausea (P = 0.001) and abdominal distension duration (P < 0.001). Esketamine also improved postoperative sleep quality, but did not affect hospitalization costs or length of stay. Intraoperative esketamine accelerates gastrointestinal function recovery after laparoscopic colorectal surgery, especially reducing postoperative gastrointestinal intolerance symptoms of nausea and distension while improving early sleep quality. However, no evident benefit was observed in reducing hospital length of stay or patient costs.

title: Quantitative dual-energy computed tomography parameters as imaging biomarkers for assessing the histopathologic grade of colorectal cancer.
authors: Ma T, Liu J, Wu M, Yu H, Liu S, Gao L
journal: Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents a major global healthcare burden. Tumor differentiation grade is a critical prognostic factor for evaluating patients with CRC. The objective of this study was to examine the value of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) quantitative parameters as imaging biomarkers for the preoperative prediction of histopathologic CRC grade. A total of 117 patients with pathologically confirmed CRC who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced DECT were enrolled and divided into low-grade (n=74) and high-grade (n=43) groups. Monoenergetic 74-keV images from the arterial phase (AP), venous phase (VP), and delayed phase (DP) were reconstructed as conventional 120 kVp-like computed tomography (CT) images. Lesion CT attenuation values, iodine concentration (IC), normalized iodine concentration (NIC), effective atomic number (Zeff), and extracellular volume (ECV) were measured in three phases by two radiologists, and clinical data were collected. Intergroup comparisons and Spearman correlation analyses were conducted to determine the associations between spectral parameters and the histopathologic grade of CRC, and multivariable logistic regression analyses were applied to identify independent correlates. Three types of predictive models were established: a baseline model incorporating clinical variables and CT attenuation values, a single spectral parameter model, and combined models integrating clinical features with different spectral parameters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and the DeLong test were used to compare the area under the curve (AUC) between the models. Bootstrap internal validation with 1,000 resamples was performed on the optimal model. Serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) concentration showed significant differences between the low-grade group and high-grade group (P=0.009), whereas triphasic 120 kVp-like CT attenuation values showed no statistical differences (P>0.05). For the AP, only IC differed significantly (P=0.011); for the VP and DP, IC, NIC, Zeff, and ECV differed significantly (P<0.05), with ECV showing the strongest correlation with histopathologic grade in CRC (r=0.650: P<0.001). Multivariable analysis identified VP IC [odds ratio (OR) =4.601; P=0.046] and ECV (OR =1.492; P<0.001) as independent correlates of high histopathologic grade in CRC, with AUCs of 0.749 and 0.889, respectively. The integrated model combining clinical indicators with VP and DP spectral parameters achieved the best performance for predicting high histopathologic grade in CRC [AUC =0.904, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.845-0.962; bias‑corrected AUC =0.904, 95% CI: 0.837-0.954], with an accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity of 85.5%, 88.4%, and 83.8%, respectively. The DeLong test revealed that this integrated model had significantly better diagnostic performance than did the baseline model (AUC =0.538; P<0.001), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed between the integrated model and the VP + DP dual-phase model (P=0.504). DECT quantitative parameters have potential clinical value for predicting the histopathologic grade of patients with CRC. They may serve as imaging biomarkers and provide valuable information for understanding tumor biological behavior.

title: Food Insecurity and Mortality From Digestive Tract Diseases in the United States.
authors: Ledenko M, Patel T
abstract: Food insecurity arising from insufficient access to food necessary for an active and healthy lifestyle is a prevalent yet underrecognized predictor of health that can increase the risk of chronic disorders. The impact of food insecurity on mortality rates from digestive tract diseases within the United States was analyzed. County-level age-standardized mortality rates for digestive tract diseases, encompassing both gastrointestinal tract and liver diseases, were obtained for 2015-2020 and linked to corresponding county-level measures of food insecurity, access to stores, enrollment in food programs, and other local variables. Separate analyses were performed for cancer and for noncancer conditions. Mortality rates from digestive diseases were significantly higher in counties within the highest compared to those with the lowest quintile of food insecurity. These associations remained positive when assessed separately for gastrointestinal tract or liver diseases, or for cancers and noncancer diseases. Food insecurity was associated with mortality from some cancers such as primary liver and colorectal cancers, but not for others such as esophageal or gallbladder cancer. Within food-insecure regions, factors such as younger age, population size and health, health care access, and economic factors were related to higher rates. Composite measures of social vulnerability or deprivation could identify locations with higher mortality. Food insecurity has a significant and detrimental association with mortality rates from digestive tract diseases. These findings emphasize the need to address food access with targeted interventions and for research on disease-specific impacts as crucial determinants of disease-related outcomes.

title: Molecular, spatial, and AI-enabled technologies for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response in locally advanced rectal cancer.
authors: Boot GF, Masotti C, Corrò C, Schraepen C, Williams HL, Wright TA, et al.
abstract: Pretreatment prediction of neoadjuvant response remains an unresolved challenge in locally advanced rectal cancer, where management is moving towards risk-adapted and response-oriented treatment strategies. Prediction remains difficult because response reflects interacting tumour-intrinsic, immune, stromal, and spatial processes that are incompletely captured by standard clinical and radiological assessment. From a technology-centred perspective, in this Review we assess how molecular, spatial, image-based, and artificial intelligence-enabled approaches are being used to study and predict response to neoadjuvant treatment from pretreatment biopsies and how readily they may be translated into clinical workflows. Genomic profiling has its clearest current clinical role in identifying hypermutated immune-responsive subgroups, whereas broader genomic, epigenomic, and immune-repertoire markers remain largely investigational. Bulk transcriptomics has generated multiple response signatures with variable reproducibility but has consistently highlighted immune activation, interferon signalling, stromal remodelling, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition as recurrent response-associated programmes; its most feasible clinical route is likely through targeted expression panels rather than open-ended transcriptome profiling. Higher-resolution approaches such as spatial transcriptomic and proteomic platforms refine these observations by localising signals to tumour, immune, and stromal compartments and capturing therapy-induced tissue reorganisation, but they are currently best positioned for deepening biological understanding and nominating rational treatment combinations for future testing. Established platforms such as digital pathology are closer to routine deployment as they build on clinically embedded workflows, although response-prediction algorithms still require robust external validation, calibration, and regulatory-grade implementation. Patient-derived models provide functional systems for testing candidate biomarkers and resistance mechanisms. Multimodal artificial intelligence may support response prediction by identifying complementary signals across data types and distilling complex signatures into parsimonious models suitable for clinical translation. Progress will depend on harmonised, longitudinal, multi-centre studies that couple biological depth with assay standardisation, model reduction, and prospective evidence that response predictors improve patient management. © 2026 The Author(s). title: Predictive value of genetic and morphological evaluation (GAME) score for outcomes after thermal ablation in patients with colorectal liver metastases.
authors: Kong Y, Yue X, Cao X, Tang F, Zhou X
journal: International Journal of Hyperthermia : the Official Journal of European Society for Hyperthermic Oncology, North American Hyperthermia Group
abstract: To evaluate the predictive value of the genetic and morphological evaluation (GAME) score for the prognosis of patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) receiving thermal ablation (TA) and compare it with the Fong score. We conducted a retrospective analysis of CRLM patients who underwent TA between January 2016 and December 2021 at two tertiary medical centers in China. Recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank testing. Prognostic variables associated with early recurrence (ER) and OS were identified through univariate and multivariate Cox regression, and nomograms were developed based on significant factors. Both the GAME and Fong scores effectively predicted RFS and OS in patients with CRLM undergoing TA treatment, though the GAME score showed superior discriminatory ability. Cox regression identified the largest liver metastasis diameter (HR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.29-0.69; The GAME score, which outperforms the Fong score in predicting the prognosis of patients with CRLM who meet the stringent eligibility criteria of this study and undergo TA, should be considered a preoperative prognostic tool.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies ENO3 as a Candidate Lactate Metabolism-Associated Biomarker in Colorectal Cancer Metastasis.
authors: Qian J, Wang M, Liu J, Gao M
abstract: Metastasis is the primary cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC), a leading global malignancy. Although metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer, the stage-associated transcriptional features of metabolic pathways during CRC progression remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize transcriptionally inferred metabolic heterogeneity during CRC progression and identify candidate molecular factors associated with metastasis. We performed an integrated transcriptomic analysis using TCGA and GEO datasets and compared metabolic pathway signatures across normal tissues, primary tumors, and metastatic lesions. An exploratory tumor lactate metabolism score (TLMS) was developed using Cox regression and LASSO analysis. Consensus clustering identified metabolic subtypes, and their associations with computationally estimated immune-cell signatures were assessed. The functional consequences of ENO3 loss were preliminarily evaluated using CRISPR/Cas9 knockout, cell proliferation assays, and an NSG tail-vein experimental lung colonization model. We observed a stage-associated reversal-like transcriptional pattern: primary tumors showed broad suppression of metabolic pathway signatures relative to normal tissues, whereas metastatic lesions showed reactivation of several signatures, including the pentose phosphate pathway. A six-gene lactate metabolism-related signature stratified patients into prognostic groups within the TCGA cohort. The high-risk group showed higher ssGSEA-inferred neutrophil abundance and enrichment of a neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-associated transcriptional signature. ENO3 expression was associated with poor outcome, while ENO3 knockout reduced MC38 cell proliferation and experimental lung colonization in NSG mice. CRC progression is accompanied by stage-associated changes in transcriptomically inferred metabolic programs. TLMS and ENO3 represent exploratory candidate biomarkers that require independent clinical validation and further mechanistic investigation, particularly with respect to lactate metabolism and the tumor immune microenvironment.
