title: Robotic colorectal cancer surgery: perioperative and oncological outcomes at a national referral center in Mexico.
authors: Aguilar-Romero JM, Vela-Sarmiento I, Melchor-Ruan J, Martinez-Said H, Aguilar-Frasco JL, Lino-Silva LS, et al.
abstract: Robotic colorectal surgery is increasingly used for technically demanding pelvic procedures, but contemporary cancer-specific experience from Latin American public oncology centers remains limited. To describe perioperative and pathological outcomes of a robotic colorectal cancer program at a national oncology referral center in Mexico. We retrospectively analyzed 75 consecutive patients who underwent robotic surgery for colorectal malignancy at the Instituto Nacional de Cancerología between June 2024 and March 2026. Colon and rectal cancer were analyzed as separate descriptive cohorts. Major morbidity was defined as Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher within 30 days. Fifty-seven patients (76.0%) had rectal cancer and 18 (24.0%) had colon cancer. No conversion to open surgery occurred (0/75; exact 95% CI 0-4.8%). Median operative time was 290 min (IQR 220-345), estimated blood loss 50 mL (IQR 30-100), and hospital stay 4 days (IQR 3-6). Major morbidity occurred in 13/75 patients (17.3%), reintervention in 12/75 (16.0%), and 30-day readmission in 12/75 (16.0%). Among rectal patients, 54/57 (94.7%) received total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) and 11/54 (20.4%) achieved pathological complete response. The circumferential resection margin was < 1 mm in 8/57 (14.0%). Mesorectal quality was complete in 41/57 (71.9%), nearly complete in 7/57 (12.3%), and incomplete in 9/57 (15.8%). Median lymph-node yield was 9 (IQR 6-12) for rectal cancer and 25.5 (IQR 16.25-32.25) for colon cancer. This series describes robotic colorectal cancer surgery within an established national oncology service, with a case mix dominated by low rectal procedures. The findings provide contemporary perioperative and pathological quality data for continued institutional audit; comparative studies and longer follow-up are required before conclusions regarding relative effectiveness can be made.
cn_title: 墨西哥国家转诊中心机器人结直肠癌手术的围手术期与肿瘤学结局
insight: 该研究描述了墨西哥国家癌症中心机器人结直肠癌手术的围手术期与病理结局，以直肠癌为主且多接受TNT，为拉丁美洲公共肿瘤中心提供了当代质量数据，但需对照研究验证其相对有效性。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性病例系列，样本量75例，无对照组，仅描述性结局，不足以改变临床实践。

title: Diffusion and geographic variation in robot-assisted colon resection after reimbursement in Japan: a nationwide billing-based analysis, 2022-2024.
authors: Omura T, Kamihara T
abstract: This study aimed to quantify how rapidly robot-assisted colon resection billing diffused after reimbursement in Japan and whether geographic variation narrowed as uptake expanded. We analyzed National Database (NDB) Open Data for fiscal years (FYs) 2022-2024. The primary outcome was the robot-assisted share of two laparoscopic billing categories for malignant colon tumor resection (robot-assisted and conventional). Variation across treating-institution prefectures was summarized using the interquartile range (IQR) for absolute spread and the coefficient of variation (CV) and Gini coefficient for relative dispersion. Longitudinal analyses included prefectures with unmasked values in all relevant years; FY2024 permitted a complete 47-prefecture cross-section. The national robot-assisted share rose from 3.38% in FY2022 to 11.40% in FY2023 and 19.55% in FY2024. In the common 33-prefecture panel, the IQR widened from 5.73 to 6.61 and 11.79 percentage points, whereas the CV fell from 1.086 to 0.630 and 0.482 and the Gini coefficient from 0.565 to 0.347 and 0.269. Across all 47 prefectures in FY2024, shares ranged from 0.00% to 41.47%; the complete cross-section was more heterogeneous than the restricted longitudinal panel, and the 14 prefectures excluded because of earlier masking had a lower median share (6.83% versus 18.05%). Rapid national growth did not translate into geographically uniform billing-based uptake. Relative dispersion decreased while absolute percentage-point spread widened, so apparent geographic convergence depended on the scale used. Post-reimbursement surveillance should report both dimensions and account for selection introduced by disclosure-related masking.
cn_title: 日本医保覆盖后机器人辅助结肠切除术的扩散与地域差异：2022-2024年全国医保账单分析
insight: 机器人结肠手术报销后3年内占比从3.4%升至19.6%，但绝对地域差距反而扩大，提示新技术推广需同步关注公平性。
grade_rationale: 基于全国医保账单数据库的大样本回顾性分析，揭示技术扩散规律，但为描述性卫生服务研究，不直接改变临床决策。

title: Single-Incision Plus One Robot-Assisted Abdominoperineal Resection Using the Hugo RAS System Through a Planned Stoma Site: A Novel Reduced-Port Robotic Surgery.
authors: Matsuda S, Itatani Y, Maeda M, Yamamoto T, Okamura R, Yoshida Y, et al.
abstract: Reduced-port surgery has been developed to minimize abdominal wall trauma while maintaining the benefits of minimally invasive surgery. However, reduced-port robotic rectal surgery remains technically challenging due to interference of external arms. The modular design of the Hugo RAS system (Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) provides greater flexibility in arm positioning to minimize external arm interference without compromising instrument maneuverability In abdominoperineal resection (APR), the incision for a permanent colostomy is inevitable. We report the first case of completely robot-assisted APR performed using the Hugo RAS system through a planned stoma site. Three robotic trocars were inserted through the planned left lower-quadrant stoma site, and one arm through the right lower quadrant. We call this approach SIPORS, Single-Incision Plus One Robot-assisted Surgery. The procedure is presented in the accompanying video. As the first case, a 50-year-old woman with rectal cancer underwent APR after systemic chemotherapy. The console time was 167 min. The procedure was completed without significant robotic arm interference. The postoperative course was uneventful except for transient cystitis. The circumferential and distal resection margins were 3 and 35 mm, respectively. The mesorectal specimen was complete, 25 lymph nodes were harvested, and the pathological stage was pT3N2bM1. SIPORS using the Hugo RAS at a planned stoma site was technically feasible and achieved an oncologically acceptable resection in this patient. It may offer improved cosmesis, reduced postoperative pain, fewer wound complications, and a lower risk of trocar-site incisional hernia. Further experience is needed to confirm its reproducibility and clinical benefits.
cn_title: 单孔加一机器人辅助腹会阴联合切除术：经计划造口部位应用Hugo RAS系统的首例报告
insight: 首次报道经计划造口部位行单孔加一机器人APR，为减少腹壁创伤提供新术式思路，但仅为个案，尚需验证其可重复性与肿瘤学安全性。
grade_rationale: 单例首次报道的技术可行性研究，无对照与随访，仅提示潜在优势，不足以改变临床实践。

title: Molecular characterization of colorectal cancer liver metastases with pure desmoplastic versus non-pure desmoplastic histopathological growth patterns using a targeted gene expression panel.
authors: Keil F, Lösch A, Mühlbauer M, Pukrop T, Blazquez R, Schlitt HJ, et al.
abstract: The histological growth pattern (HGP) at the interface of colorectal adenocarcinoma liver metastases (CRCLM) and liver parenchyma provides important prognostic information. This study aimed to identify transcriptomic signatures underlying the predominant HGPs in CRCLM. We retrospectively evaluated the HGP of 495 CRCLM of 232 patients with metastasectomy at the University Hospital Regensburg between 2003 and 2016. A representative subset of 106 metastases from 53 patients was analyzed for RNA expression at the metastasis-liver interface using the NanoString nCounter® PanCancer Progression Panel. The most common HGPs in the NanoString subcohort were the infiltrative replacement (rHGP, 47.2%) and the non-infiltrative desmoplastic type (dHGP, 46.3%). Unsupervised clustering of CRCLM gene expression profiles identified four gene clusters, two significantly enriched for pure dHGP or pure rHGP. Differential expression analysis between pure dHGP and all other HGPs (i.e., non-pure dHGP) identified 55 significantly differentially expressed genes. Gene set enrichment analysis corroborated previously reported signals (extracellular matrix organization, stromal/endothelial gene sets, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition enrichment in pure dHGP; glucose metabolism in non-pure dHGP) and additionally revealed α6β4 integrin signaling as feature of non-pure dHGP. Patient identity, rather than HGP, was the dominant driver of gene expression variance, though AGR2 was consistently and significantly overexpressed in non-pure dHGP across different analytical strategies. These findings corroborate known transcriptomic differences between HGPs, identify α6β4 integrin signaling as an additional candidate pathway enriched in non-pure dHGP CRCLM, and underscore the substantial contribution of patient-specific factors to gene expression variability in CRCLM outweighing HGP.
cn_title: 结直肠癌肝转移纯促纤维增生型与非纯促纤维增生型组织学生长模式的分子特征：基于靶向基因表达面板的分析
insight: 本研究揭示纯促纤维增生型与非纯促纤维增生型肝转移灶的转录组差异，并发现α6β4整合素信号通路及AGR2作为潜在标志物，提示患者个体因素对基因表达变异的影响超过生长模式，为肝转移精准分型提供新线索。
grade_rationale: 基于靶向基因表达面板的回顾性转化研究，样本量中等，发现新候选通路但未外部验证，暂不足以改变临床实践。

title: Single-port robotic and conventional multiport laparoscopic colectomy for colon cancer: an overlap-weighted comparison of perioperative and oncologic outcomes.
authors: Jo MH, Lee HA, Kim HS, Chung SS, Noh GT
abstract: Comparative evidence for single-port colectomy with robotic system remains limited, particularly for long-term cancer control. We compared perioperative recovery and oncologic outcomes following single-port robotic surgery (SPRS) and conventional multiport laparoscopic surgery (CMLS) in colon cancer. This retrospective study screened 710 patients treated surgically between March 2019 and February 2025. The analytic cohort was balanced with propensity score overlap weighting (PSOW), after which operative, postoperative, pathologic, and survival data were compared. The analysis included 472 patients (142 SPRS and 330 CMLS). PSOW balanced the four covariates specified in the propensity model. SPRS had a longer mean operative time (255.0 vs. 197.5 min, p < 0.001), but no patient required open conversion (0.0% vs. 3.1%, p = 0.011). Compared with CMLS, SPRS was followed by earlier passage of flatus (2.4 vs. 3.4 days), earlier tolerance of a soft diet (3.3 vs. 4.8 days), and a shorter postoperative stay (7.5 vs. 8.5 days) (all p ≤ 0.001). Pain scores through postoperative day 5 were lower after SPRS (all p < 0.001), whereas complication rates and pathologic measures were similar. Three-year relapse-free survival (RFS) was 95.2% after SPRS and 95.1% after CMLS (p = 0.835); the corresponding overall survival (OS) were 97.2% and 94.8% (p = 0.104). Surgical modality was not an independent predictor of RFS or OS. Within the available follow-up, SPRS provided oncologic results comparable to CMLS while being associated with less postoperative pain and enhanced recovery. These data support SPRS as a feasible approach for selected patients with colon cancer.
cn_title: 单孔机器人与传统多孔腹腔镜结肠癌根治术的围手术期及肿瘤学结局比较
insight: 单孔机器人结肠癌手术可加速康复、减轻疼痛且肿瘤学结局不劣于多孔腹腔镜，为微创术式选择提供新证据，但对肝转移等晚期肠癌的适用性尚需验证。
grade_rationale: 回顾性单中心研究，样本量中等（472例），虽采用PSOW平衡混杂，但证据等级不足以直接改变指南。

title: Anesthesiological considerations and complications in robotic surgery: a retrospective analysis.
authors: Kuhn P, Oremek M, Kuenster AL, Labonte A, Kroeplin M, Vilz TO, et al.
abstract: Robotic-assisted surgery has become increasingly prevalent across various surgical disciplines. Understanding anesthesiological factors influencing perioperative outcome is essential for optimizing patient care. This retrospective analysis evaluated 200 patients who underwent robotic surgery across three surgical categories: gastrointestinal (GI, n=60), hepatopancreticobiliary (HPB, n=28), and colorectal (n=112) procedures. We conducted an exploratory analysis of associations between anesthesiological parameters-including fluid management, surgical duration, and blood loss-and clinical outcomes such as intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, total hospital length of stay, complication severity (Clavien-Dindo classification) using univariable and multivariable regression models. The exploratory analyses suggested potential associations between surgical duration and outcomes across surgical specialties in multivariable analysis. For GI procedures, longer surgical duration was associated with higher odds of severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III; OR = 1.80 (1.21, 2.66)). In colorectal surgery, surgical duration was independently associated with both development of severe complications (OR = 1.28 (1.01, 1.62)) and total hospital length of stay (log-scale, β = 0.08 (0.03, 0.12)). Fluid intake was associated with an increased hospital length of stay in colorectal surgery (log-scale, β = 0.10 (0.03, 0.17)). Anesthesiological management, particularly surgical duration and fluid management, showed associations with perioperative outcomes in robotic surgery. The estimated effects provide preliminary insights into the magnitude of these associations and may serve as a basis for hypothesis generation and the design of future prospective studies. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to investigate the potential clinical relevance of anesthesiological and perioperative management strategies.
cn_title: 机器人手术的麻醉学考量与并发症：一项回顾性分析
insight: 该研究提示机器人结直肠手术中手术时长和液体管理可能与围手术期结局相关，为肠癌机器人手术的麻醉优化提供了假设生成依据。
grade_rationale: 单中心回顾性探索性分析，样本量有限（n=200），仅能提示关联，不足以改变临床实践。

title: Augmenting colonoscopy with artificial intelligence and robotic assistance: a human-factors scoping review toward a task-based shared autonomy paradigm.
authors: Manfredi L, Annicchiarico A, Gravante G
abstract: Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention but remains a high-demand psychomotor and cognitive procedure, characterized by operator dependency, variable performance, and substantial physical and mental workload. Increasing evidence links procedural quality and safety to clinician-related factors, including musculoskeletal strain, fatigue, and non-technical skills. Concurrently, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic technologies are emerging as potential tools to address these limitations. We conducted a scoping review with narrative synthesis of literature on human factors, ergonomics, AI, robotic technologies, and shared autonomy in colonoscopy and surgical robotics. Evidence synthesis: Colonoscopy performance remains limited by non-negligible miss rates and variability driven by both technical and human factors. Ergonomic constraints and cognitive workload contribute significantly to operator strain and may affect vigilance and decision-making. AI systems-including computer-aided detection (CADe), diagnosis (CADx), and quality monitoring-have demonstrated improvements in detection metrics and procedural standardisation, although concerns regarding cognitive offloading and potential deskilling persist. In parallel, emerging robotic and soft-robotic platforms aim to enhance navigation, improve procedural ergonomics, and reduce operator musculoskeletal strain, although clinical evidence remains limited. These technologies converge within a task-based shared-autonomy paradigm integrating physical, perceptual, and cognitive augmentation, with different procedural tasks operating at different levels of human-system control. A task-based shared-autonomy framework may provide a coherent model for integrating AI and robotics into colonoscopy while preserving human supervision and clinical judgement. Future developments should prioritise human-centred design, workflow integration, and multidimensional evaluation strategies to ensure safe and effective clinical implementation.
cn_title: 人工智能与机器人辅助结肠镜的人因学范围综述：迈向任务导向共享自主范式
insight: 提出任务导向共享自主框架整合AI与机器人辅助结肠镜，强调人因工程与认知负荷，为提升肠癌筛查质量与安全提供新范式。
grade_rationale: 范围综述与叙事性综合，非系统定量证据，但提出整合框架具方向性启示，尚不足以直接改变实践。

title: A dual-site oral nanovaccine programs anti-colorectal tumor immunity from small intestinal priming to large intestinal boosting.
authors: Yang K, Xu H, Liu G, Bao S, Yang Q, Gao Q, et al.
abstract: Oral vaccines hold great promise for colorectal cancer (CRC) immunotherapy but are limited by inefficient mucosal delivery and a lack of spatiotemporal control over immune activation. Here we report a spatiotemporally programmed oral nanovaccine that implements a dual-site vaccination strategy through a sequential and causally linked immune cascade, initiating immune priming in Peyer's patches of the small intestine and subsequently amplifying immunity at colorectal tumor sites. The nanovaccine (DPML@OVA-CpG), composed of antigen- and CpG-loaded mesoporous polydopamine nanoparticles stabilized by β-glucan and plant-derived lipids, resists gastrointestinal degradation and targets gut-associated lymphoid tissues. Following oral administration, it induces robust systemic effector and memory T cell responses via small intestinal priming, while a fraction traffics to colorectal tumors. There, near-infrared irradiation triggers immunogenic cell death of tumor cells and, together with locally released CpG, converts tumors into autologous in situ vaccine factories. This spatiotemporally orchestrated strategy achieves potent therapeutic efficacy against liver metastatic CRC, extending survival compared to PD-L1 antibody therapy and traditional single-site oral vaccination.
cn_title: 双位点口服纳米疫苗：从小肠致敏到大肠增强的程序化抗结直肠癌免疫
insight: 该研究提出双位点口服纳米疫苗策略，实现小肠致敏与肿瘤局部增强的时空免疫级联，为结直肠癌肝转移提供新型免疫治疗思路。
grade_rationale: 研究为临床前动物实验，机制创新性强但尚未进入临床验证，暂不具备实践改变潜力。

title: Outcomes of Total Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: A Prospective Observational Real-World Cohort in Johannesburg, South Africa
authors: Amod, S.; Tunmer, M.; Campbell-Roper, L.; Demetriou, G.; Gaylard, P.; Krawitz, T.; Kruger, D.; Fabian, J.; Harran, N.
abstract: BackgroundTotal neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) is increasingly used for treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) to improve treatment compliance, oncological outcomes and opportunities for organ preservation. However, evidence describing its implementation and outcomes in low- and middle-income countries remains limited. This study evaluated the feasibility, treatment delivery, oncological outcomes and organ preservation outcomes of TNT in a real-world South African setting. MethodsThis was a retrospective review of a prospective cohort of adults with histologically confirmed, non-metastatic LARC treated with TNT at the Wits Donald Gordon Medical Centre, Johannesburg, between March 2022 and January 2026. Treatment was individualised following multidisciplinary review and included induction and/or consolidation systemic chemotherapy with either long- or short-course radiotherapy. Following TNT, treatment response was assessed clinically, endoscopically and radiologically. Patients with a clinical complete response (cCR) were offered watch-and-wait (WW) surveillance, while those with an incomplete response were recommended for total mesorectal excision (TME). The primary outcome was organ preservation, assessed as TME-free survival. Secondary outcomes included tumour regrowth, disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and local recurrence-free survival (LRFS) following TME. ResultsForty-six patients were included; median age was 63 years, 67.4% were male, 82.6% had T3-T4 tumours and 80.4% had node-positive disease. TNT was completed as planned in 95.7% of patients. Grade [≥]3 toxicity occurred in 19.5% during chemotherapy and 8.9% during radiotherapy. Twenty-one patients (45.7%) achieved a cCR and entered WW surveillance. TME-free survival was 46% (95% CI 31-60) at 1-year and 18% (95% CI 8-32) at 3-years. Three-year OS and DFS were 87% (95% CI 64-96) and 76% (95% CI 53-89), respectively. Among patients managed with WW, 3-year regrowth-free survival was 53% (95% CI 26-75). Three-year LRFS following TME was 94% (95% CI 68-99), and all patients undergoing TME or completed salvage surgery achieved an R0 resection. ConclusionTNT was feasible and well tolerated in this real-world South African cohort, with high treatment completion and favourable medium-term oncological outcomes. Although almost half of patients initially achieved a cCR, declining TME-free and regrowth-free survival demonstrated that durable organ preservation was less frequent, highlighting the importance of structured surveillance and timely access to salvage surgery. These findings support the feasibility of delivering contemporary multimodal rectal cancer care in an appropriately resourced African setting.
cn_title: 南非约翰内斯堡局部晚期直肠癌全程新辅助治疗的前瞻性真实世界队列结局
insight: 在资源有限的非洲真实世界环境中证实TNT可行且耐受良好，但持久保肛率有限，提示需结构化监测与及时挽救手术，为肠癌TNT推广提供中低收入国家证据。
grade_rationale: 预印本未经同行评审，不参与分级

title: Decision models can offload structured clinical tasks from large language models
authors: Ariel, D.; Laban, G.; Endelman, S.; Balicer, R.; Dagan, N.; Cohen, S.
abstract: Decision models like Jev read text and return probabilities, categories, or ordinal levels, with confidence scores for the latter two, at a fraction of large language models (LLMs) cost. We explored how Jev could be integrated into clinical workflows for all these output types: mortality risk estimation, categorical Choosing-Wisely decisions for patient questions, and ordinal colon cancer staging. With standard LLM-style inputs, Jev trailed five flagship LLMs: mortality AUROC was 0.822 versus 0.837-0.846; Choosing-Wisely accuracy, 87.7% versus 98.4-100%; and staging accuracy, 45.4% versus 94.2-100%. Developer-recommended input alterations improved staging accuracy to 75.8% with medical context, 82.1% with task decomposition, and 85.8% with both. None of Jevs staging errors had full confidence. Using Jev for fully confident staging decisions and LLMs for the rest was non-inferior to each LLM alone and cut flagship LLM costs by 33-44%. Prompted as designed, decision models may efficiently share structured clinical tasks with LLMs.
cn_title: 决策模型可分担大语言模型的结构化临床任务
insight: 专用决策模型Jev在结肠癌分期等结构化任务上可替代部分LLM调用，混合策略不劣于单用LLM并降本33-44%，提示肠癌AI工作流可分层部署。
grade_rationale: 预印本未经同行评审，不参与分级

title: Replacing animal-sourced with plant-sourced proteins alters gut microbiota and biomarkers associated with colorectal cancer risk in healthy adults: A randomized feeding study
authors: Jian, C.; Pellinen, T.; Karkman, A.; Neuvonen, M.; Niemi, M.; Salonen, A.; Pajari, A.-M.
abstract: Epidemiological studies associate replacing animal-sourced with plant-sourced protein with lower colorectal cancer (CRC) risk, but controlled feeding studies have rarely tested how this substitution alters the gut microbiota and CRC-related biomarkers. In a 12-week randomized controlled feeding study, 136 healthy adults consumed diets providing 30 energy percent (E%), 50 E%, or 70 E% of protein from plant sources. Change in gut microbiota composition was the primary outcome; stool characteristics, fecal N-nitroso compounds (NOCs), and fecal and plasma bile acids (BAs) were secondary outcomes. The 70% plant-protein diet significantly restructured the gut microbiota, increasing fiber-associated Lachnospiraceae and Roseburia while reducing Methanobrevibacter and several asaccharolytic taxa. Microbial functional potential shifted toward plant-carbohydrate degradation, with lower amino acid degradation and methanogenesis. Fecal pH decreased, stool characteristics suggested faster colonic transit, and potentially carcinogenic total and haem-derived NOCs declined progressively with plant-protein replacement. The 70% plant-protein diet also reduced fecal secondary and taurine-conjugated BAs, including the CRC-associated BAs DCA and LCA. Plasma glucuronidated BAs increased, expanding the circulating pool of readily excreted BA conjugates. Higher insoluble fiber intake was associated with greater microbiota restructuring and lower fecal NOCs. Methanogen carriers had higher baseline fecal NOCs and features of slower colonic transit, and showed weaker microbiota and less favorable BA responses to the 70% plant-protein diet. Baseline methanogen carriage thus could be exploited for participant stratification in future dietary interventions. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03206827.
cn_title: 用植物蛋白替代动物蛋白改变健康成人肠道菌群及结直肠癌风险相关生物标志物：一项随机喂养研究
insight: 随机对照喂养研究证实高比例植物蛋白饮食可重塑肠道菌群、降低粪便NOCs和致癌性胆汁酸，为饮食干预降低肠癌风险提供机制证据，并提示产甲烷菌携带者可作为分层因素。
grade_rationale: 预印本未经同行评审，不参与分级

title: Quantifying Cancer Clinical Trial Eligibility Using Artificial Intelligence-Based Matching
authors: Goel, K. P.; Myall, N. J.; Dickerson, J.; Caswell-Jin, J. L.; Johnson, T.; Worth, J. E.; Gensheimer, M. F.
abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and validate an artificial intelligence-enabled platform that combines efficient screening with explicit eligibility logic by converting unstructured cancer trial criteria into reusable structured queries, and illustrates potential eligibility using synthetic patients. METHODS: We downloaded actively recruiting US interventional treatment trials for advanced/metastatic breast cancer, colon cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer from ClinicalTrials.gov. Medical oncologists created 24 synthetic patient vignettes. A large language model converted trial eligibility criteria into Structured Query Language (SQL) code and patient information into structured records, enabling rule-based matching without further LLM inference. Cancer details and treatment history were considered, but not laboratory results or comorbidities. Validation included physician editing of generated eligibility code for 30 trials and independent assessments by two physicians, followed by consensus adjudication, for eligibility across ten trials. We descriptively summarized potential eligibility by trial characteristics and when varying age, ECOG performance status, sex, and ZIP code. RESULTS: Of 833 candidate trials, 746 met inclusion criteria. Performing matching for all 746 trials took a median of 0.459 seconds per patient, excluding patient-data preparation. Against physician consensus, automated matching agreed on 230/240 patient-trial pairs (95.8%; sensitivity 83.3%, specificity 100%). Across synthetic patients, potentially eligible trials ranged from 10 to 258 without geographic restrictions. Counts decreased with worse performance status and geographic restriction and were relatively stable across ages 30-90. Later-phase, randomized, and molecularly selective trials generally matched fewer vignettes. CONCLUSION: LLM-generated SQL enables rapid, explicit rule-based screening for potential trial eligibility. Evaluation in synthetic vignettes supports feasibility, while missed matches underscore the need for further validation.
cn_title: 基于人工智能匹配量化癌症临床试验资格
insight: 该研究利用大语言模型将试验标准转化为结构化查询，实现快速、可解释的资格筛查，为肠癌临床试验匹配提供新工具，但需进一步验证以减少漏匹配。
grade_rationale: 预印本未经同行评审，不参与分级

title: Novel adenoma-immune phenotypes are associated with risk of metachronous polyps and colorectal cancer in a bowel screening cohort
authors: McSorley, S. T.; Iwata, T.; Ammar, A.; Al-Badran, S. S.; Irvine, L.; Kennedy-Dietrich, C.; Legrini, A.; DeKoning, M.; Fisher, N.; Parsons, E. C.; Dunne, P.; Sampson, C.; Reines March, G.; Maka, N.; Jamieson, N. B.; Johnstone, M. S.; Lynch, G.; Edwards, J.
abstract: BackgroundCurrent British Society of Gastroenterology (BSG) guidelines misclassify metachronous lesion risk after polypectomy in approximately 40% of patients. Building on evidence that immune exclusion drives progression of adenomas to colorectal cancer, this study examined immune profiles in screen-detected adenomas as a predictive biomarker for metachronous lesion risk. MethodsPatients undergoing polypectomy within the Scottish Bowel Screening Programme, with surveillance colonoscopy between 6 months and 6 years were included (n=2642). Chromogenic immunohistochemistry (IHC; n=2466), 6-plex multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF; n=331), and spatially resolved 6000-plex single cell transcriptomics (n=7) were applied to adenoma microarrays. Cell density and location were measured using QuPath. Hierarchical then K-means clustering was used to define immune cell density-based clusters, which were compared to future lesion events using Kaplan-Meier curves and the log rank test. ResultsAfter adjustment for age, sex, site, size and dysplasia, adenoma CD3+ T cell density was significantly associated with future colorectal neoplasia (OR 1.44, 95% CI 1.20-1.72, p<0.001). Using mIF three immune cell density clusters were identified; 1) high T cell density, low macrophage density, 2) low T cell density, low macrophage density, and 3) high T cell, macrophage and SMA density, with significant differences in future lesion risk (Cluster 1: 22%, Cluster 2: 41%, Cluster 3: 36%, p=0.032). Bulk RNAseq and spatial transcriptomic analysis revealed significant variation in T cell and macrophage co-location and gene expression profiles between clusters. ConclusionAdenoma immune contexture emerges as a possible determinant of future metachronous lesion risk, offering a novel biomarker to refine surveillance.

title: Microbial Invasion and Immunosuppression Drives Adenoma Progression in Early Colorectal Cancer Development
authors: Liang, W.; Falk, L.; Lucarelli, D.; Putze, P.; Metwaly, A.; Zheng, Y.; Springer, F.; Winogrodzki, T.; Chan, Q.; Pauli, T. M.; Zhang, Y.; Zeller, G.; Meier, M.; Schnieke, A.; Ebner, F.; Haller, D.; Flisikowska, T.; Saur, D.; Flisikowski, K.
abstract: Several inherited predispositions to colorectal cancer exist, most notably familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), which typically involves a germline loss-of-function mutation in one APC allele. A second hit in APC or related loci leads to aberrant Wnt signalling, triggering adenoma formation with near-complete penetrance. Yet, substantial variability in disease onset and severity, even among siblings with identical APC germline mutations, implicates environmental modifiers. Emerging evidence points to the gut microbiome as a critical regulator of adenoma initiation and progression, particularly in early-onset CRC. Here, we show that bacterial invasion is associated with neutrophil immunosuppression, T-cell exclusion and adenoma progression in a porcine model of FAP. Longitudinal mapping of progressing and regressing polyps using single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and integrated microbiome profiling resolved the cellular and microbial architecture underlying these divergent lesion states. Single-cell RNA-seq identified 35 cell subpopulations and showed that regressing polyps are enriched for central-memory CD4+ T cells, cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and inflammatory neutrophils, whereas progressing polyps contain immunosuppressive/PD-L1-associated neutrophils, regulatory and dysfunctional T cells. Spatial transcriptomics with a custom host panel and targeted bacterial probes linked bacterial-high adenomatous regions to immunosuppressive neutrophil niches and T cell exclusion, while regressing lesions showed predominantly lumen-adjacent bacterial localization and spatially organized immune surveillance. These results provide a spatially resolved map of cellular and microbial organisation in early colorectal polyp progression and regression and reveal a microbiome-driven, neutrophil-mediated mechanism of early tumour progression with implications for CRC interception.
cn_title: 微生物侵袭与免疫抑制驱动早期结直肠癌腺瘤进展

title: Positive selection and structural disruption of KCNA5 by mutation in colorectal cancer
authors: Xu, B.; Shorthouse, D.
abstract: Ion channels regulate cell proliferation, survival and migration, but the functional consequences of many ion channel mutations in cancer are unknown, and electrophysiological characterisation at scale is impractical. Here we use the mutational landscape of colorectal adenocarcinoma as a functional filter to identify potassium channel mutations under selection. A dN/dS screen of 16 potassium channels expressed in the large intestine identified KCNA5 (Kv1.5) as the strongest candidate under positive mutational selection. These mutations cluster in the T1 tetramerisation, S1-S4 voltage-sensor and pore domains, yet avoid the selectivity filter, indicating that selection does not favour loss of conduction. Within the pore region, the observed mutations occupy a biophysical space distinct from known C-type inactivation, activation-gate and toxin-binding mutations. In the voltage sensor, mutations affect gating-charge arginines. In the T1 domain, mutations fall on inter-subunit interfaces conserved across the KCNA family, and saturation mutagenesis energy calculations predict that they destabilise subunit contacts or the folding of the domain. Molecular dynamics simulations of D166N and G128R show loss of coordinated interface dynamics and distortion of the local backbone, respectively. Transcriptomic analysis of KCNA5-mutant tumours shows reduced expression of cell-cycle, KRAS-related and inflammatory pathways, and we observe differences between transcriptional effects induced by T1 and S1-S4 domain mutations. These changes are not reproduced by low KCNA5 expression alone, consistent with an effect specific to the mutant protein. Together, these computational results highlight that KCNA5 is under mutational selection in colorectal adenocarcinoma, and that these mutations are likely functional and induce phenotypic effects on tumors.
cn_title: 结直肠癌中KCNA5的正向选择及突变导致的结构破坏
insight: 该研究揭示KCNA5在结直肠癌中受正向选择，突变通过破坏通道结构而非简单功能丧失影响肿瘤表型，为离子通道突变的功能解读提供新范式，提示KCNA5突变可能作为肠癌分子分型或治疗靶点。

title: Spatiotemporal profiling of T cell repertoires in Lynch syndrome reveals convergent immune responses through neoplastic progression
authors: Edwards, P.; Swinyard, O.; Ronel, T.; Jiang, Y.; Nageswaran, G.; Sakr, C.; Yasmin, S.; Grant, H.; Smith, E.; Braeutigam, K.; Braeutigam, K.; Varughese, S.; Datt, P.; Martinez, A.; Fisher, J.; Chain, B.; Shiu, K. K.; Jansen, M.; Baker, A.-M.; Monahan, K. J.; Graham, T. A.
abstract: Surveillance of individuals with Lynch syndrome (LS), who are carriers of heterozygous inactivating mismatch repair (MMR) gene mutations that predispose to colorectal cancer, enables the study of tumour-immune coevolution during tumour initiation. Somatic loss of MMR activity in the LS colon leads to the accrual of cancer driver mutations, and also of neoantigens likely to generate an adaptive immune response. However, the spatial and temporal immune dynamics in colon and peripheral blood are uncharacterised. Here we show that the neoplastic evolution of mismatch repair deficient (MMRd) clones leads to large-scale and sustained reorganisation of the T-cell repertoire in colon and peripheral blood. We performed dense spatiotemporal profiling of T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires from 109 colonic biopsies (11 tumour samples, 98 normal bowel) from seven individuals, with eight matched blood repertoires. We additionally analysed 13 colorectal polyp repertoires from eight participants, 286 cross sectional blood repertoires from 242 participants (198 LS and 44 non-LS) and 52 longitudinal peripheral blood samples from 26 individuals with LS. We detected tumour-associated T cell clones, some of which were widely present in normal bowel tissue and also detectable in peripheral blood. Sequence similarity analysis revealed conserved TCR architectures across tissue compartments and recurrent clustering patterns between patients, that were not present in non-Lynch controls, consistent with convergent MMRd-associated antigen-driven immune selection. We identified systemic signatures associated with local tumour immune activity and revealed evidence of structured repertoire remodelling before overt malignancy. Longitudinal profiling revealed frequent turnover of low-abundance clonotypes, whereas highly abundant clonotypes persisted for several years. Collectively, our data defines the local and circulating TCR landscape associated with colonic neoplasia in LS, and provides a framework for LS blood-based immune monitoring, early interception and biomarker development.
cn_title: 林奇综合征结直肠癌变过程中T细胞受体库的时空动态图谱
insight: 该研究揭示林奇综合征结直肠肿瘤发生过程中T细胞受体库在肠道和外周血中的时空重塑规律，为基于血液的免疫监测和早期干预提供了新框架。

title: PRC2-binding regions are hotspots of DNA methylation entropy in pre-cancer and cancer
authors: Bukovec, D.; Misheva, M. S.; Gjorgjievska, M.; Kungulovski, G.
abstract: DNA methylation aberrations and variability are pervasive features of cancer, yet their relationship with chromatin regulation remains incompletely understood. Across hundreds of matched tumor-normal methylomes, regions with the highest methylation entropy in both tumor and normal tissues were consistently enriched for PRC2-associated factors. In tumors, inter-sample methylation variability was increased across the full range of PRC2-associated levels, while mean methylation progressively increased from low- to high-PRC2-binding regions; this gradient was substantially weaker in matched normal tissues. PRC2-associated regions with higher DNA methylation levels were preferentially associated with poised and repressed chromatin states, reduced chromatin accessibility, and reduced gene expression. Independent normal-precancer-cancer cohorts showed that this PRC2-associated methylation state emerges early, with precancerous and malignant tissues displaying highly similar profiles that are distinct from those of healthy tissues. Single-cell colon cancer methylomes independently confirmed increased methylation entropy at PRC2 regions. Higher PRC2-region entropy was associated with scores reflecting hypoxic states, aggressive tumor features, and poorer survival outcomes. Collectively, these findings identify PRC2-binding regions as hotspots of DNA methylation variability that become dysregulated during tumorigenesis.
cn_title: PRC2结合区域是癌前及癌变过程中DNA甲基化熵的热点
insight: 该研究揭示PRC2结合区是DNA甲基化熵热点，在癌前阶段即出现异常，并与缺氧、侵袭性及不良预后相关，为肠癌早期干预和预后评估提供新视角。

title: A role for CIZ1, a Nuclear Matrix Protein Overexpressed in Cancer Cells, in Controlling the Initiation of DNA Replication
authors: Hossain, M.; Tramantano, M.; Naik, S.; Stillman, B.
abstract: DNA replication licensing is tightly coordinated with cell-cycle progression to ensure genome stability. Here we demonstrate that CIZ1, a nuclear matrix scaffold protein in human cells, coordinates DNA replication licensing through direct interactions with the Origin Recognition Complex (ORC), CDC6, and Cyclins E/A-CDK2. The C-terminal zinc finger region of CIZ1 mediates binding to the cyclin-binding motifs of ORC1 and CDC6, and Cyclin -CDK-dependent phosphorylation regulates these interactions. Cell cycle analyses demonstrated a dynamic association of CIZ1 with ORC1 and CDC6. Functional studies showed that CIZ1 depletion impaired MCM loading, reduced DNA synthesis, delayed S-phase progression and inhibited cell proliferation. Cancer cells overexpressing CIZ1 exhibited an enhanced dependency on its expression, and CRISPR tiling screens identified the C-terminal regulatory region containing cyclin-binding motifs and CDK phosphorylation sites as essential for cell proliferation. Acute degradation of CIZ1 further revealed an unexpected role in maintaining CCCTC-binding factor (CTCF) occupancy at specific genomic loci and regulating transcriptional programs associated with cell adhesion and migration, indicating that CIZ1 links DNA replication with higher-order genome organization. Finally, depletion of CIZ1 significantly suppressed colorectal tumor growth in xenograft models. Together, these findings establish CIZ1 as a multifunctional scaffold that integrates DNA replication licensing, Cyclin -CDK signaling, and chromatin architecture.

title: Deep-learning-driven tumor microenvironment profiling improves immunotherapy response prediction
authors: Wang, R. H.; Benard, B. A.; Ilerten, I.; Zdravkovic, S.; Al-Humadi, R.; Nasr, S.; Howitt, B.; Gentles, A. J.
abstract: Immunotherapy has transformed the management of many cancers, such as clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), yet durable clinical benefit is achieved in only a subset of patients. Immunotherapy outcomes are governed by the multicellular tumor microenvironment (TME), through the structured and directional interplay of regulatory programs and ligand-receptor communications. Yet most existing methods for immunotherapy response prediction rely on independent signatures or cell types and fail to model the structured and directional signaling network within the TME. To address this gap, we introduce EcoNet, a computational framework that first models ecosystems consisting of co-occurring cell states, then constructs intercellular and intracellular signaling networks based on the ecosystems, and applies a graph attention network to derive embeddings from the signaling network for immunotherapy response prediction. Pretrained on 2,532 pan-cancer immunotherapy samples across multiple cohorts, EcoNet outperformed existing prediction methods by 7.5-19.9% and marker-based signatures by 4.4-21.2% in AUC, and its high-attention genes were enriched among those required for T-cell-mediated tumor killing in an independent CRISPR screen; applied to ccRCC with disease-specific fine-tuning, it stratified an independent ccRCC cohort by clinical outcome (P=0.024). Biologically, high-attention genes capture an interferon-responsive program that enhances antigen presentation and immune infiltration. To validate these findings, we curated a ccRCC clinical cohort profiled with CosMx single-cell spatial transcriptomics (46 samples, ~450,000 cells) and found the response-associated TME configuration identified by EcoNet localized to immune-enriched niches, supporting the response stratification. These results establish EcoNet as a generalizable framework for TME-informed therapeutic response prediction, readily extensible to other cancer types and therapeutic contexts.
cn_title: 深度学习驱动的肿瘤微环境图谱提升免疫治疗反应预测

title: An RFX-driven ciliogenic cell state defines ex vivo FGFR-inhibitor sensitivity in colorectal cancer
authors: Kralickova, L.; Miglino, N.; Esposito, C.; Pfaendler, R.; Wegmann, R.; Ballesteros Cuartero, P.; Mena, J.; Panebianco, F.; Boos, L. A.; Richter, U.; Rahimzadeh, P.; Mehra, T.; Koelzer, V. H.; Piscuoglio, S.; Wicki, A.; Snijder, B.
abstract: Genomic stratification leaves most patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) without opportunities for targeted therapy. Seeking tumour state-linked drug sensitivities, we combined image-based ex vivo drug profiling with matched transcriptomics in 127 prospectively collected patient biopsies across CRC stages and molecular subtypes. Network-level integration identified a ciliogenic cell state defined by upregulation of cilia related genes with selective sensitivity to the FGFR inhibitor erdafitinib. This ciliogenic signature was associated with poor progression-free survival (hazard ratio 2.28; adjusted p=0.0098), even in early-stage colorectal cancer. Furthermore, knockdown of the transcriptional regulators RFX2 and RFX3, upstream of the ciliogenic cell state, attenuated erdafitinib sensitivity. Orthogonal bulk and single-cell analyses across normal, primary and metastatic tissues contextualised the ciliogenic programme along a transition from canonical epithelial states towards fetal and non-canonical tumour states, concomitant with Wnt-related remodelling, FGFR1/FGFR2 upregulation, and loss of intestinal epithelial identity. Together, these findings define a tumour-intrinsic ciliogenic cell state as a feature of CRC progression, revealing a patient-stratified repurposing opportunity for targeted therapy beyond the current CRC treatment paradigms.

title: Chromosome 7 gain establishes a just-right WNT signaling state during colorectal tumorigenesis
authors: Zaalberg, I. C.; Cane Gasull, P.; Vromans, M.; Brunet Guasch, M.; Marcekova, N.; Vinken, A.; Middelkamp, S.; Wardenaar, R.; Koot, D.; Carvalho, B.; Snippert, H.; Nicholson, M. D.; Foijer, F.; Schubert, M.; Lens, S. M. A.
abstract: Aneuploidy is a hallmark of colorectal cancer, yet the functional consequences of recurrent chromosome gains and losses remain largely unknown. Leveraging advances in human colon organoid culture and chromosome copy number engineering, we here identify the gain of chromosome 7 as an adaptive event following APC loss-of-function mutation. Trisomy 7 confers a cell-intrinsic fitness advantage to APC-mutant colon organoids, while selective removal of the additional chromosome 7 copy from patient-derived colon cancer organoids severely impairs colorectal cancer organoid growth. By comparing transcriptomes of isogenic disomy 7 and trisomy 7 organoid lines, we found that chromosome 7 gain promotes organoid fitness through attenuation of excessive WNT-driven stemness caused by bi-allelic APC mutation. The gain of chromosome 7 thus establishes a just-right WNT signaling state. This effect of chromosome 7 gain is conserved from early adenoma-like APC-mutant organoids to advanced colorectal cancer organoids carrying additional oncogenic driver mutations. Moreover, consistent with our organoid data, gain of chromosome 7 is particularly common in tumors of colorectal cancer patients whose APC genotypes confer relatively high WNT activity. Overall, this work demonstrates that chromosome-specific aneuploidy can act as an adaptive mechanism to optimize, rather than maximize, oncogenic signaling during tumor evolution.
cn_title: 7号染色体获得在结直肠癌发生中建立“恰到好处”的WNT信号状态
insight: 该研究揭示7号染色体获得是APC突变后优化WNT信号的适应性事件，提示非整倍体可作为肠癌演进中的信号微调机制，为肝转移等晚期阶段的染色体演化研究提供新视角。
grade_rationale: 预印本未经同行评审，不参与分级

title: Cellular proximity and conditional coordination in the colorectal and pancreatic tumor microenvironment: a patient-level analysis of multiplexed imaging
authors: Bhadury, S.; Frankel, T. L.; Rao, A.
abstract: Immune cells in the tumor microenvironment are organized, and in colorectal and pancreatic cancer their arrangement around the tumor epithelium carries prognostic information. Multiplexed tissue imaging records the position and phenotype of every cell in a section, and studies of such images now routinely report that two cell types are spatially associated. However, the summaries behind these reports answer different questions. A proximity statistic asks whether two cell types lie close together more often than expected by chance. A conditional network asks whether their local densities rise and fall together once the other cell types are held fixed. The two can disagree, because every cell type is abundant where tissue is cell-dense and because the images of one patient are repeated measurements of that patient. We asked how epithelial and immune cells are organized in two settings: colorectal cancer with a Crohn's-like reaction (CLR) or diffuse inflammatory infiltration (DII), in 140 CODEX images from 35 patients, and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) against its precursor, intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN), in 207 multiplex immunofluorescence images from 141 patients. We developed a patient-level analysis that keeps proximity, recurrent local composition and conditional coordination as separate quantities, tests conditional organization as a function of local epithelial density within each section, checks before every conditional estimate that the two cell types are disjoint sets of cells observed together in enough images, and calibrates each conclusion by patient-label permutation, cellularity adjustment under two definitions, spatial-scale perturbation and fully nested leave-one-patient-out prediction. In colorectal cancer, the conditional association between epithelial and myeloid density turned negative with local epithelial density about four times faster in DII than in CLR (difference $-0.0553$ per quartile; 95% CI, $-0.0833$ to $-0.0273$; patient-label familywise $P=0.006$), with no accompanying difference in proximity. In the pancreas, cytotoxic and helper T cells were closer together in PDAC than in IPMN at every scale examined ($q\leq0.023$), whereas their conditional association differed between the two diseases under only one of the two cellularity definitions. Recurrent neighborhoods carried the most patient-level information in colorectal cancer (AUC 0.794) and combined spatial features in the pancreas (AUC 0.771). Pancreatic epithelial--immune and regulatory T-cell quantities could not be estimated from these cores and are reported as such. The analysis is implemented in the R package spatialMIFtools, available at https://github.com/sagnikbhadury/spatialMIFtools.
cn_title: 结直肠与胰腺肿瘤微环境中细胞邻近与条件协调的患者水平多重成像分析

title: Workflow and instrumentation for multiscale correlative imaging in voluminous cryogenic specimens
authors: D'Imprima, E.; Zagoriy, E.; Mimietz-Oekler, S.; Kirmse, R.; Hallady, A.; Mbonu, P. N.; Ronchi, P.; Jechlinger, M.; Mahamid, J.
abstract: Cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) enables molecular-resolution imaging of intracellular environments, but is constrained by the need to generate electron-transparent sections of the biological specimen and thus a limited imaging volume. To alleviate such limitations, we present a multiscale correlative workflow that links cryo-confocal fluorescence microscopy (cryo-FLM), cryo-focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (cryo-FIB-SEM) volume imaging (cryo-vEM), and cryo-FIB serial lamellae lift-out for cryo-ET in high-pressure frozen voluminous specimens. An integral part of this workflow is a sample holder that preserves specimen orientation across instruments, reduces manual handling, and overcomes stage-tilt limitations in cryo-FIB-SEM hardware. Applied to vitrified colorectal cancer organoids, we demonstrate that this workflow enables fluorescence-guided site preparation for cryo-vEM, which provides biological context beyond the limited field of view of cryo-ET, and targeted lift-out for fabrication of multiple lamellae from defined regions of interest. The reconstructed tomograms reveal subcellular architecture and cell-cell interfaces. This workflow establishes a modular methodological framework for continuum-resolution cryogenic imaging of complex 3D biological specimens.

title: The pan-cancer whole-genome landscape of Adolescent and Young Adult solid cancers
authors: van Putten, J.; Rosendahl Huber, A.; Koster, R.; Roerink, S.; de Ligt, J.; Roepman, P.; Kas, S.; van Boxtel, R.; van der Graaf, W.; Cuppen, E.; Nienhuis, H.; The GENAYA consortium,
abstract: Cancer incidence in adolescents and young adults (AYAs; 18-39 years) is rising, but how their tumors differ genomically from those of older adults (OAs) is unclear. We analyzed paired tumor-normal whole-genomes from 698 AYAs and 5,220 OAs, with subcohorts matched by cancer group to disentangle age from tumor type. AYA tumors carried fewer somatic variants yet largely shared the same genetic drivers; many apparent age differences reflected age-dependent cancer subtypes, such as IDH-mutant glioma and HPV-positive cervical cancer. Colibactin, APOBEC and homologous recombination deficiency-associated signatures were more prevalent in AYA colorectal, gynecological and breast cancers, respectively, but were not more mutagenic when present, suggesting earlier-life activity rather than AYA-specific mutagenesis. Tumor type-concordant pathogenic germline variants were enriched in AYAs (10.9% overall versus 6.6% in matched OAs; p=0.006), often with a somatic second hit. Age thus shaped AYA cancer genomes through mutational processes, subtype composition and germline predisposition, supporting comprehensive tumor-normal profiling beyond driver-focused testing.

title: Lipid nanoparticle-mediated RNAi targeting of KRAS mutants sensitises colorectal cancer cells to chemotherapy
authors: Wang, Y.; Su, S.; Zahra, K.; Sang, R.; Molloy, M. P.; Hutvagner, G.; Deng, W.
abstract: KRAS mutations, including G12D, G12V and G13D, are major oncogenic drivers in colorectal cancer (CRC) and are associated with therapeutic resistance. However, approved KRAS inhibitors remain focused on G12C subtype, leaving these prevalent variants without approved targeted therapies. Here, we developed a lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based RNA interference (RNAi) strategy to target these three KRAS variants using a single small interfering RNA (siRNA) sequence. The developed siRNA-LNPs reduced KRAS mRNA and protein expression in HCT116 (G13D), SW620 (G12V) and LS180 (G12D) cells, but not in KRAS wild-type HT29 cells, suppressing the cellular proliferation, clonogenic survival and migration. Transcriptomic profiling revealed changes in KRAS associated signalling, including suppression of cell-cycle and DNA repair programmes, providing a rationale for combining siRNA silencing with the fluoropyrimidine chemotherapeutic agent 5-fluorouracil (5-FU). The combination produced synergistic effects across all three KRAS-mutant CRC cell models and enhanced the apoptosis in both monolayer cultures and 3D spheroids. Collectively, these findings provide proof of concept for this combination strategy and support its further investigation as a potential therapeutic approach for KRAS-mutant CRC.
cn_title: 脂质纳米颗粒介导的RNAi靶向KRAS突变体使结直肠癌细胞对化疗敏感

title: Cross-Platform Evaluation of a Tumor-Budding-Associated Gene Signature in Colorectal Cancer.
authors: Sarkar, P.; Sarkar, P.
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics has identified AIF1, LIF, MRC1, and TNC as enriched in tumor budding (TB) regions of colorectal cancer. We investigated whether this TB associated gene module could be detected in bulk transcriptomic data. Pairwise gene co-occurrence was analyzed in bulk RNA-seq (TCGA-COADREAD, n=547) and single-cell RNA-seq (GSE178341, n=26,057 cells) using Fisher's exact tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. In bulk RNA-seq, pairwise fold-enrichments were weak (1.16 to 2.72), with AIF1 to LIF showing no significant association (FE=1.16, FDR=0.31). In single-cell data, the same pairs showed 31 to 184.5 fold enrichment (all FDR < 8e-38). Total UMI counts provided no evidence of doublet artifacts explaining these co-detection patterns. Exploratory enhancer-promoter interaction analysis in HCT116 cells further suggested these genes are controlled differently. GOT1 and MDH1, two malate-aspartate shuttle genes, showed lower expression in late-stage CRC (FDR less than or equal to 0.010). A bulk-derived risk score showed a modest association (Cox HR=1.21, p=0.021). Overall, TB-associated co-expression was more clearly detected at single-cell than bulk resolution, highlighting the importance of transcriptomic resolution when studying tumor-microenvironment-associated gene signatures.
cn_title: 肿瘤出芽相关基因标签在结直肠癌中的跨平台评估

title: MassBank Human: The annotated human metabolome
authors: Matsuda, F.; Hayasaka, R.; Torigoe, T.; Takahashi, M.; Takahashi, Y.; Yoshizawa, A. C.; Tsugawa, H.; Okuda, S.; Neumann, S.; Schymanski, E. L.; Izumi, Y.; Hirayama, A.
abstract: Mass spectrometry-based metabolomics is essential for deciphering human metabolic functions and metabolite dark matter. However, the dark matter of the human metabolome is intricately hidden. Therefore, we developed MassBank Human, a curated library that distills 36,512,540 MS2 spectra from 76 public human datasets into 203,886 high-quality spectra via spectral averaging, recalibration, and filtering to achieve high mass accuracy. We further used three metabolite annotation tools and developed a Zipf-Bayesian rank aggregation framework to aggregate their rankings with false discovery rate control. This framework assigned molecular formulas, chemical classes, and planar structures to 55,564, 22,619, and 14,198 spectra, respectively. Approximately half of the annotated structures potentially originated from food, pollutants, or gut microbiota. In a metabolome analysis of colorectal cancer cells, MassBank Human doubled structural annotation coverage (10.6% to 21.2%), identifying acetylated polyamines as markers of metabolic rewiring. This community resource provides an annotated foundation for exploring human metabolomes.

title: Pan-cancer nucleosome landscapes reveal tumor heterogeneity and inform cell-free DNA-based detection
authors: Yang, S.; Ye, J.; Yuan, J.; Huang, X.; Yin, Y.; Liu, Z.; Li, W.; Li, Y.
abstract: Background: Nucleosome positioning and occupancy are fundamental features of chromatin organization, yet their variation across human cancers and potential utility for noninvasive cancer detection remain poorly characterized. Methods: We systematically characterized nucleosome organization across 410 primary tumors spanning 23 cancer types using ATAC-seq, establishing a high-confidence pan-cancer nucleosome atlas validated by independent MNase-seq data. We characterized shared and cancer-type-enriched nucleosome patterns, investigated their associations with tumor heterogeneity and regulatory alterations, and evaluated tissue-derived nucleosome signatures for cancer classification and detection using circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). Results: The atlas identified shared and cancer-type-enriched nucleosomes associated with distinct regulatory programs. Notably, nucleosome occupancy provided information complementary to chromatin accessibility for tumor stratification and revealed molecular heterogeneity within individual cancers, including subgroups associated with Basal-like breast cancer. In hepatocellular carcinoma, differential nucleosome analysis revealed cancer-associated chromatin remodeling involving regulatory pathways, transcription factor motifs, and candidate genes. Importantly, tissue-derived nucleosome signatures were detectable in cfDNA, enabling classification among three cancer types (AUROC = 0.877) and colorectal cancer detection (AUROC = 0.930), with an AUROC of 0.773 in an independent validation cohort. We also developed OncoNucAtlas, a publicly accessible database facilitating exploration of these nucleosome landscapes. Conclusions: Our study cancer-associated nucleosome organization as a complementary source of epigenomic information and demonstrates the potential of tissue-derived nucleosome signatures for cfDNA-based cancer detection. The pan-cancer atlas provides a resource for investigating tumor heterogeneity and developing noninvasive cancer detection approaches.

title: Hierarchical distribution matching enables comprehensive characterization of common and condition-specific cell niches in spatial omics data
authors: Liu, Y.; Xiao, J.; Ma, X.; Wan, X.; Jiang, P.; Wang, Z.; Chen, Y.; Yang, C.
abstract: Deciphering cell niches in complex tissues is essential for understanding tissue structure and disease. Recent advances in spatial omics have enabled subcellular resolution and accurate cell identity mapping. However, robust delineation of cell niches and disease-associated spatial patterns remains difficult. We introduce Harmonics, a novel computational framework that systematically identifies both common and condition-specific cell niches from spatial omics data through hierarchical distribution matching. Harmonics also includes a suite of downstream modules that facilitate comprehensive niche characterization. We demonstrate its scalability, accuracy and generalizability across datasets spanning diverse species, tissues, diseases, spatial modalities, and technological platforms. For condition-agnostic datasets, Harmonics outperforms baseline methods in both accuracy and robustness, and further demonstrates the capability to resolve niche structures at finer granularity. Across diverse diseases including pulmonary fibrosis, triple-negative breast cancer, and colorectal cancer, Harmonics enables precise identification of condition-specific niches and reveals disease-associated dynamics, subtype-specific spatial patterns, and structured immune architectures. We envision Harmonics as a practical and versatile tool for spatial niche analysis that can be applied across a wide range of biological contexts and seamlessly integrated with existing spatial omics workflows.

title: Antibody-drug conjugate combination therapy targeting LGR5 and MET with different payloads enhances efficacy in preclinical colorectal cancer models
authors: Subramanian, S.; High, P. C.; Guernsey-Biddle, C.; Cappellino, M. G.; Sullivan, S. P.; Liang, Z.; Aldana, A. M.; Li, L.; Pan, S.; Carmon, K. S.
abstract: Leucine-rich repeat-containing G protein-coupled receptor 5 (LGR5) is a marker of cancer stem-like cells frequently upregulated in colorectal cancer (CRC) with lower expression in normal tissues, making it a favorable target for antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs). ADCs combine antibody specificity with potent cytotoxic payloads to enhance efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity. LGR5-targeting ADCs incorporating different payloads demonstrate strong initial tumor inhibition, yet tumors eventually recur due in part to LGR5 downregulation, necessitating more effective strategies to prevent relapse. We show treatment with chemotherapies or an LGR5-targeting ADC coupled to a topoisomerase 1 inhibitor payload (8E11-CPT2) reduces LGR5 levels and increases MET receptor expression and/or activation in CRC cells, supporting a therapeutic approach to target LGR5 and MET simultaneously. Accordingly, we engineered a MET-targeting ADC (ABT-700-SG3199) via site-specific conjugation of the anti-MET antibody telisotuzumab (ABT-700) with the DNA-crosslinking pyrrolobenzodiazepine (PBD) dimer SG3199. ABT-700-SG3199 exhibited superior potency and efficacy in CRC models compared to the clinical-stage MET-targeting ADCs ABBV-399 and ABBV-400, which use the same antibody backbone conjugated to different payloads. Treatment with ABT-700-SG3199 increased LGR5 expression, and the combination of ABT-700-SG3199 with 8E11-CPT2 enhanced CRC cell-killing efficacy, reinforcing the rationale for a dual-targeting approach. In patient-derived xenografts, combined administration of 8E11-CPT2 and ABT-700-SG3199 markedly delayed tumor relapse and prolonged survival compared with single-agent treatment. Taken together, these findings reveal a reciprocal regulation between MET and LGR5 in response to LGR5- or MET-targeting ADCs in CRC models and support a LGR5/MET dual-targeting therapeutic strategy to enhance efficacy and potentially overcome resistance and relapse.
cn_title: 靶向LGR5与MET的双抗体偶联药物联合治疗在结直肠癌临床前模型中增强疗效
